This was enhanced to 550 MPa when aged and warm worked. This could be as a result of sparse distribution of suspected precipitates of v|/ [8]. This is evident from the microstructure (Plate 8,Fig.4). It is however, important to mention that, the application is only limited to where loads of 1/3 of its Ultimate Strength can only be useful. There is a wide gap in the mechanical properties when the alloy was cooled rapidly rather than at ambient condition. During rapid cooling the alloy was waterquenched to allow the formation of a 6 precipitates with a coherent lattice structure. The un

broken continuity led to coherency (Plate 7, Fig.7). Since, the rate of diffusion is slow, a separate Я structure could not form rather, an intermediate Я and a matrix led to a distortion in the _\\i_ -lattice in the neighbourhood of these nuclei. This distortion hindered the movement of dislocations and so the strength and hardness increased. This accounted for the UTS of 420.7MPa compared to as-cast sample which recorded half to one-third of the strength. 

However, at ageing condition, Cu atoms segregate by diffusion to form Copper rich zones called Guinner -Preston (GP Zone 1). This increased with further growth at 165°C to produce a GP zone 2 where a n precipitate phase was formed. This produced a stronger effect as the precipitates generate stresses that helped in preventing dislocation movement. 

This accounted for the variation between the Al-2.03 Cu (as-cast) when tested on the UTM and when heated to 165°C as a result of rapid diffusion at a higher temperature. As cast recorded 98.5 MPa with no precipitate formation, while at 165°C in 6 hours ageing the Alloy recorded 550MPa at 20 percent deformation (Plate8,Fig.4). This inferred that ageing and percent deformation (mechanical) have the tendency of increasing the strength of Al-2.03Cu alloy. 

###### Conclusion and Recommendation 

A combination of load (mechanical) and heat treatment introduce a tremendous improvement to the strength of Al-2.03 Cu alloy required for piston in automobile. This was a result of finer precipitates of CuAb and v|/ obtained. It could be discovered that the properties required for a high performance Al-2.03 Cu could only be determined by the treatments at higher temperature, deformation, and time. The varying percentage of deformation at varying temperature conditions as 300°C to 400°C also played a major role in ascertaining the extent to which the material can be loaded with increasing temperatures. This was further substantiated by the MATLAB technique.

###### **Abstract** 

We proposed thermit reduction-electroslag remelting method of preparing the large scale CuCr alloy. But there are pores and oxide inclusions in CuCr alloy prepared by thermit reduction process. This paper studied mainly the effects of ratio of reactant and additive on the inclusion type and their occurrences in CuCr alloy. The alloy prepared in different process conditions was characterized via XRD, SEM, OM and TEM and metallographic microscope, in which the existing state and micro-structural defects of inclusions are analyzed. The results show that there are three distinct regions: copper-rich regions, chromium-rich regions and the inclusion regions. Inclusions are mainly in the form of stomata and AI2O3 phase, mainly locating in the copper-rich phase and the interface area of chromium-rich phase and the copper-rich phase. Adding Na3AlF6 and heating agent can effectively reduce the inclusion content in the alloy. 

###### **1 Introduction** 

In recent years, with the development of high power vacuum and high-pressure technology ,the CuCr alloy contact material which has many advantages gradually replaced the traditional W-Cu and Cu-Bi series alloy contact material, and become the first choice of material in high-voltage and high-power vacuum switch contacts'<sup>1</sup> "<sup>31</sup> . The traditional powder metallurgy method, infiltration method and vacuum arc melting method'<sup>4</sup> "<sup>81</sup> are using metal Cu powder and Cr powder as raw material by casting molding, and have disadvantages such as high production costs, complicated process, poor product density and low yield, especially in the large size alloy ingots'<sup>9</sup> "<sup>121</sup> . At present, the world regards CuCr alloy new preparation technologies as the first place, and how to achieve a l

arge size the CuCr alloy ingot preparation has become a hot research of CuCr alloy'31 . Zhang Ting-an and Dou Zhihe'1 "31 who are supported by national natural science fondation of china successfully successful developed new technologies and core equipment to prepare large-size copper-chromium alloy through aluminum thermal reduction-secondary refining method, and obtained two national invention patents. The method includes two key steps: one is get CuCr alloy 247 consumable ingot by Thermit-SHS with electromagnetic stirring, the other is to refine the CuCr alloy ingot to remove the pores, inclusions and other defects by electroslag remelting technology to get dense and uniform CuCr contact material. The preliminary study results show that: means of electromagnetic stirring evidently inhibit effect of alloy ingot macrosegregation during the electromagnetic casting stage, but there are still microstructure defects such as alumina inclusions and pores in the alloy ingots. Therefore, Zhang Ting-an et al refer new ideas of using the electroslag remelting to refine CuCr alloy ingots and effectively remove the defects of the ingots such as pores and inclusionsPI . At present, there is no report of study on the electroslag remelting refining processes of CuCr alloy (the refining slag, remelting current). This article will research mode of occurrence and distribution law of inclusions in the large-size CuCr alloy ingots by Al Thermit-SHS under magnetic field stirring action and provide a theoretical basis for chosing refining slag to remove inclusions by electroslag refining. Meanwhile the article analyses the effect of reduction conditions of Thermit-SHS on the types of inclusions, mode of occurrence and distribution of regular inclusions in alloy ingot, and refer theory for inclusions regulation in the large-size alloy ingots. ###### **2 Experiments** 2.1 Experiment procedure Ratios of reactants are as follows: the amount of CuO in actual ingredients are more excess of 5% than the theoretical amount, Al powder are more excess of 10% than the theoretical amount, additive CaF2 or Na3AlF6 ingredient quantity is accounted for 5% or 10% of the total mass of the reactants, and heating agent KCIO3 ingredient quantity is accounted for 5% of the total mass of the reactants. ###### **Abstract** 

In this paper, vacuum distillation technology has been employed to study the possibility and regularity of separating copper and enriching lead, silver and other valuable metals from copperbased multi

component alloys. The result of experiment indicated the practicability of vacuum distillation dealing with copper base complex multi-component alloy to separating lead and silver, when the vacuum distillation temperature was 1637K, distillation time was 60min; residual gas pressure was 20-30Pa, the removal rate of silver was 95.86%, of lead was 99.63%; the evaporation rate of copper was 0.745%. The removal rate of arsenic, antimony and tin respectively were 83.09%, 48.12% and 24.54%. Vacuum distillation method is applicable for dealing with the copper-based multi component alloys, silver and lead can realize effective recovery. 

###### **Introduction** 

Copper generally go with lead mineral, therefore, to remove copper from lead becomes an inevitable link in lead smelting. Dross from removed copper usually contains lead, arsenic, antimony, tin and noble metal silver. In abroad, soda ash-iron dust is adopted to process copper dross of this kind. The outcomes of this process are lead matte, wet lead, scoria smoke dust etc'<sup>1</sup> "<sup>5</sup> '. The dominant components of all the outcomes are copper and lead. Moreover, in the process of tin smelting, copper contained by-products are produced, such as, crude tin alloy, tin lead electrolytic anode slime and so on. Copper content of all the products are ranging from few percentages to several tens percentage. Those products, no matter merge into main producing process, or separate treatment cost losses of valuable metal. For one hand, the containing of copper of outcomes from pyrogenic attack is less than 50%, for the other hand, a lot of valuable metal need to be processed, which increase the cost of retrieve. 

Comparing with traditional metallurgical method, vacuum metallurgy is with outstanding characteristics of producing three wastes, no use of reagent and simple technological process. And it is wildly used in the fields as metal thermal reduction, alloy separation, recycling of secondary resource, waste pyrolysis and so on'<sup>6</sup> "<sup>1</sup> .Today, the first nature resource gradually goes short, it holds great potential benefit both in economy and society to study on the program.

Therefore, in this thesis, based on adopting vacuum distillation technology to study various elements, humbly providing theoretic and practical basis for industrial production.

Hence one can see that distillation temperature possess enormous implication in silver volatilization. When the temperature is 1773K and distillation time is 60min, the removal rate of silver is 99.63%. Thus it can be seen in Table8, in the same distillation temperature (1673K), distillation time extends 8 times, the removal rate of silver increases 1.18 times, which indicates that compare with distillation temperature, distillation time has less influence on silver volatilization. When 261 the distillation temperature is 1637K, distillation time is 240min, the removal rate of silver is 99.93%, and silver content in residue is 0.0005%, which illustrates that silver can be totally removed from copper in vacuum distillation. The Influence of Distillation Temperature and Time on Tin Volatilization. It is shown in Table VII and Table VIII that when the distillation temperature is 1773K, distillation time is 60min; the removal rate of tin is 34.16%. When the distillation temperature is 1673K and distillation time is 240min, the removal rate of tin is 35.77%, which indicates that at the same distillation time and temperature, purely extend distillation time and raise temperature have little influence on tin volatilization. The Influence of Distillation Temperature and Time on Antimony and Arsenic Volatilization.We can see in Table VII that in the same distillation time (60 min), as soon as distillation temperature raise 300K, the removal rate of As and antimony increase 1.36 times and 2.42 times respectively. Distillation temperature has little effect on volatilization of arsenic and antimony. When the temperature is 1773K, and distillation time is 60min, the removal rate of arsenic and antimony are 88.58% and 88.87%. It can be concluded that based on table8 that, in the same distillation temperature (1573K), if the distillation time extended by 8 times, the removal rate of arsenic increase 1.11 times, and 1.70 times for antimony which influenced a lot by distillation time. When distillation temperature is 1573K, distillation time is 240min, the removal rate of arsenic and antimon

y are 92.02% and 83.50%. 

The Influence of Distillation Temperatures and Time on Copper Volatilization It can be shown in Figure 3 and Figure 4 that raising the distillation temperature and lengthen the distillation time increase removal rate of copper. When distillation temperature is 1673K, distillation time is 240min; the removal rate of copper is 12.206%. While when the distillation temperature is 1773K, and the distillation time is 60min, the removal rate of copper is 5.48%. Copper will be easily volatilized in high distillation temperature and long distillation time. 

We can naturally draw conclusions as follow: ©vacuum distillation is an effective way to separate lead and silver from copper base alloy. In the condition that the temperature is above 1437K, distillation time is more than 30min, and the gas residual pressure is 20~30Pa, the removal rate of lead is greater than 99%. The removal rate of silver is influenced by the distillation temperature and time. When distillation temperature is above 1637K, distillation time is more than 60min, and the gas residual pressure is 20~30Pa, the removal rate of silver is greater than 95%, the amount of residue is less than 200ppm. With the raising of distillation temperature and lengthen of the distillation time, the removal rate of silver can be more than 99%. © the remove of arsenic, antimony and tin can not be fulfilled by vacuum distillation. Theatrically, if saturated vapor pressure of arsenic and antimony are greater than that of lead and silver, they can be moved. When distillation temperature is 1673K, distillation time is more than 60min, lead and silver can be moved completed yet for arsenic and antimony, there still 20%~50% residue left. The reason for these phenomena is because that arsenic and antimony combines with copper as what is shown in Figure 5. These new compounds still active after melting. In vacuum, saturated vapor pressure of Sn is low, which is similar with copper, so it can be combined with copper. When distillation temperature is 1673K, distillation time is 240min; the removal rate of tin is 35.77%. Tin is being enriched in the residue. © To ensure safely copper does not volatilize and enriched in residue, the temperature should be under 1673K, and meanwhile, distillation time should be less in 60min.

###### **Conclusion** 

(1) The practicability of vacuum distillation dealing with copper base complex multi-component alloy to separating lead and silver. When the temperature is 1673K, distillation time is 60min, system residual gas pressure is 20-30pa, the removal rate of lead is 99.63%, of silver is 95.86% and of copper is 0.745%. lead and silver are separated from copper, left copper enriched. 

(2) In the process of vacuum distillation dealing with copper base complex multi-component alloy, arsenic and antimony combines with copper forming a new compound, which brings about impossibility of separation. Distillation temperature and time have great influence

on antimony, but have little influence on arsenic. 

(3) In the process of vacuum distillation, separation of Sn and Cu can not be fulfilled. When distillation temperature is 1673K, distillation time is 60min, and system residual gas pressure is 20-30pa, the removal rate of Sn is 35.77%. Sn is enriched in residue. 

(4) With the raising of distillation temperature and lengthen of distillation time, evaporation rate of copper increases. When distillation temperature is 1674K, distillation time is 60min, and system residual gas pressure is 20-30pa, the removal rate of copper is 0.745%. Thus, when distillation temperature is 1673K, distillation time is 240min, and system residual gas pressure is 20-30pa, the removal rate of copper can be 12.026%. 

(5) Vacuum distillation has great industrial application value in processing copper base complex multi-component alloy, especially in dealing with lead and silver. Vacuum distillation can promote further study on performance of furnace of this field.

###### **Abstract** 

This paper has outlined forms of Au & Ag losses in copper smelting process and methods for increasing Au & Ag recovery, analyzed factors influencing Au & Ag recovery in copper converting process, presented Au & Ag behavior in copper electrorefining process, and reviewed effect of current density/electrolyte circulation rate during electrolysis and surface finish of cathode on Au & Ag losses. Measures and research direction for decreasing Au & Ag losses in electrolysis have also been introduced. Based on Au & Ag behavior in copper electrorefining process and previous studies by others, new approach for increasing Au & Ag recovery in copper smelter has been discussed. And brief comparison has made between continued multiplication method and equilibrium method application in the case of calculation of Au & Ag recovery in copper smelter. 

###### **Introduction** 

As gold and silver are the major by-products from copper smelting process, efficient Au & Ag recovery has become one of the key approaches for copper producers to increase economic efficiency. With similar physicochemical properties, Cu, Au and Ag belong to the first subgroup of elements in the same periodic table. Au and Ag will be enriched into Cu phase firstly when both matte-slag phase and copper-matte phase appear in copper smelting process. However, great changes have taken place in Au & Ag proportions into individual phase due to changes of physicochemical conditions in each smelting process. ###### Au & Ag Losses in Dust 

For the purpose of understanding Au/Ag movement in copper smelting process for one Chinese smelter, Jianlin Lai' ' laid special stress on investigation of production processes for Flash

Investigation results showed that direct enrichment rates of Au in these production processes were 90.03%, 95.47% and 92.01% respectively, and that direct enrichment rates of Ag in these production processes were 82.52%, 93.5% and 94.95% respectively. In flash smelting process, carryover of Au & Ag into dust were 9.62% and 12.29% respectively. Lan Lin' ' studied movement and distribution of Au & Ag in ISP process, and noticed carryover of Ag in dust at 5.07%. 

According to the investigation made by Jianlin Lai and Lan Lin, it demonstrated that Au & Ag losses increased with the increase of dust rate of metallurgical furnaces. Even if there was possibility to install Au & Ag recovery equipment in dust treatment plant, total Au & Ag recovery still got dropped. Therefore, the efficient way for increasing Au & Ag recovery is always to decrease dust rate. Moreover, the influence of dust rate on Au & Ag recovery shall be considered when we compare advantages and disadvantages among different copper smelting technologies.

###### **Abstract** 

In this paper, results of a novel synthesis method of carbon-coated LiNiiЯMniЯCoiЯC^ cathode material for lithium-ion battery are reported. The carbon coating was produced from a precursor, glucose, by microwave-pyrolysis method. The structure, morphology and electrochemical performance of the bare and carbon-coated LiNiiЯMniЯCoiЯC^ were characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy and charge-discharge tests respectively. The L8(2 ) orthogonal experiments were carried out to optimize LiNiiЯCoiЯMniЯCyC technological conditions. The conditions of the orthogonal experiments were that the glucose content were 1.5 % and 4 %, the holding time were 15min and 30min, the heating temperature were 400 °C and 500 °C and the solvent were FLO and CH3CH2OH. The main experiment target include specific capacity at 0.1C and 0.2C^ Capacity retention rate^ medium voltage attenuation rate and The fifth discharge medium voltage. The data were analyzed by Minitab 14 statistics software. The results of analysis of variance indicated that the most influential factor was the glucose content despite of discharge rate. Secondly, the effect of the solvent was equivalent to the holding time.

###### **Experiment** 

######

Sample Preparation 

The spherical (NiiЯMniЯCoiЯXOFTh ( Lanzhou Jinchuan ) and IJ2CO3 ( China lithium, 99.9% ) powders with molar ratio 1:1.06 were ball-milled thoroughly. The excess amount of Li was used to compensate for the loss of Li during calcinations. The powder was sintered in the microwave reactor at 1243 K for 30 min after drying at 323 K. LiNiiЯMniЯCoiЯC^ powder was mixed with glucose of 3 wt% by mechanically mixing for 8 h, and then pyrolyzed in a microwave reactor (Figure 1) at 673 K for 15 min after drying. 

###### Experimental Equipment 

Experiments were carried out using a novel microwave reactor, the schematic of which is shown in Figure 1. The microwave reactor with a frequency of 2450 MHz and a maximum power output of 1500 W was fabricated by the Kunming University of Science and Technology. 

###### Characterization 

X-ray diffraction (XRD) data for the finely ground samples were collected at 298 K using a Bruker D8 X-ray diffractometer with CuKa radiation (X=1.5406 В). It was operated at 40 kV and 300 111A in the 20 range of 10° to 80° in the continuous scan mode with the step size of 0.01° and the scan rate 1.0 (°/min). The scanning electron microscope (SEM) image of the particle shapes and morphologies of the bare and carbon-coated LiNiiЯMniЯCoiЯC^ were obtained using a Philips XL-30E instrument. The electrodes were fabricated from a 85:10:5 (mass percent) mixture of active materials: acetylene black as the current conductor and polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) as the binder. The PVDF was dissolved in N-methylpyrrolidinone, before the active material and the conductor mixture were added. After homogenization, the

slurry was evacuated for 20 min to remove the residual air. The slurry was then coated on a thin aluminum foil (20-um thick) and dried overnight at 60-70 °C. The electrode was pressed with a pressure of 10 MPa and punched into 16-mm-diameter disks. The electrochemical cells were prepared as per 2016-coin-cell hardware with lithium metal foil as both the counter and reference electrodes. The cells were assembled in a vacuum glove box. ###### **Abstract** 

Metal aluminum produced by non-electrolysis process received much attention due to its lower energy consumption. In this paper, carbothermic reduction and carbothermic-chlorination of alumina in normal pressure and vacuum were studied. The products were examined by means of XRD, EDS and SEM. During the carbothermic reduction process using carbon reductant in normal pressure, no metal aluminum was found. However, when coal was used as reductant, a mixture containing metallic aluminum, AI4C3, and silicon was obtained, but metallic aluminum couldn't be separated from the mixture. During the carbothermic-chlorination process in vacuum, AI4O4C and AI4C3 were produced by the reaction between alumina and carbon, and AICI3 gas reacted with AI4O4C and AI4C3 to produce A1C1 gas. Metallic aluminum was produced due to the disproportionation of A1C1 gas and condensed on the collecting plate. Meanwhile, the initial temperature of carbothermic reduction of alumina reduced in vacuum compared with that in normal pressure. 

###### **Introduction** 

Industrial production of primary aluminum is carried out in alumina cell by the so-called HallHйroult process, necessitating the use of very high currents of low voltage. The alumina from which metallic aluminum is gained must be chemically pure, otherwise impure metal results. The main drawbacks of the electrolytic production are its very high energy consumption, the release of perfluorocarbons, and the high specific CO2 emissions [1]. During the past years, there were a lot of attempts to produce metallic aluminum by carbothermic reduction of AI2O3 [2, 3]. Cox [4] determined the vapor pressure over the AI2O3-C system and performed X-ray diffraction analysis of condensed products. It was demonstrated that an increase in the carbon content in the system leaded to the sequence of transitions: Al203^Al4C>4C^Al20C^Al4C3 ->-Al [5]. In any carbothermic reduction process for aluminum, extremely high temperatures (2000 °C ) were required [6]. In spite of considerable effort, the carbothermic reduction of alumina to aluminum remains a formidable technical challenge, due to the high temperatures required, and to the formation of aluminum carbide and oxycarbide byproducts [7]. 

Carbothermic-chlorination process [8, 9] was an effective way of extracting inorganic materials in the metallurgical industry. In this process, aluminum in the form of alumina reacted with a 

287 

chlorinating agent in the presence of carbon. The corresponding aluminum subchlorides formed and separated from alumina in gaseous form were unstable at the temperature of operation and decomposed readily to get desired metallic aluminum. Coal is the most abundant fossil i

n the world, and coal is an appropriate candidate for the reducing agent because of its low price. Furthermore, coal has some other physical and chemistry properties which distinguish it from graphite. Coal particles swelled to different extents and therefore generated solid residues with different physical structures. These pore structures governed the rate of mass transport during the carbothermic process of alumina and decreased the spraying of raw material, which increased the yield of products [10]. Bauxite is the main raw materials for alumina industry [11]. Carbothermic-chlorination of alumina process is crucial to the development of advanced technologies for bauxite especially low Al/Si minerals utilization. In this paper, aluminum chloride and coal were used as chlorinating agent and reducing agent, and carbothermic reduction of alumina in normal pressure and carbothermic-chlorination of alumina in vacuum were investigated, respectively. 

###### **Experimental** 

###### **Equipment and procedure** 

The carbothermic reduction of alumina with coal in normal pressure was conducted in an induction furnace. The furnace has a 15-KVA power capacity and used a four-turn induction coil and a graphite crucible for melting. Cooling water was circulated through the induction coil. The crucible was placed in a vertical quartz tube. The end of the quartz tube was sealed. The top cap contained threaded channel through it allowing for plastic gas line to be attached. The mixture of alumina and coal was placed in the graphite crucible. Opened cooling water and heated the mixture. In order to obtain experimental reaction temperature, potencies ranging from 5 to 7 kw were used. 

The carbothermic-chlorination of alumina in vacuum was conducted in an electric resistance furnace. This furnace composed three zones: reaction zone, AICI3 sublimation zone and metallic aluminum condensation zone. The reaction zone was provided with a central removable tube that permitted to insert a thermocouple in order to know the temperature. The AICI3 sublimation zone composed of a heating device with a digital thermometer. The metallic aluminum condensation zone consisted of a box-like collecting plate, where most of the reaction products were condensed. Once the reagent solid sample was placed in the reactor, opened cooling water and vacuum pump, and heated the reaction zone. Vacuum degree was regulated by a corresponding control and measuring devices. 

###### **Raw materials and sample preparation** 

Alumina powder was industrial grade (92.99%). Coal was from Wayuanchong mine in Yunnan province. Anhydrous AICI3 was analytic quality. The solid samples used in the experiments were mixtures of AI2O3 and coal particles, obtained with a molar ratio (1:3) and mechanical mixing time (30 min).

###### **Abstract** 

A continuously pilot synthesis by microwave-heating was used in preparing the cathode material LiNii/3Coi/3Mni/3C>2 for Li-ion battery, which used Nii/3Coi/3Mni/3(OH)2 and Li2CC>3 as raw materials. Decomposition of the raw materials and synthesis of LixNii/3Coi/3Mni/302 would be finished in single roasting process. In addition, using microwave-heating would reduce the reacting time largely. Furthermore, the yield of LixNii/3Coi/3Mni/302 synthetized in single roasting process was 50 kg. Meanwhile, the effects of Li:(N

i+Co+Mn) molar radio (Li:(Ni+Co+Mn)=1.06, 1.075, 1.09, 1.15) was studied in this paper. XRD, SEM and EIS were used in characterizing the cathode material. The results showed that the best Li:(Ni+Co+Mn) molar radio was 1.075. It was found that the LiNii/3Coi/3Mni/3C>2 synthetized with Li :(Ni+Co+Mn)= 1.075 had homogenous distribution of particles and ideal layered structure. The galvanostatic charge-discharge(0.1C, 2.75-4.3V, vs. Li /Li) tests showed that the initial discharge capacity of the LixNii/3Coi/3Mni/302 was 159.5mAhg"<sup>1</sup> , and the discharge capacity was 157.6mAhg"<sup>1</sup> after 10 cycles. 

###### **Introduction** 

Recently, as the cobalt was expensive and the restriction of dynamic power, the commercial cathode Li2Co02 which was expensive, toxic, and high pollution had exposed its defects'<sup>1</sup> "<sup>2</sup> '. Since TOhzuku'<sup>3</sup> ' first reported the layered LiNii/3Coi/3Mni/3C>2, this material had high reversible

The microwave-heating teshnology was different from the traditional heating. The microwave-heating delievered the energy to the molecule by dielectric loss of material in microwave region. By this energy transmitting way, the energy would be accumulated repidly in the microsocpic area of material. In a word, the microwave-heating twchnology had its advantages of selective heating, efficient, environmental protection and so on'<sup>1</sup> . Recently, as the advantages of microwave-heating , many researchers'<sup>11</sup> ' had applied this technology to prepare LiNii/3Coi/3Mni/3C>2, which could reduce the reacting time and cost apparently. However, the volatizing of lithium which couldn't be avoided in the traditional way would be improved obviously by using this technology. Although preparing the LiNii^Coi^Mn^C^ in microwave-heating way had a lot of advantages, the researches couldn't realize a large-scale preparation or continuously industrial manufacture. In this work, LixNii/3Coi/3Mni/302 with various Li:(Ni+Co+Mn) molar radios(Li:(Ni+Co+Mn)=1.06, 1.075, 1.09, 1.15) were prepared using a continuously pliot way by microwave-heating. The crystal structure, the microscopic morphology, and the electrochemical properties of LiJSfii^Coi^Mni^C^ were studied and reported in this paper. 

###### Experiment 

Using Nii/3Co

i/3Mni/3(OH)2 and Ь2C03 as raw materials, Nii/3Coi/3Mni/3(OH)2 was mixed with Ь2C03 using a ball mill. Four kinds of mixed materials were prepared, which had Li:(Ni+Co+Mn) ofl.06, 1.075, 1.09, 1.15. The mixed materials were fired at 750Dfor 60 min, and finally fired at 940 D for 60 min by using a microwave continuous roasting furnace which made by key laboratory of unconventional metallurgy for education ministry of Kunming university of science and technology. The furnace could divide into three parts: the preheating stage, the roasting stage, the cooling stage. The temperature of the furnace could be adjusted in three steps. Firstly, testing air temperature of the furnace. Secondly, using a temperature measuring ring to test the temperature of the material. Thirdly, adjusting the air temperature according to the temperature of the material. In the continuous preparing process, the time of material pushing was adjusted in order to control the formulated time that the material stayed in the roasting stage. By controlling the above steps, the continuous prepartion of LixNii/3Coi/3Mni/302 could be realized. In this work, few materials were used to adjust the temperature of the roasting stage(750D, 940 D). Then, the rate of material pushing was 15 minutes per plate, so that all the material could stay in the roasting stage for 60 min. The roasting of four kinds of the mixed materials could be finished in one cycle. The weight of LiJSfii^Coi^Mni^C^ was 50 Kg. 

The phase purty was measured by X-ray diffusion(XRD) measurements. XRD measurements were performed using Rigaku D/max 220 X-ray diffusionmeter with Cu target. Scanning electric

###### **Abstract** 

This research used the austempering heat treatment on the SCM435 thin specimen with a type of double loop and obtained the Cr-Mo bainite structure, and then we could further investigate the mechanical properties of SCM435 bainite structure. Experimental data showed the stability of the mechanical properties of specimen with austempering temperature 830°C for 25 minutes was better than that of 15 minutes. The size of austenite grain affected the strength of thin specimen. After austempering at 830°C-25minutes and salt bath at 290°C, the stability of UTS was better than that of salt bath at 310°C and 330°C- The average hardness of all specimens was about more than HRA70. The specimen with austempering at 830°C-25minutes and salt bath at 290°C-30minutes had bigger grain size of austenite and retained y, it also had higher hardness and strength toughness. So, its stability was improved for tensile strength comparing with traditional tempered martensite process. 

###### **Introduction** 

SCM435 is a Cr-Mo steel with high strength and high hardness properties, and it has been widely used in machine parts, shafts, gears and strength screw products [1-3]. However, this system often has lower reliability due to the brittleness of high-temperature tempering and quenching inequality. Considering the austempering heat treatment can obtain the uniform bainite structure to improve the temper brittleness, and the austempering heat treatment is a continuous process that it also has efficiency and uniformity. For the thin plate specimens, the mechanical properties of the bainite structure are better than traditional martempering structures. 

In this study, the SCM435 sheet was made into double loop-type thin plate specimens by punch-shear to highlight the stress concentration to study the effect of the brittleness [3-4]. Considering the bainite structure has excellent mechanical properties [3, 5-6], and i

t can reduce the brittleness effect of the thin plate specimen (improve the strength and ductility) by controlling the different phase of base composition (the retained austenite content). According to the reference [7], the characteristics of austempering SCM435 still not have been studied and the salt meet the environmental demands. Therefore, this research used the heat treatment conditions to control the different bainite structures of SCM435 alloy, and then investigated the tensile strength and hardness to obtain the application data of SCM435 alloy. 299 **Experimental Procedure Introduction** The chemical composition of the SCM435 is given in Table 1, the carbon content is 0.37 wt.% and contains the other alloying elements such as Si, Cr, Mn. ###### Cost Benefits of EAF Bottom Purging Systems Due to Metallurgical Improvements 

###### Marcus Kirschen , Ashraf Hanna , Karl-Michael Zettl 

1 RHI AG, Wienerbergstrasse 9, A-l 100 Vienna, Austria 2 RHI Canada, 4205 Fairview St, Burlington L7L 2A5, Canada 

###### Keywords: EAF, Bottom purging, benefits, metallurgy 

###### **Abstract** 

Bottom purging systems are well established practice in refining metallurgy and an increasin

gly important technology for the EAF process in steel industry. Direct bottom purging provides efficient mixing of the entire melt volume, increases turbulence intensity in the melt, and improves mass exchange of alloy additions or oxygen. Continuously rising columns of dispersed gas bubbles helps to increase removal of volatile components carbon monoxide and hydrogen avoiding boiling retardation. Direct purging (DPP) systems provide cost benefits especially for EAF processes where metallurgical constraints have to be considered, e.g. for alloyed and stainless steel production, foundries. Case studies are presented. 

###### **Introduction** 

###### **Current EAF Technology and Production Constraints in Steel Industry** 

Approximately 30 % of steel, 446 Mio. tonnes in 2011, was melted in the electric arc furnace (EAF) with increasing tendency due to its large flexibility in production volume and raw materials. With recent increase of prices for ferrous raw materials the requirements for production of high quality steels from low quality scrap, direct reduced iron (DRI) and blends of ferrous raw material in various qualities increased. Maximum yield of ferrous raw material, oxygen, carbon, and alloys and minimum energy costs are of high importance. At modern high productivity levels even small process improvements provide considerable cost savings. Such improvements are caused, e.g., by efficiency increase of mass and energy transfer in the EAF. Optimization of flow pattern in the steel bath is therefore important for efficient melting of scrap and DRI and high homogeneity of the melt [1-4]. 

###### **Technology of EAF Bottom Purging** 

Since the early 1980s, various injection systems for oxygen or inert gases have been introduced to the EAF to improve melting efficiency. Usual EAF technology provides few sources of momentum to move and mix the steel melt and slag: AC electric arcs and oxygen injectors affect the surface of the steel volume with restricted efficiency as the viscous slag layer covers the steel melt. DC electric field applies to the central steel volume above the bottom electrodes to some extent. By far the highest efficiency in movement of the entire steel melt provides purging by rising gas bubble columns from the bottom to the top of the steel volume (Figure 2). 

Bottom purging systems based on gas injection by a single tube or by multi-hole plugs have been developed, buried in the EAF hearth ramming mix (indirect purging) or in contact with the steel melt (direct purging). Today, direct purging systems with multi-hole design represent the majority of bottom purging systems in EAFs in steel industry world-wide, e.g. the RHI DPP 

309 

purging brick series (Direct Purging Plug). Approximately 9 % of the EAFs are equipped with bottom purging systems today. RHI delivers bottom purging plugs to more than 80 customers world-wide, to EAFs with tap weights from 6 t to 250 t. Tendency for bottom purging is increasing (Figure 3) wit

Increasing number of customers for direct EAF bottom purging bricks (based on RHI deliveries) Safety Gas purging bricks are installed in a channel of surrounding bricks in the EAF hearth (Figure 4) thus (1) facilitating the exchange of the purging brick in the EAF hearth and (2) increasing safety standards as the hearth ramming mix is installed, de-aired, compacted, and sintered without interference of the purging system. The remaining gap at the purging brick is filled with 2 special filling mixes adapted to the special sintering behavior near the slightly cooling DPP brick (Figure 4). By this standardized lining strategy highest safety requirements are fulfilled and breakthrough incidents are a thing of the past. The DPP purging brick consists of fused magnesia of highest quality and high quality graphite, porosity is as low as in other high quality MgO-C bricks used in the EAF walls, 2.9 density is in the very same range. Gas is supplied to the steel bath by max. 19 steel tubes with 1 mm diameter (Figure 5). By providing multiple small holes the infiltration of the brick by metal or slag at low gas flow rate is restricted to the most upper part. Reopening of blocked tubes by melt movement caused by the 310 neighboring tubes is then facilitated and reported as common during DPP purging operation. Single-hole purging bricks remain blocked after deep infiltration of the one tube. A wear indicator in the purging brick is based on a pressurized gas line. A pressure drop of the opened wear line indicates a remaining minimum brick length of approx. 350 mm and the purging brick is closed by interruption of the gas supply. Surrounding DPP Purging

DPP purging brick for EAF bottom stirring Gas **Injection** Typical DPP gas flow rates applied are in the range from 10-100 1/min or higher if required. Nitrogen gas is applied in most cases, sometimes Argon. The initial momentum of the gas jet is dissipated in the steel melt few centimeters above the hot face of the plug and the gas volume is distributed to a large number of well distributed gas bubbles rising to the steel surface. Consequently, the impact of the gas flow to the melt movement depends only on the gas volume applied, less on tube number, tube diameter

or arrangement of tubes. A large number of small tubes decreases risk of blocking and provides a high number of gas bubbles even at very low gas 

311 

flow rates. Low gas flow rate does not only provide maximum gas efficiency but avoids the formation of an open eye of the steel surface. The corresponding "soft bubbling" mode is the common mode of operation in most DPP applications. However, some customers apply higher gas flow rates to reach their targets under special EAF operation conditions. 

A typical gas control station for supply of 3 DPP purging bricks is shown in Figure 6. Each brick is controlled separately. Gas flow rates can be controlled independently from the EAF control, by using particular EAF operation signals, or by entire incorporation to the level 2 control system.

In small EAFs at foundries however, very low gas flow rates are applied to avoid an open eye of the steel melt due to lower slag thickness. Very low gas flow rates require small diameters of gas supplying tubes in order to decrease risk of infiltration at low gas pressure. Requirements on precise gas control also increases with decreasing gas flow rates to avoid splashing at overdriven high gas flow rate and to avoid infiltration and blocking at too low gas flow rates. DPP purging bricks with variable number of gas tubes performed very well at small EAFs and very low gas flow rates. 

###### **Process Related Benefits** 

EAF process benefits of direct purging systems are related to increased movement of the steel bath and increased mixing of the lower with the higher steel melt volumes. Reported benefits of DPP bottom purging system are: 

- Increased thermal and temperature homogeneity of steel melt: 

   - _■S_ Decreased melting time of scrap and DRI 

   - _■S_ Increased heat transfer in super-heating period 

   - _■S_ Increased power input 

   - _■S_ Decreased specific electrical energy demand 

   - _■S_ Decr

eased deviation of measured steel temperature at EAF and at ladle furnace _■S_ Avoidance of skull formation or remains at EAF hearth at tap ("clean furnace") 

- Increased chemical homogeneity of steel melt: 

   - _■S_ Increased metal yield 

   - _■S_ Increased input of secondary ferrous raw materials 

   - _■S_ Decreased deviation of measured carbon content at EAF and at ladle furnace 

   - _■S_ Increased yield of alloys 

   - _■S_ Increased rate of carbon oxidation, in particular for hot metal charges 

   - _■S_ C.O product closer to equilibrium conditions resulting in less alloy addition, better alloy prediction and more stable LF operation 

   - _■S_ Increased dephosphorization (decreased rephosphorization) 

   - _■S_ Decreased oxygen consumption 

- Provision of gas bubble columns in steel melt: 

   - _■S_ Avoidance of instantaneous or retarded CO boiling of steel melt 

From a series of case studies at customers with very specific targets of the DPP system the typical observed benefits were higher than 5 kWh/t electrical energy saving, 0.5-1 min decrease of power-on-time, and a 0.5 % increase of yield. Corresponding over-all cost savings were customer-specific, with a minimum value in the order of 1.5 €/tsteei, often higher. 

Bottom purging systems are claimed to have the shortest payback time compared to other measures for increasing EAF energy efficiency [5]. 

###### **Metallurgical Constraints for Special and Alloyed Stainless Steelmaking** 

Additional constraints apply for production of alloyed or high alloyed Cr or Cr-Ni raw steel melts in the EAF. Melting of stainless steel scrap requires higher specific electrical energy demand due to higher specific heat capacity of Cr alloys and due to lower heat conductivity of 

313 

stainless steel scrap. Optimum process of stainless steel melting requires therefore, e.g., increased bath movement to maximize heat transfer. 

As oxidation of carbon and chromium occurs at very similar oxygen activities in the steel melt, special care is taken in order to minimize chromium loss during oxygen injection. Homogeneous distribution of carbon, chromium and oxygen in the steel melt helps significantly to avoid concentration gradients and to improve yield. 

Low FeOx content and high &2O3 content of the EAF slag in stainless steel operation inhibits often efficient slag foaming. This is due to the low solubility of &2O3 in EAF basic slag that results in precipitation of &2O3 bearing solids and stiffened slag. Lack of FeO in the slag decreases the formation of CO gas, too [6]. High oxidation of Cr to the slag is in most cases caused by carbon deficiency of the steel volume that is affected by the oxygen injector. Improved mixing improves decarburization and chromium yield. 

In foundries the metallurgical fine-tuning of the raw steel melt is often done in the EAF. Yield of ferro-alloys depends on the activity of the metal alloy in the steel melt and of the activity of its oxides in the slag. Co

mpositional gradients in the steel melt leads to higher oxidation of alloys than necessary. Stirring of the melt by DPP purging increases homogeneity of the melt and yield. 

###### Case Studies 

DPP purging systems were also installed recently at EAFs for stainless and special steel production and in EAFs of foundries (2011 and 2012). EAF bottom purging systems quickly turned out as sustainable EAF technology for all 3 customers. 

- Recent application of a bottom purging system with 3 DPP bricks in a 100 t EAF for stainless steel production resulted in an increase of + 0.5 % yield at 0.5 m /t decrease of oxygen consumption and 5 kWh/t electrical energy demand. Depending on EAF process step gas flow rates between 50 and 110 1/min were applied. 

- Application of a single DPP bottom purging system in a 6 t EAF in a foundry for specialty steel and high alloyed steel products resulted in an significantly increased yield of alloys. 10 1/min gas flow rate was applied. 

- Installation of a DPP system in an 10 t EAF increased yield of ferro-alloy and decreased tap-to-tap time and electrical energy demand. 1 DPP purging brick installed, 7-10 1/min gas flow rate. 

###### Conclusions 

DPP bottom stirring systems are installed at a variety of EAFs in steel industry, from unalloyed and low alloyed to specialty and stainless steel production, from 6 t to 250 t tap weight. Especially in EAF steelmaking with metallurgical constraints bottom purging provides cost benefits by increased yield of ferroalloys, decreased electrical energy demand and oxygen consumption, and by advantages of more homogeneous melt concerning measurements and process control.

###### RESEARCHES ON REDUCTION ROASTING OF LOW-GRADE MANGANESE OXIDE ORES USING BIOMASS CHARCOAL AS REDUCTANT 

Yuanbo Zhang, Daoxian Duan, Zhixiong You , Guanghui Li, Xiaohui Fan, Tao Jiang 

(School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan 410083, China) 

Key words: low-grade manganese oxides, reduction roasting, biomass charcoal 

###### **Abstract** 

Presently, high-grade manganese oxide ores are usually utilized by a coal-based reduction roasting process. However, there were some obvious drawbacks, including serious environmental pollution, high energy consumption, etc. The reduction temperature is relatively high (850-900 °C). In this study, a kind of biomass, pine black charcoal, was used as a reductant to reduce low-grade manganese oxide ores. Under the optimal conditions of reduction temperature of 600-650 °C, roasting time of 30-45 min and ratio of ore to reductant 5:1, the leaching efficiency of manganese reached more than 98%. Compared with the traditional coal-based reduction process, the reduction temperature is reduced by 250-300 °C. 

###### **Introduction** 

Manganese plays a very important strategic role in the national economy, and it is widely used not only in the metallurgical industry, but also in the light industry, chemical industry, medicine, agriculture, etc [1]. The average grade of manganese ores in China is evenly about 21%, which belongs to typical low-grade manganese ores [2]. Therefore, large quantity of high-grade manganese ores is required to import in order to meet the rapid development of Chinese manganese industry. As reported, the conventional treatment of reduction roasting has been widely applied for processing manganese oxide ores, in which coals or reducing gases (CO, H2 or CH4) were usually used as reducers [3]. However, there were some insuperable problems, such as high energy consumption, poor operating conditions, serious environmental pollution, etc [4-9]. 

In recent years, biomass resources have been widely used as a clean, cheap and renewable energy in many fields of energy consumption. In this study, a kind of biomass charcoal, pine black charcoal, was used as a reductant to reduce the low-grade manganese oxide ores. The biomass charcoal is a black porous solid fuel. They are made from the wood, crop straws, etc., which are incompletely burned or pyrolyzed without air [10]. Tao Jiang , Gui-hong Han *, Yan-fang Huang , Guang-hui Li , Yuan-bo Zhang

Hunan, China, 410083 

Keywords: Oxidized pellets, Reduction extent, Swelling behavior 

###### **Abstract** 

Under isothermal conditions, the reduction behavior of oxidized pellets balled with bentonite was investigated with CO-CC>2gas mixers in the temperature range from 900 °C to 1100 °C. The whole reduction of oxidized pellets was followed up by means of weight-loss technique. And the swelling index of pellets was examined by visualizing physical changes of pellet in a horizontal tube furnace. The results present that the reduction rate of oxidized pellets is increased with the increase of reduction temperature. While the swelling index is firstly increased and then decreased with the increase of reduction time and reduction extent, which can be ascribed to the disruptive stresses induced during the transformation of hematite to magnetite. The maximum swelling index is gradually increased with the increase of reduction temperature and CO content. 

###### **Introduction** 

With the rapidly development of iron and steel industry, direct reduction iron has been considered as one kind of high quality bur

dens in electric furnace steelmaking [1]. At present, "Two-step" coal-based direct reduction process, which employs oxidized pellets as raw materials, has been used in industrial production [2]. The reduction behavior of iron ore oxidized pellets has been becoming one of the most frequently studied topics in extractive metallurgy[3]. The heat and mass transfer in direct reduction processes results in a series of stepwise reduction reaction (hematite-magnetite-wustite-iron), accompany with the volumetric swelling of pellets[4]. A lot of literatures have been reported on the reduction model of ferrous oxides and swelling behavior of pellets. A. A. El-Geassy K, et.al [5-7] revealed that the reduction process was controlled by chemical reaction at early stage by employing pure Fe2Ы3 as raw materials and CO as reduction gas. Chen Y [8] made research on the reduction kinetics of porous oxidized pellets and obtained the rate constant and activation energy of at different reduction stage. In addition, the swelling and disintegration of iron ore pellets was affected by chemical composition of pellet and reducing parameters, which have been studied by numerous investigators [3,9,10]. ###### Vanadium Distribution Between Blast Furnace Slag and Hot Metal 

Jia-Rong Yan , Bing Xie , Xiao-Yi Zeng , Qing-Yun Huang , Hong-Yi Li 'College of Materials Science and Engineering; Chongqing University, Chongqing, 400044, China 

Keywords: vanadium, distribution ratio, blast furnace, hearth of blast furnace 

###### **Abstract** 

In order to utilize vanadium resource in vanadium-titanium magnetite ore efficiently, vanadium distribution ratio between hot metal and slag should be improved during BF process, meanwhile the precipitating of Ti(C,N) in slag must be minimized. Effects of temperature, TiC>2 content in the slag and basicity on vanadium distribution between slag and hot metal w

ere investigated by experiment and thermodynamic calculation. The results indicated that high temperature, low TiC>2 content and high binary basicity of slag were beneficial to increase the vanadium distribution ratio. The effects of temperature and TiC>2 content in slag on vanadium distribution were stronger than that of slag basicity. 

###### **Introduction** 

Vanadium is an important element that is widely used in industrial fields. Most of vanadium resource is hosted in vanadium bearing titanomagnetite [1]. Vanadium bearing titanomagnetite is thus one of the domainate raw materials to produce the vanadium products. In other words, the comprehensive utilization of vanadium bearing titanomagnetite is beneficial for vanadium resource utilization. Vanadium bearing titanomagnetite sources are abundant in Pan Xi of China [4]. 

Pan Steel is the main vanadium products producer and the BF-BOF process is the mature process utilized to produce vanadium slag. In the BF-BOF process vanadium bearing titanomagnetite is firstly pelletized or sintered and then charged into blast furnace. After being smelted in blast furnace, most vanadium is reduced into the hot metal. The vanadium bearing hot metal is treated by the BOF process to obtain vanadium slag and semi-steel. Finally, the slag is treated by some hydrometallurgical process and vanadium products are thus obtained. Actually, the BF process plays a vital role in the whole flow for vanadium recovery. The hot metal with high vanadium content contributes to the production of high grade vanadium slag in the following BOF process, and eventually is beneficial for the production of different kinds of vanadium products. Therefore, high vanadium distribution ratio between the hot metal and slag in the blast furnace is required. During reduction of vanadium oxide, some of TiЫ2 would be transferred as Ti(C,N), which is harmful for the high efficiency production of BF, therefore, the relationship between vanadium reduction and Ti(C,N) generation was carried out in this research. 

To understand the influencing factors on the vanadium distribution between the hot metal and slag, several researches have been carried out. Liu[8] and Chao[9] studied the effect of temperature on the vanadium distribution in the blast furnace by kinetic analysis, the results revealed that higher temperature contributed to easier diffusion of vanadium into the hot metal. Meanwhile, some other study [10] results indicated that a higher content of TiЫ2 in slag would result in higher viscosity of slag which had a negative affecting on vanadium diffusion.

The thermodynamic model based on the electronic theory of metallurgical slag was employed to analyze the law of the vanadium distribution between hot metal and slag. The reduction of vanadium will be more easier at high temperature due to small value of AG<sup>e</sup> . The movement of vanadium ion will be speeded up at high temperature, which strengthens the effect of diffusion and contributes to the diffusion of vanadium ion into molten iron ultimately. Meanwhile, the collision probability between different kinds of particles (C, V<sup>3+</sup> , etc) will be increased at high temperature, which is beneficial to reduction of vanadium. 

Some researches had proven that Ti(C,N) solid particles will be easily precipitated with temperature increasing. It was commonly believed that 1470 °C -1480 °C was the sensitive temperature area for Ti(C,N) precipitation, and the foamy phenomena was not serious [6] below 1470°C. Therefore, temperature controlled between 1470°C~1480°C could be beneficial for vanadium reduction and Ti(C,N) precipitation.

###### **Conclusion** 

1. High content of Ti0 2 in slag is not favorable for vanadium reduction due to its negative effect on the slag viscosity. Exceeded reduction of TiC>2 will result in generation of Ti(C, N), and worsen diffusion of vanadium. 

2. High binary basicity will contribute to vanadium reduction due to the double functions of lime. Lime reacts with SiC>2 so the reaction between V2O3 and silicon is improved, and the forming of Ti(C,N) will be prevented as lime reacts with TiC>2, which is favorable for vanadium diffusion f

rom slag to hot metal. 

3. The vanadium distribution ratio and the vanadium reduction reaction rate will be increased with increasing temperature. Hearth temperature being controlled between 1470°C~1480°C was beneficial for vanadium reduction and Ti(C,N) precipitation control.

###### **Abstract** 

Antimony resources are rich in china, its reserves and productions are ranking the first in the world. The Chinese antimony mineral resources are mainly existed in the form of three types, such as stibnite, antimony-gold ores and jamesonite. The antimonial dust that produced from lead smelting process is an important secondary antimony resource. The different process that was adopted to extract antimony depends on the different raw materials. The process of blast furnace volatilization smelting is mainly used to treat stibnite and antimony-gold ores. But jamesonite is treated by the process of roasting-sintering-blast furnace smelting. And antimonial dust is treated in the reverberatory furnace. Many new technologies that are applied in these traditional antimony smelting processes play important roles, such as deleading agent, antimony white production, air-oxidation method, direct-blowing method, bath smelting technology, and so on. At the same time, the development of antimony smelting technology in china is prospected according to the requirement of the state environmental protection. 

###### **Introduction** 

There are five countries that produce antimony in the world, such as china, Tajikistan, Bolivia, Russia, and South africa, but China is the largest country of antimony production in the world. In the world, the antimony productions of 2008, 2009, and 2010 are 182,000 tons, 154,000 tons, and 167.000 tons respectively, but Chinese antimony productions are 166.000 tons, 140,000 tons, and 150,000 tons respectively. So Chinese antimony production was accounted for more than 89% of the world in 2010. It indicates that China have irreplaceable advantages in antimony resource and production all over the world. 

Antimony production in China is mainly concentrated in Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan and Gansu provinces, the main enterprise are Hunan Hsikwangshan Twinkling Star Co., Ltd, Hunan Chenzhou Mining Co,Ltd, Guangxi China Tin Group Limited by Share Ltd, and Yunnan Muli antimony industry Co.,Ltd, etal. The main mineral raw materials of antimony smelting in china are stibnite, antimony-gold ore, and jamesonite, etal, and antimonial dust from lead smelting process is the important secondary resource. According to incomplete statistics, the proportion of Chinese antimony production from different material in 2010 can be seen in Figure . 1. 

Throughout surveying the current antimony smelting industry in China

, more than 95% of antimony was produced by hydrometallurgy process. Stibnite and antimony-gold ore are treated by the process of volatilization smelting in blast furnace, and most of antimony is 341 volatilized in the forming of crude antimony oxide. The process of roasting- sinteringsmelting in blast furnace is applied to treat jamesonite, and antimonial dust is smelted in the reverberatory furnace, antimony is concentrated in the intermediate product of lead-antimony alloy. At last, the qualified antimony products are prepared from crude antimony oxide or lead-antimony alloy. Through elaborating the corresponding typical processes of them, it is focus on the important technical innovations of them in this paper. The development direction of antimony smelting technology is prospected. D Stibnite (78000t )

When the stibnite mineral is treated by different ore dressing methods, three types of ore can be produced, they are rich lump ore, lean lump ore and antimony concentrate. The lean lump ore are treated by volatilization roasting in roasting furnace, and the antimony concentrate and rich lump ore are smelted in blast furnace, all of antimony is volatilized in the form of crude antimony trioxide. Then the crude antimony trioxide is reduced and refined in reverberating furnace, and the qualified antimony ingot or antimony white can be produced[l,2]. Though the direct recovery rate of antimony can reach to 90%, but there are two problems, environment pollution with sulfur oxide and harmlessness treatment of alkaline slag with As. The flowsheet is shown in Figure .2. ###### Technical Innovation Antimony white (antimony trioxide) is as important as antimony ingot in all the antimony products. The self-heating method of producing antimony white was developed in 1958 by Hunan Hsikwangshan Twinkling Star Co., Ltd, and antimony white was produced by blowing air into pure antimony melt directly[3,4,5]. In order to improve the quality of it, the top-blown method which had advantages of low cost and stable quality was invented in 1997. The schematic diagram of antimony white furnace can be seen in Figure .3. On the basis of the news report in literature, the antimony-gold ore has been treated by two processes of the electric furnace smelting process in Russia and the blast furnace smelting process in China. The process of blast furnace smelting -electrolysis of gold-antimony alloy was the research results that developed in 1960s, and it has been applied to treat the antimony-gold ore in Hunan Chenzhou Mining Co, Ltd for many years. ###### Process The process of blast furnace volatilization smelting-electrolysis of gold-antimony alloy was introduced as follows. The briquette that made from the antimony-gold ore, lime and coke are drying in the air. The dry briquette is smelted in the blast furnace firstly and more than 90% of antimony is volatized in the form of crude antimony oxide and about 10% antimony exists in the form of metallic antimony that act as the collecting agents of gold in the forehearth of the blast furnace. The crude antimony was main materials for extracting gold. The crude antimony had to be oxidized to remove most of antimony and the gold was enriched in the gold-antimony alloy, which was then cast into anodes to be handled in the electrolysis. The anode mud was subsequently treated to produce gold bullion by the three procedure, such as nitric acid leaching, smelting in the crucible furnace and blowing in the muffle furnace. The gold bullion was casted into anodes to electrolysis and the 99.95% gold ingot can be produced The antimony oxide produced from the blast furnace must be treated by reduction smelting and oxidation blowing, and antimony oxide and gold-antimony with high-lead can be produced. The antimony oxide h

ad to be treated in the reverberatory furnace to produce antimony product. The gold-antimony with high-lead would be treated with gold-antimony alloy [7]. ###### New Technologies Along with the progress in technology, many new methods have been applied in this process. The roasting method that was used to treat the antimony matte was transferred to the ore dressing method. The solvent extraction was used to refine the gold-silver alloy instead of the electrolytic method. The technology of selective chlorination leaching under controlling potential was applied to concentrate gold from the gold-antimony alloy and gold-lead alloy instead of the electrolysis method, alkaline slag was recovered by the second reducing smelting method substituting for the mixed-salt method of sodium arsenate[8]. ###### EFFECT OF REDUCTION CONDITIONS ON PRE-REDUCTION BEHAVIORS OF SELF-FLUXED PELLETS IN COREX PROCESS 

De-qing Zhu, Zi-fu Gao , Jian Pan 

School of Minerals Processing and Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha410083, China 

Keywords: COREX, Pre-reduction, Metallization Rate, Compressive Strength 

###### **Abstract** 

In order to prod

uce high quality metalized products and prevent from burden cohesion during pre-reduction, self-fluxed pellets were made for COREX process in the paper. The effects of reduction temperature and reducing gas composition on pre-reduction behaviors of self-fluxed pellets are studied. The results show that the prereduced pellets have poor quality and deposited carbon appears when the reduction temperature is between 600°C and 700°C. The metallization rate, reduction degree and compressive strength of prereduced pellets are promoted by the elevating reduction temperature and mole fraction of H2. Pellets reduced by pure H2 at 800 °C have high metallization rate (96.2%), reduction degree (99.4%) and compressive strength (960N/pellet). In all tests, self-fluxed pellets display normal swelling (RSI<15%) behavior which reveals that self-fluxed pellets are suitable for COREX process. Increasing reduction temperature and mole fraction of H2 in reducing gas is benefit for pre-reduction of pellets. 

###### **Introduction** 

Compared with Blast Furnace, the COREX process has advantages of short flow sheet, using non-coke coal and high-energy utilization. Acidic pellets and lump ores are the chief ironbearing burden for COREX process which could lead to low melting point substance appearing in per-reduction process. In addition, the acidic hematite pellets tend to swell during the reduction [1-3]. This will result in decreasing compressive strength of pellets, burden cohesion, bad air permeability and poor work status in shaft furnace. Adding carbonate flux could restrain burden bonding to some extent in actual production, but decomposition of carbonate flux increases energy consumption. Worse still, weak reduction potential is unfavorable to iron material reduction [4, 5]. 

With the purpose of preventing pellets from being crushed and cohesion during reduction, high compressive strength and low swelling of pellets during reduction are required. As self-fluxed pellets have good metallurgical performances [6, 7]. Therefore, the research was carried out to study the reduction behaviors of self-fluxed pellets with different reduction temperatures and reducing gas composition, including the metallization rate, reduction degree, compressive strength and reduction swelling index. The high quality prereduced pellets were produced by optimizing reduction temperature and reducing gas compositions, and the self-fluxed pellets could be a good kind of charging burden for COREX process.

Pellets of 500g were prepared with size of 10 ~ 12.5 mm and 12.5 ~ 16 mm accounting for 50%, respectively. The pellets were reduced in the reaction tube ( 75 mm x800 mm) for 3 hours. The pellets were cooled in nitrogen atmosphere when the reduction was finished. The reducing gas flow rate was 0.8m -h" . The influence of gas composition on reduction behavior was studied by changing the H2 / (CO + H2) mole ratio (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) when the temperature was fixed at 800 °C. The compressive strength is determined by the metallic iron grain and slag phase in prereduced pellets. The swelling is caused by the crystal lattice distortion during hematite being reduced to magnetite in pellets [9]. Figure 3 depicts the microstructure o

f the prereduced pellets at different temperatures. The distribution of metallic iron grains changes from punctiform to lamellar. The metallic iron grains are less distributed while the magnetite and pores distribute in a big area 

356 

(Figure 3(a)), which result in low compressive strength and high swelling index. When the temperature increases, the crystal particles make pellets dense due to the lamellar distributed of metallic iron grains become more and pores get less (Figure 3 (b), (c), (d)). Therefore the compressive strength increases and swelling index comes down. Additionally, the calcium ferrite (CaO-Fe2C>3) is formed in the pellets roasted process. Metallic iron layer is generated on the surface of calcium wustite rather than iron whisker during reduction. The presence of Metallic iron layer would inhibit the pellets expansion to a certain extent, so the reduction swelling indices are relatively small (<15%).

Although the metallization rate of prereduced pellets at 900°C (94.9%) is higher than that at 800 °C (80.1%) , the pellets and lump ore stick together in actual production at high temperatures(>850°C) [10-13]. So the reduction temperature is set at 800°C in the following gas optimization tests in order to get better quality prereduced pellets. 

###### Effect of Reducing Gas Composition on Pellets Redction Behavior 

The effect of reducing gas composition on metallization rate, reduction degree, compressive strength and reduction swelling index of prereduced pellets are shown in Figure 4. Reduction degree and compressive strength of pellets are improved by an increase in mole fraction of H2 in reducing gas. Metallization rate, reduction degree and compressive strength are achieved to

81.1%, 70.4% and 522 N-pellet"<sup>1</sup> when the pellets was reduced by pure CO (H2 /(CO + H2)=0).As the mole fraction of H2 increases to 100% (pure H2), the metallization rate and reduction degree reach 96.2% and 99.4%, respectively, and the compressive strength is 960N-pellet" . While the reduction swelling index drops from 11.2% to 5.5% with the mole fraction of H2 at 50%. After that the swelling index rises slightly. The pellets have normal swelling (<15%) with the increasing mole fraction of H2. 

Due to the fact that H2 has better thermal conductivity, lower viscosity coefficient and smaller atomic radius and larger diffusion ability than that of CO. H2 diffuses faster than CO into the reaction surface in pellets, and at the same time, reaction product H2O spreads faster than CO2 from reaction surface to the outside air. Which illustrates H2 is more active than CO [14]. Therefore the elevation of mole fraction of H2 in reducing gas could enhance metallization rate and reduction degree of prereduced pellets.

###### CALCINATION FACTORS OF RUBIDIUM EXTRACTION FROM LOWGRADE MUSCOVITE ORE 

Shan Zhiqiang<sup>1-2</sup> , Shu Xinqian<sup>1</sup> , Feng Jifu<sup>2</sup> , Zhou Weining<sup>2</sup> 

1 School of Chemical and Environmental Engineering, China University of Mining & Technology; Peking, Haidian District, 100083, China Comprehensive Utilization Research Institute of Resource, Guilin Research Institute Geology for Mineral Resources; Guilin, Qixing District, 541004, China 

**Keywords:** Modified calcination, Muscovite ore, Chlorinating agent 

###### **Abstract** 

Modified calcination conditions on the extraction of rubidium resources from muscovite (KAl2[AlSi30io](OH)2) ore are systematically studied. The impact of

various factors on the rubidium leaching rate is also analyzed, including the agent types, roasting time, the mass ratio, roasting temperature, etc. The results indicate that the best agent is a combination of sodium chloride and calcium chloride, its mass ratio of muscovite/NaCl/CaC^ is 1:0.25:0.25. Calcined at 850 D for 30 minutes, the rubidium leaching rate is up to 90%. The reaction of muscovite ore with the chlorinating agent CaC12 has been studied by TG/DSC, the calcined intermediates are identified by XRD, and the surface morphology before and after leaching is characterized by SEM. Rubidium chloride products can be obtained with a purity of 92% by using t-BAMBP extraction, hydrochloric acid reextraction and purification. 

###### **Introduction** 

Rubidium is one of rare alkali metals, which is found in 1981 by German R.W. Bunsen and G.R. Kirchhof. Rubidium includes the following features: atomic number is 37, each atom weight 85, the body-centred cubic lattice, each unit cell has two metal atoms, and the density is 1.532g/cm<sup>3</sup> . The properties of low melting point (312.46 K) and malleability make rubidium have a strong chemical activity and photoemission. Rubidium provides a main material for manufacturing phototube with a wide range of light waves, which possess high sensitivity and stability. Efforts are being made to carry out research on rubidium ion gngine, magnetic flux generators and thermoelectric transudcer, etc. Rubidium exists in muscovite ore(KAl2[AlSi30io](OH)2 (monoclinic system and hexagonal layered structure) as isomorphism and replace the large radius of the potassium atoms, as well as part of rubidium locate between structure layers. The complex components bring great difficulty in comprehensive recycling. 

Ion exchange, precipitation and extraction are the three main methods in the rubidium resource recovery from muscovite ore. However, the ion exchange method lead to a substantial decline in value for the actual production and complex sample analysis, for high solubility of inorganic ion exchange agent in the water, the poor anti-interference ability of organic resin to the presence of multicharged ions and other reasons. It's main disadvantage of precipitation method is high reagent consumption. To get high-purity substances must be through several precipitation and separation. Rubidium can be easily separated from mother liquor by solvent extraction technology. During rubidium production process, modified calcination is the key process. Its aim is to maximize rubidium leaching rate and determine the mutual correlations among the various factors. 

361 

So, it is important to develop an efficient method for extracting rubidium from its ore and it has been a thrust area of research and development.

###### **Abstract** 

A high iron content manganese ore was reduced at 900-1200 °C and followed by a magnetic separation process. SEM and EDS analyzes were employed to examine the transformation of microstructure and phase in reduced sample and the mechanism was revealed. Results showed that elements enriched during reduction. Iron existed in the metal iron phase and most of oxygen formed compound with manganese. Consequently a clear distinguish between iron phase and manganese minerals formed, which was beneficial to the separation of iron and manganese. But the iron phase can not be monomer dissociation in grinding process and manganese compounds turned into magnetic product as package and mechanic inclusion due to the isomorphism of iron and manganese and the small particle size. And MnO could be found partially in iron phase, which hindered the further separation of manganese and iron.

###### **Abstract** 

WorleyParsons has used Discrete Event Simulation methods in conjunction with more traditional process models to assess the performance of copper smelting operations. This work was performed to determine the plant capacities and suitability of proposed de

bottlenecking options including accounting for the planned and unplanned (breakdowns) shutdowns in the various parts of the plant and supply chain. This paper outlines the methods used along with demonstrating the benefits of selecting a feasible option and minimizing capital and operating costs. ###### **Introduction** Traditionally for debottlenecking studies of smelters and other process plants, a mass balance is performed based on continuous operating rates and expected operating hours. Smelters have several points of failure that will restrict, if not take the entire plant offline. By using a more detailed model, validated against plant experience, bottlenecks can be demonstrated and strategies to remove them to increase plant availability and economic. The modeling simulates the plant performance in real time, and by performing enough simulation the expected long run performance of the plant can be estimated. The models have been built using ExtendSim which is a powerful Discrete Event Simulation software package that is ideally suited to the batch and semi-batch processes and events that occur within smelter operating environments. The value of performing this work is that the operational performance of the plant can be assessed ensuring production targets are met, without using excessive capital outlay. ###### **The Optimization Process** Common steps to any optimization process are to identify the limits/constraints within your smelter, and then to look at ways to remove or ease this restriction on your plant. Other changes to the plant, operating practices and expansions can also be simulated. The actual process of performing the optimization includes several steps in the cycle as shown in Figure 1 : Collecting data, building the model, performing the simulation, reviewing the results to ensure they are reasonable, modeling scenarios and presenting the masses of information in a clear way. This is a collaborative process between metallurgists, engineers, operators and clients. 379 Data Collection

Case **Studies** The best way to illustrate how these models have been used is to examine work that WorleyParsons has performed for clients. The two studies represent a smelter where material is transferred by launder between furnaces and another using a crane aisle. Copper Smelter: Launder Transfer Operation As part of a project to debottleneck and increase production through a copper smelter, WorleyParsons was examining the impacts of increased production through the system, and the various improvements that were required to process the increased rates through the plant. One of the challenges on this plant is the decoupling of the feed preparation plant from the furnace and managing the increasing slag fall from the furnaces and increased overall metal production rates. This included examining the furnaces throug

h to the Anode furnaces and slag cleaning furnace to the slag hauler operation. WorleyParsons has a number of in-house process models that are used for simulation of the various furnaces found in smelters. This ranges from simplified spreadsheet models to more complex METSIM models of furnaces. One of the challenges of using a spreadsheet to model a system is that it becomes unwieldy to use to simulate the operation of a furnace with time. Additionally spreadsheets are notoriously hard to debug when errors are found within them. Typically only a single furnace is modeled to reduce the complexity using a spreadsheet, whilst a modeling package has the ability to model the entire operation. The model contains two types of furnaces: continuously operated furnaces like the flash furnace; and semi-batch operated furnaces as such as the Slag Cleaning furnace and the anode furnace. The continuously operated furnace is fed material for smelting unless the furnace is offline, no feed is available and the furnace is below the maximum operating level. Tapping occurs when a minimum level of material is in the furnace - although there needs to be an available pot and/or furnace to tap into. 380 For the batch operated furnaces, the furnace is operated through the operating cycle. Cycles are incremented on either achieving the required volume/mass of material (or emptying/lowering the furnace level) or the elapsed cycle time has occurred.
