###### **Abstract** 

In the sintering process, the behavior and performance of iron ores is extremely complex. Different minerals have different sintering properties. In order to use iron ores rationally and effectively, multilevel fuzzy evaluation method is used to establish the comprehensive evaluation model of iron ores. Because of the relative independent characters of iron ores in sintering process, the characters can be divided into physical and chemical properties, granulation performance, and sintering properties, are divided, and together with iron ores prices as the first level index for judging, which are used as the second level index for judging. Using the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to determine the weight of each index, which is used as the second level index. The relative membership matrix is determined by triangular membership function, the comprehensive evaluation model is established. 

###### **Introduction** 

In China, sintering is the main method for iron ores agglomeration. Sinter accounts for more than 80% of the blast furnace. Sinter production in the iron and steel enterprises in China plays an important role[l-2]. As the main raw material of iron ores sintering, the objectivity and integration of iron ores evaluation is essential. The iron ores evaluation methods include of metric ton price evaluation method, iron grade of a single iron ores sintering, acid-base balance method, composition assessment method and other methods which are based on the chemical composition and physical properties of iron ores to measure the quality of iron ores[3]. The high-temperature mineralization is an important process in sintering process, which affects the structure and mineral composition of the sinter, and has a close relationship with the quality of the sinter[4]. Therefore, in consideration of the physical and chemical properties, granulation properties, mineralization performance and sintering properties, the iron ores are evaluated by multi-level fuzzy comprehensive evaluation. The multi-level fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method makes a comprehensive evaluation, applying fuzzy transform principle and maximum membership degree principle, considering a number of factors related to the thi

ngs which are evaluated. The method has lower requirements for the amount of data, and which integrates qualitative with quantitative judgment. It has a unique advantage to make up for the deficiencies of traditional evaluation methods. It also can comprehensively evaluate the iron ores in a relatively short period, reduce a lot of experiments, improve efficiency and guide the sinter production[5-6]. 385 ###### **Modeling** The Determination of Evaluating Indicator According to the performances of the iron ores in sintering process, the evaluation indexes are divided into the physical and chemical properties, granulation performance, mineralization properties and sintering properties, which are used as the first layer of the evaluation index. 1) The performances of the iron ores in sintering process are divided into the physical and chemical properties, granulation performance, mineralization properties and sintering properties which are used as evaluation index. The weights of the evaluation index are defined by AHP. This method considers the complicated relationships among the properties of iron ores. And the weights are accurately determined. 

2) By using the triangle membership function, the relative membership degree is identified, which includes three types value: maximum value, minimum value, fixed value. 

3) The multistage fuzzy evaluation model on iron ores sintering is established. According to the principle of maximum membership degree, the iron ores grade can be determined by the final evaluation results. The model can achieve a comprehensive evaluation of the performance of iron ores in a relatively short period, reduce the amount of experimental work, improve efficiency and guide the sintering production.

###### CFD MODEL DEVELOPMENT FOR GASEOUS REDUCTION OF IRON ORE FINES USING MULTILAYER MOVING-FLUIDIZED BED 

Huiqing Tang<sup>1</sup> , Ying Mao<sup>1</sup> , Long Ma<sup>1</sup> , Zhancheng Guo<sup>1</sup> 

^tate key laboratory of advanced metallurgy, University of Science and Technology Beijing; 30 Xueyuan Rd.; Beijing, 100083, China 

Keywords: CFD model, Gaseous reduction, Iron ore fines, Multilayer moving-fluidized bed 

###### **Abstract** 

A new 2D computational fluid dynamic (CFD) model was developed for the gaseous reduction of iron ore fines in an innovative reactor- multilayer moving-fluidized bed. The solution of the proposed model was performed by integration of FLUENT and PHOENICS. Numerical results of cold state were compared with the experimental data and the agreement between them was good. A hot case-gaseous reduction of iron ore fines using syngas with this reactor was simulated using the present CFD mode. Results indicate that under the given simulation conditions, total pressure drop is 90 Pa less than that under cold state though the gas supply rate is increased about 4m3 under hot state. Gas temperature decreases from 1073 K at the bottom to 500 K at the top, Utilization efficiency of the gas reduction potential is about 27 %. For ore fines reduction, the final reduction fraction could reach 0.70 and solid temperature 900 K. 

###### **Introduction** 

With the development of coal gasification technology, various coals could be converted to Syngas with air or steam. Therefore gaseous reduction of iron ore fines becomes an acceptable alternative process for iron making besides blast furnace routefl] and moreover it still has some advantages in processing low grade iron ore fines[2]. Gaseous reduction using fluidized bed technologies is the most competitive in all direct reduction iron-making processes up to now. It has the advantage that ore fines can be directly charged to the process without prior treatment while its disadvantages are particle agglomeration and high gas/solid ratio[3]. To avoid these advantages, a new reactor, multilayer moving-fluidized bed reactor has been developed for carrying out the gaseous reduction. Hydrodynamic behaviors of gas and fines in the reactor were studied and the results were satisfying[4]. However, due to

its unique structure of the multilayer moving-fluidized bed and unique gas-solid flow pattern, models of multiphase flow as IPSA, DPM and Eulerian Model could not give a satisfying solution. The current paper is developed a new CFD model and a new solution approach for simulation of the reactive gas-solid flow in the multilayer moving-fluidized bed for its optimization, design improvement and future scale-up. ###### **Physical Model** The lab-scale reactor is mainly composed of a vertical gas chamber(300mmx70mmx 1200mm) and five perforated plates(carbon steel, aperture ratio: 20%). The perforated plates are installed in the gas chamber with an inclination angle of 7.0 degree and linked using flowing- down channels. Ore fines are feed in at the top and collected at the bottom. Reducing gas is introduced 401 from the bottom and released from the top. The ore fines flow downwards weakly bubbling along the Z-shape path of the perforated plates and the flowing-down channels because of the drag force and the gravity. Gas flows upward penetrating the ore layers one by one. Thus the ore fines get heated and reduced. B

Gridgen exports the grid of the whole computational domain for FLUENT and exports the grid of zone D for PHOENICS and thus the two package could be ensured to have mesh elements in zone A with the same sizes and the same positions. The gas-flow model which covers the whole computational domain is solved using FLUENT while the solid-flow model which only covers domain D is solved using PHOENICS. They share the grid elements in zone D which are of the same sizes and the same positions. The 405 two packages ran on two networked work stations simultaneously and are linked together by data exchange on zone D for updating source items of both models. Each simulation runs until the non-dimensional residuals of the continuity equations of both gas phase and solid phase reached the convergence criterion of 0.0001. ###### **Results and Discussion** ###### Validation Cold model experimental results[4] were used to validate the CFD model. ###### Hot Case Study The reducing gas for simulation is the product of co-gasification of coal and methane. It's a mixture of H2: 45%, H 20: 1.0%, CO: 45% ,C02: 1.0% andN 2 : 8.0% namely Syngas. Operation conditions for the simulation are : For gas, its supply rate is 44.0 m3 /h and its inlet temperature 1073K; for ore fines, its feed rate is 240g/min and its inlet temperature 300K. The mass composition of the iron ore fines is assumed to be: Fe2Ы3: 90%, A12Ы3: 7%, Si0 2 :3%. 406 Gas Phase Behavior Hot state simulation results showed the gas flow pattern (stream lines) was similar to that under cold state. Figure 3(a) gives gas pressure profile under hot state. The total pressure loss of gas phase in the reactor under hot state is some 80 Pa less than that under cold state though gas supply rate is increased to 44 m3 /h. This difference is mainly due to that pressure drops on the top two plates are 50 Pa and 70 Pa respectively and are far less than the average pressure drop per plate, 85 Pa under the cold state. Pressure drops on the lower three plates are nearly equal to their counterparts under cold state. Gas temperature profile under hot state is given in Figure 3(b). Total gas temperature drop is about 600 K in the reactor and gas temperature drop is about 200 K on the top plate and on the bottom plate and is about 70 K on the middle three perforated plates. Profiles of CO and H2 mole fractions are shown in Figs. 3(cd). CO and H2 exhibit very different behaviors. CO continuously reacts with the iron ore fines on the perforated plates except the top one; its mole fraction deceases from 0.45 at the bottom to 0.29 at the top. H2 reacts with iron ore fines mainly on the bottom perforated plate but reacts little as the gas flows through the other four plates; its mole fraction deceases from 0.45 at the bottom to 0.37 at the top. Utilization rate of the gas reduction potential is about 27 %. Solid Phase Behavior For simplicity, to evaluate the reduction and heating efficiencies of the ore fines in the reactor, variations of reduction fraction and temperature of the solid phase along the middle stream line of the solid phase are considered and are shown in Figure 4. Zero increase intervals on solid temperature line and reduction fraction line reflect ore fines flowing through flowing-down channels. From Figure 4, it could be seen that the fi

nal reduction fraction reaches 0.70 and the final solid temperature 900 K. Temperature and reduction fraction of the ore fines increase as the ore fines flow downward. Some 90% of the reduction takes place on the lower three plates and the reduction on the top plate could be negligible. The solid temperature increases from 300 K to 700 K when the ore fines flow through the top two plates and increases from 700 K to 900 K when they flow through the others. It could be concluded that the higher two plates mainly play a role of preheating the ore fines and the lower three plates play a role of reducing the ore fines besides the role of heating the ore fines. A combination analysis of gas behavior and solid behavior shows that the top two plates in the reactor could be saved. There are two reasons: (l).pressure drops on these two plates are less than those on the others under hot state and this would make the reactor difficult to control;(2).Function of these two plates for the solid phase is mainly preheating and this could realized by other means. 407 Figure 3. ###### DEFORMATION SIMULATION OF COPPER PLATES OF SLAB CONTINUOUS CASTING MOLD 

Xiang-ning Meng ' , Wei-ling Wang , Miao-yong Zhu , Ryosuke O. Suzuki 

School of Materials & Metallurgy, Northeastern University; 3-11 Wen Hua Rd.; Shenyang, Liaonmg, 110819, P. R. China Faculty of Engineering, Hokkaido University; Kita-13 Nishi-8, Sapporo, Hokkaido, 060-8628, Japan 

Keywords: Slab continuous casting, Mold, Deformation of copperplates, Cooling structure, Finite element analysis 

###### **Abstract** 

A finite-element thermal-stress model of continuous casting mold is conducted to predict deformation of copper plates and its change with different cooling structure. The results show that deformation behavior of copper plates is mainly governed by cooling structure and thermalmechanical conditions, deformation amount is related to structure geometry, and a small deformation mutation occurs in cooper-nickel boundary due to different properties. The maximum deformation of hot surface centricities of wide face locate at 100 mm below meniscus and that of narrow face locate at meniscus and terminal of water slots and significant curvature fluctuations on both sides of copper-nickel boundary. The maximum deformation of centricities is increased up to 0.05 mm with thickness increment 5 mm of copper plates, and maximum deformations are only depressed 0.01 mm and 0.02 mm with increments of 1 mm nickel layer thickness and 2 mm water slot depth respectively. 

###### **Introduction** 

In conventional continuous casting of steel, a large amount of sensible and latent heat of molten steel dissipate in primary cooling zone and make continuous casting mold under enormous heating load giving rise to thermal stress, deformation, high-temperature fatigue and creep not only depress mold life-span, but reduce casting stability ' . Many studies focused more on heat transfer, solidification and shrinkage of solidifying shell to provide inverse proposals for optimizing cooling system and even designing new taper of mold ' ' , but it is generally useless to those of having been manufactured or being put into production. Therefore, mold-related forward problems show necessity to be discussed deeply, and stress and deformation distributions based on special thermal conditions in mold should be analyzed in order to explore suitable cooling structure of mold directly. Samarasekera et al. ' ' examined heat flow and distortion of two-dimensional longitudinal sections and investigated effect of cooling water velocity, copper plates thickness and carbon content on formation of rhomboidity and longitudinal corner cracks. O'Connor et al. ' ' developed a three-d

imensional mathematical model to compute thermo-mechanical state in thin-slab mold and calculated temperature and deformation of mold wall to assess roles of various process parameters on impacting mold life. Thomas et al. ' ' predicted temperature, distortion and residual stress in mold and indicated increased distortion requires increased remachining, which reduces mold life and increased residual stress increases the probability of a catastrophic crack failure. Park et al. ' ' determined heat-flux profiles in funnel-shaped and parallel thin-slab molds based on an inverse heat conduction model and thermocouple temperature measured in-plant and put them into three- 

411 

dimensional finite-element thermal-stress model to predict temperature, distortion and residual stress of mold wall. Koric et al. ' ' focused on prediction of temperature, distortion and residual stress in mold and in particular to clarify that mold life is significantly affected by temperature and its rigidity, but little effect by mechanical including clamping force, bolt prestress, friction and ferrostatic pressure. Meng et al. ' ' predicted temperature and thermal stress in a slab mold and analyzed effect by cooling system geometry and casting speed quantitatively. In present study, a three-dimensional finite-element thermo-mechanical model with type-switched element is transformed from previous heat-transfer finite-element model ' , and mold deformation is simulated in order to shed light on thermo-mechanical behavior with special thermal conditions and different mold geometry at high casting speed. 

###### **Mathematical Models** 

###### Finite-Element Entity Model 

In previous research discussed temperature calculation of mold copper plates ' , a threedimensional physical entity model following design diagram has been established according to geometry shown in Figure 1 (a) and Figure 1 (b). In present study, entity model is transformed into a new thermo-mechanical model for stress-strain finite-element analysis and meshed using three-dimensional 10-node tetrahedral thermal solid element. In order to simulate stress and deformation of hot copper plates of slab mold, following assumptions have been made: (1) perfect bonding exist between hot copper plates and steel backup plates, and internal stress caused by bolts connection is neglected, (2) properties of thermal and mechanical of hot copper plates and steel backup plates are isotropic, (3) physical properties such as density and heat capacity of materials change little with temperature, and thermal conductivity is dependent on temperature, (4) steel backup plates is of relative low-temperature and high rigidity then assumed to be elastic only and hot copper plates is modeled as a bilinear elastic-plastic material and (5) copper and steel follow von Mises yield criterion as common metal materials, and unit deformation of metals is caused by equivalent stress from deviator strain energy.

The deformation of copper plates presented specific regularity subject to cooling structure, mold geometry and heat-transfer conditions and maximums are 0.34 mm and 0.4 mm on wide and narrow face respectively and appeared in meniscus. 2. The deformation is increased with thickness of copper plates. The primary cooling and heat flux have greater impact on deformation, while property difference of copper and nickel has little effect. 3. The nickel layer is too thin to affect deformation significantly, and almost no impact on wide face. The maximum decline of 0.01 mm with thickness increment 1 mm appears in narrow face adjacent to copper-nickel boundary. 4. The deformation is reduced with depth of cooling water slots, and maximum is 0.02 mm with depth increments 2 mm of deep and shallow water slots. ###### AN ESTIMATION MODEL FOR THE VISCOSITIES OF CAF2-(CAO)AL2O3 SLAGS 

SHI Guan-yong<sup>1</sup> , ZHANG Ting-an<sup>1</sup> , NIU Li-ping<sup>1</sup> , DOU Zhi-he<sup>1</sup>

Keywords: viscosity; estimation model; CaF2-(CaO)-Al203; ESR slags. 

###### **Abstract** 

In the preset work, the viscosity model (named modified KTH model) proposed by Sichen Du and S. Seetharaman _et al_ and extended by Shu Qi-feng was applied to the ESR slag systems. A correlation to predict the viscosities of CaF2-(CaO)-Al203 slags using interaction coefficients of different cations in the presence of O<sup>2</sup> " and viscosity interaction coefficients between O<sup>2</sup> " and F" in the presence of different cations has been developed. The interaction coefficient between O<sup>2</sup> " and F" in the presence of Al<sup>3+</sup> was determined from the experimental data as shown in known l

iteratures. The good agreement between the calculated viscosities and the experimental data in the CaF2-(CaO)-Al203 systems has indicated that this approach can be successfully employed to predict the viscosities of ESR slags. 

###### **Introduction** 

Reliable viscosities data of high-temperature slag melts are important for the modeling and design of high temperature metallurgical processes. Although a number of experimental measurements have been carried out, the available viscosities data is still scarce compared to the needs of today's technology, especially in the case of complex melts. In process simulations, the needs of viscosity descriptions for complex systems which could enable the extrapolation of the data as functions of temperature and composition is strongly felt today. 

Dou Zhihe, _et al._ ''"''developed a new method, named as Aluminium Thermal ReductionElectroslag Remelting method, for preparing the large-size immiscible alloys such as CuCr alloy. This method includes the two key steps. The one is aluminium thermal reductionelectromagnetic casting step, during which the Self-consumption ingots were gotten; and the other is the electroslag remelting step, during which the Self-consumption ingots would be refined to get the alloy ingots. The CaF2-Al2C>3 and CaF2-CaO- AI2O3 slag systems are the primary slag systems using in the electro-slag remelting process. In the preset work, the modified KTH model proposed by Sichen Du and S. Seetharaman _et al_ '<sup>3</sup> ~<sup>6</sup> ' and extended by Shu Qifeng'<sup>7</sup> ' was applied to the CaF2-Al2C>3 and CaF2-CaO-Al203 slag systems. A correlation to predict the viscosities of CaF2-(CaO)-Al203 slags using Gibbs energy of mix for viscosity in the presence of different cations has been developed.

###### **Conclusion** 

A mathematical model for estimating the viscosities of CaF2-(CaO)-Al2C>3 slags using Gibbs energy of mix for viscosity in the presence of different cations has been developed in the present work. The reliability of the model in extrapolating the viscosity data as a function of temperature and composition has been demonstrated, the model calculations are in good agreement with the experimental data in CaF2-(CaO)- A1203 system.

Keywords: Thermodynamic modeling, CaO-FetO-CaF2, mould flux, Modified Quasichemical Model, FactSage. 

###### **Abstract** 

All relevant thermodynamic and phase diagram data in the CaO-FetO-CaF2 system were critically reviewed. One set of model parameters describing the Gibbs energy of all phases has been obtained as a result of critical evaluation of the available data and optimization of the model parameters. The Modified Quasichemical Model was used to describe the interactions in the liquid phase. All calculations were performed using the FactSage thermochemical software. 

###### **Introduction** 

Slags containing CaF2 are of significant interest to the steelmaking community. Notable examples of slags containing significant amounts of CaF2 include Electro-slag Remelting (ESR) slags [1] and mould flux for continuous casting [2]. The role of these slags is, among other things, to refine steel by absorbing inclusions and dissolved impurities. During slag-steel interaction, some iron from the steel will inevitably get oxidized and form iron oxides which will dissolve into the slag. With this in mind, it is important to understand the interaction between CaF2 and FetO for accurate prediction of slag composition and process optimization. A thermodynamic optimization of the CaO-FetO-CaF2 was thus undertaken. 

All thermodynamic and phase equilibrium data were collected and critically reviewed. A set of Gibbs energy functions wa

s found which describes the most reliable experimental data. These functions can be used to back-calculate the phase diagram and thermodynamic properties of the system making these functions self-consistent and consistent with thermodynamic principles. These functions can be incorporated into a database for oxyfluoride systems CaO-Si02-Al2C>3Na20-MgO-Li20-MnO-FeO-F allowing for better prediction of the equilibrium in slags pertaining to this composition. ###### **Abstract** 

The viscous flow phenomenon in slag close to the liquidus temperature was considered. A simple approach that liquidus temperatures of melt could be derived from viscosity data was employed. The potential of this method for estimating the liquidus temperatures of pure water and binary alloy was demonstrated. The liquidus temperatures of the CaO-AL^ based slags obtained from the second derivative method depends upon the number of viscosity values available at different temperature intervals. The results indicated that plots start deviating from the straight-line behavior at temperature as expect, and the second derivatives show the break points at a certain temperature, which is the liquidus temperature. Comparisons among the present observations as well as the characteristic temperature of the selected slags, which measured by the hemisphere method and DSC, indicated that it is possible to get a reasonable idea of estimate the liquidus temperatures from activation energies for viscous flow. 

###### **Introduction** 

The liquidus temperature of slag, which has a significant effect on the kinetics of chemical reactions and the slag-metal separation, is extremely important for metallurgical operations. Experimental measurements of the liquidus temperatures of slags are difficult, since slags invariable supercool. In addition, behavior of a single constituent in a multi-component slag is different in different circumstances due to its interaction with other constituents. Hence, it is essential to study the liquidus temperature of each particular slag resulting from a special process. Usually, the compositions of the slags aimed to the single liquid region of the phase diagram However, the phase diagram of many slag systems, which back often to the 1950's, involves considerable uncertainties. Many liquidus temperatures are given as dotted lines in Slag Atlas [1]. Disagreements between the phase diagram and the reality have been found [2]. 

Viscosity as an important physical property is sensitive to the slag structure. It is well known that the viscosities of liquidus increase with decreasing temperature. The temperature dependence of the viscosity is usually expressed in the form for the Arrhenius relationship. Recent viscosity measurements show a deviation of the temperature dependence of viscosity from the Arrhenius law in certain ranges of temperature [3-7]. That devia

tion behavior is near the melting point. As some solid particles often precipitate from slags at and below the liquidus temperature, the viscosities exhibit non-Newtonian behavior, and show a sharp viscosity increase near and below the liquidus temperature. This would result in departures form linearity in the logarithm of the viscosity plot vs. the inverse of the temperature in contrast to the classical Arrhenius behavior. Seetharaman et al. [7] has shown that the second derivative of the activation energy for viscous flow with respect to temperature shows a break around the 

435 

liquidus temperature of the slag. A more simple approach that values of liquidus temperatures could be derived for slags from viscosity data, which is the focus of the present article. It is hoped that the present work would estimating the liquidus temperatures of slag from the viscosity data more efficient. 

###### **Theoretical Analyses And Evaluation Method** 

###### Temperature dependence of viscosities 

The viscosity of liquid depends upon the nature of the chemical bond and the configuration of the species in the liquid. As a function of the interionic forces, viscosity for molten slag dependent on the sizes and charges of the ions involved. Stronger forces would lead to an increase in the viscosities [8]. As we known, when a homogeneous liquid silicate is being cooled, the long-range ordering in the system is expected to increase, which is probably due to the long-range electrostatic shielding of ions, and the degree of ordering increase. As a consequence, the viscosities of slag increase with decreasing temperature as expect. Arrhenius equation is one of the most frequently formulas used to represent the temperature dependence of the viscosity of slag in a wide temperature range. 



where A is proportionality constant, R is the gas constant, Q is the apparent activation energy for viscous flow, which represents the change of frictional resistance for viscous flow, and T is the temperature in K. Viscosity data as a function of temperature are usually presented in the form of the logarithm of viscosity as a function of the inverse temperature. The activation energy of melt, which is actually a measure of the resistance to flow in the liquid due to the variation of the electrostatic forces between the ions, is a very important factor for viscosity. The activation energy is related to the energy needed to break interionic bonds, and the latter is directly linked to thermodynamics [9]. 

It is, however, important to point out that molten slags are made up of discrete ionic structural units and their activation energy is closely related to the type of ions and ionic complexes present as well as the interionic forces they give rise to. Since types and sizes of ions changes with temperature, the activation energy changes with temperature. An improved fit can, in this case, be obtained by using the Weymann [10], Brostow [11] and The Vogel-Tammann-Fulcher (VTF) equ

ation [12] relationship. However, the temperature dependence of the viscosity is still fully empirical. 





###### Second derivative of the viscosity activation energy with respect to temperature 

It has been shown previously that the activation energy for viscous flow can be correlated to the thermodynamic excess Gibbs energy of mixing; thus, one would expect that the formation of ionic associations should also be indicated in the second derivative of the activation energy for viscous flow with respect to temperature [7]. The classical Arrhenius definition of activation energy for viscous flow (Eq. [1]) has been considered in the present work. The choice of Arrhenius expression was due to the fact that the Weymann equation, on the other hand, takes into account the temperature dependencies of both the activation energy and the pre-exponential 

436 

term. While the current approach is also based on the non-constant activation energy, it attempts to analyze the variation, find a function that is more sensitive to associations in the liquid, and relate it to the liquidus temperature. Hence, the Weymann expression was not used in the present analysis.

This would mean that the first derivative, when plotted against temperature, should show a corresponding change. Consequently, the second derivative should start from zero at temperatures sufficiently higher than the liquidus temperature, but deviate from the zero line around the critical temperature. It is difficult to predict the nature of the function beyond this point for real systems from the measured viscosity data, as the liquid may exhibit non-Newtonian behavior. 

It is significant to point out that the present method is based on the relationship between interionic associations and their consequential effects on slag viscosities, which was shown by Seetharaman et al [7]. In principle, any property that reflects the interionic interactions and the structural evolution, cluster behavior at different temperature intervals should show the same characteristic. If agglomeration or atomic rearrangement is manifested in the viscosities of slags, other physical properties like electrical conductivity should reflect this phenomenon as well. 

###### Estimated the liquidus temperatures of pure water and binary alloy 

In order to verify the aforementioned reasoning, it is necessary to test the hypothesis with reliable viscosity data as a function of temperature, which extends to below the freezing point. Seetharam

an et al. [7] has shown that the second derivative of the activation energy for water with respect to temperature shows a break around the liquidus temperature. This was also attempted in the case of water, where reliable viscosity values [13] are available from the ambient temperature to that of super-cooled liquid. The viscosities and the second-derivative activation energies of pure water as a function of temperature are presented in Figure 1. The results show that the second derivative exhibits a break at 273K around the freezing point, which is the liquidus temperature. It should be noticed that the values correspond to single-phase homogeneous liquid even below 273 K. This clearly shows that the nonrandom thermal agitation in the pre-solidification melt has led to the liquid to produce the solid phase at this point. The phenomenon may even be extended to the case of a liquid solution from which a dissolved phase is separating, as a solution of salt in water. This analogy can further be extended to slags, from which a solid phase would precipitate out at sub-liquidus temperatures if held indefinitely at this temperature. The potential of this method for estimating the liquidus temperature from activation energy for viscous flow was demonstrated. To illustrate this point in the case of more-complex systems, it is necessary to analyze the 437 experimental raw data from viscosity measurements. The viscosities of Pb38.iSn6i.9 and Pb44.8Bi55.2 binary alloy (all in wt %) were chosen [4]. And the second-derivative exercises were attempted. ###### **Conclusions** 

The second derivative of the activation energy for viscous flow with respect to temperature was found to exhibit a break at the liquidus point. This article considers a simple approach that values of liquidus temperatures could be derived for slags from viscosity data. The potential of this method for estimating the liquidus temperatures of pure water and binary alloy was demonstrated. Experimental data for the viscosities of CaO-Al2C>3 based slags have demonstrated the occurrence of a discontinuity in the second-derivative function, which is in accordance with the liquidus temperature as determined by different temperature of the selected slags, which measured by the hemisphere method and DSC. The present observations indicated that it is possible to get a reasonable idea of estimate the liquidus temperatures from activation energies for viscous flow.

###### **Abstract** 

The energy is introduced directly into the volume of the honeycomb ceramic regenerator due to the complex interaction of microwaves with minerals in microwave gas heating system. A threedimensional numerical model is developed to simulate the electromagnetic field by solving Maxwell's equations using finite-difference time-domain method. Computational result is presented for the microwave power absorption of the regenerator. Effects of the dielectric constant and the effective loss factor on the microwave power absorption in the regenerator are studied as well. Numerical results show that the heating pattern strongly depends on the dielectric property of the regenerator. The demonstration of the model of electromagnetic field distribution can be applied effectively and efficiently to optimize the fundamental parameters in the microwave heating processing. 

###### **Introduction** 

In recent years, microwave energy has been utilized in many fields, such as food processing, chemical engineering and mineral processing [1]. In contrast to conventional heating, where heat is transferred from a surface to the interior, microwave energy is introduced directly into the volume of minerals due to the complex interaction of the microwave with the mineral. Based on volumetric heating effects, microwave heating has several advantages such as pollution free, rapid heating technique, internal heating, high efficiency over conventional heating [1-4]. 

In order to understand and optimize the process of microwave heating, several numerical studies on modeling microwave heating have been reported. [2-17]. Two different approaches were followed to predict the power absorption applying Lambert's law and solving Maxwell's equations, respectively [14, 15]. Maxwell's equations provide the accurate solution for microwave propagation within materials, whereas Lambert's law provides a good approximation [14, 16], and Lambert's law is valid only for large sample dimensions and high loss dielectric of 

443 

materials [5, 17]. In the present study, Maxwell's equations were solved to predict the distribution of electromagnetic fields. 

This study reports a 3D simulation of the electromagnetic field inside a microwave hightemperature reactor in order to understand the influence of the dielectric constant and the effective loss factor on heating patterns.

The ore samples previously subjected to drying, calcination and prereduction stages were smelted in alumina crucibles in a horizontal tube furnace under argon atmosphere. For the smelting system used in the present work, 1550 °C and 40 minutes were determined to be the optimum smelting temperature and time, respectively. 25% excess coal addition in prereduction stage was reported to be crucial to obtain the desired Ni content in the final product. Colemanite in calcined form has long been known as a flux used in pyrometallurgical systems such as steelmaking and copper matte-smelting. To investigate the effects of calcined colemanite addition on the ferronickel metal-slag system, calcined colemanite of 2% and 4% of the total metal and slag weight was charged as a flux and smelted under the optimum conditions described above. 

###### **Introduction** 

Nickel and its alloys are important to enhance certain material properties like strength, corrosion resistance, ductility, thermal and electrical conductivity. The leading sector of nickel use is fenonickel production for stainless steel industry. It is also used in the production of low alloy steels and nonferrous alloys as well as in casting and coating industries. 

There are considerable amount of nickel ore reserves present in Gordes and Caldag regions of Turkey. Various pyrometallurgical/hydrometallurgical studies have been conducted for nickel extraction using these limonite and nontronite type ores [1-7]. In addition to these, considerable amount of nickel ore reserves was found in Sivrihisar region, Central Anatolia, in the first decade of the millennium. The mining activities have been continued in this region since then. The calcination, prereduction and smelting behavior of Sivrihisar latйrites (1.26% Ni) have been examined in recent laboratory-scale studies [8-10]. 

In the current work, fenonickel smelting experiments were conducted using Sivrihisar latйrites to investigate the effects of temperature, time and excess coal addition in prereduction stage on metal nickel content. Moreover, in an effort to examine the effects of calcined colemanite addition on the fenonickel metal-slag system, calcined colemanite of 2% and 4% of the total metal and slag weight was charged as a flux and smelted under the optimum conditions obtained in this study.

Smelting experiments were conducted using laboratory-scale horizontal tube furnace under argon atmosphere. In each run, alumina crucible having dimensions of 25 mm x 32 mm x 60 mm was used. Prereduced calcine and MgO were thoroughly mixed and placed into alumina crucible and the system was heated to experiment temperature and waited at that temperature for a predetermined time. Then, the system was cooled to room temperature with the cooling program of the furnace. All these operations were conducted under argon atmosphere such that average Ar gas flowrate of 10 cc/min was satisfied. The experiments were performed at 1500, 1550 and 1600°C. At the end of the experiments, the crucibles were broken and the solidified metal and slag particles were collected. The slag particles were ground with disc grinder and the particle size was lowered to -74 microns. Both the metal and the slag were analyzed under scanning electron microscope and their chemical compositions were obtained with EDS. The detailed and more accurate chemical analyses were conducted in the laboratories of Eregli and Steel Works Co. (ERDEMIR). Chemical analysis of the metal was performed with ICP method while that of the slag was obtained using XRF machine. ###### **Results and Discussion** ###### Effect of Temperature Effect of temperature was examined with the experiments conducted at 1500, 1550 and 1600 °C. In those experiments, the charges prereduced with 50% excess coal were smelted. MgO was added to the smelting charge such that (MgO/Total charge) weight ratio was adjusted as 0.20. This ratio was determined using FeO-MgO-Si02 phase diagram with the electric arc furnace slag compositions of Greek and Macedonian ores, which have similar characteristics with Sivrihisar latentes [11]. In the smelting experiments, no coal addition was made. The smelting period at the predetermined temperature was 40 minutes. The variation of Ni content with temperature is given in Figure 1. The nickel composition of the metal was reported as 8.95% at the experiment conducted at 1500 °C. This value was found as 9.66% and 10.12% at the runs performed at 1550 and 1600 °C, respectively. It was found that there was a noticeable increase in metal Ni content when the temperature was increased. However, even the highest nickel composition obtained at 1600 °C 454 was reported to be less than the nickel amount to be present in the standard ferronickel alloy. In order to decrease the metal iron content in the resultant Fe-Ni alloy, it was thought that the coal used at the prereduction stage should be decreased. Therefore, the smelting experiments were repeated with the charge prereduced with 25% excess coal. The results obtained with 25% excess coal is also shown in Figure 1. 1550

It was therefore reported that it is possible to satisfy the desired nickel composition in the metal when 25% excess coal was used at the prereduction stage. On the other hand, contrary to the experiments conducted with 50% excess coal at the prereduction, an increase in the smelting temperature from 1550 to 1600 °C caused a decrease in nickel content in the resultant alloy. The experiments performed to analyze the effects of temperature showed that production of standard ferronickel from Sivrihisar latйrites is possible. It was also concluded that 1550 °C was the optimum smelting temperature for the smelting system used in the current work. ###### Effect of Excess Coal Used at the Prereduction The effect of excess coal used at the prereduction stage was partly discussed in the effect of temperature section. Although 50% excess coal used at the prereduction fulfilled the optimum results for prereduction, smelting of this prereduced calcine yielded an Fe-Ni alloy which is poor in nickel as well as the standard ferronickel alloy composition is concerned. On the contrary, 25% excess coal used at the prereduction produced acceptable nickel composition values at all temperatures used in the present study. Under the lights of these results, it was thought to analyze the effect of excess coal used at prereduction on smelting, in detail. In this extent, charge mixtures containing 37.5%, 12.5% and 0% excess coal were prepared and prereduced at the optimum conditions of prereduction. After prereduction, smelting experiments were conducted at 1550 °C for 40 minutes. Smelting charges were prepared such that (MgO/Total charge) weight ratio was again fixed as 0.20. The variation of amount of nickel in metal with the % excess coal used at the prereduction stage is given in Figure 2. The nickel amount in the metal was reported as 0.0576 g when no excess 455 coal was used at the prereduction. This quantity of nickel corresponded to a very low nickel recovery of 27.92%. The smelting experiment conducted with this charge also yielded a very small amount of metal. Other than this run, the experiments performed in the extent of this study produced metals always heavier than 0.70 g. On the other hand, at the end of this experiment only 0.17 g metal accumulated in the crucible. Although the nickel content of the beads obtained were reported as 33.88%, the nickel recovery was very poor. Therefore, it was concluded that excess coal practice must be applied at the prereduction stage to obtain acceptable nickel recoveries for the smelting system under consideration. ###### Effect of Time 

The effect of time was investigated with the experiments conducted with the charges smelted for 40, 80 and 120 minutes at 1550 °C. The experiments were performed for the batches prepared 

456 

using 50% and 25% excess coal at the prereduction, just like the ones performed for various temperatures. (MgO/Total charge) weight ratio was again adjusted as 0.20. 

The effect of smelting time on metal nickel composition is shown in Figure 3. The smelting experiments conducted with the charge prereduced with 50% excess coal showed that metal nickel content increased significantly with an increase in smelting period. At the end of 40 minutes, the metal nickel composition was reported as 9.66%, while it was found as 10.03% when the smelting period was doubled. The metal nickel content reached to 13.67% when the charge was allowed to be smelted for 120 minutes. The experiment performed with the charge prereduced with 25% excess coal produced a metal containing 19.77% Ni at the end of 40 minutes smelting. It was found that the metal nickel composition decreased to 17.33% when the smelting period was extended to 80 minutes. A further increase in smelting time did not produce a significant change in the metal nickel content, which was reported as 17.32% at the end of 120 minutes smelting. Therefore, it was concluded that a smelting period of 40 minutes was sufficient for the setup used in the current work. It was also reported that the amount of nickel in the metal and the corresponding nickel recovery values was badly affected when the smelting time extended. At a glance, these findi

ngs are not in accord with the expectations but they were most probably related to smelting system used in the course of this study. In this extent, it was observed that the extent of interactions of metal-slag system with the alumina crucible increased with an increase in smelting time. This changed the smelting conditions and might cause such unexpected results. These observations were confirmed with the changes in slag AI2O3 compositions (Figure 4). For both batches, slag alumina compositions were found to increase significantly with the increase in smelting period. This increase was more pronounced and earlier in the ones smelted with the charges prereduced with 25% excess coal: The slag alumina content was reported as 24.90% at the end of 40 minutes smelting, while it was noted as 38.90% when the time was doubled. Use of calcined colemanite in steelmaking converters was found to be beneficial to enhance slag fluidity so it can be used instead of fluorite as long as extreme care should be taken not to allow significant slag carry-over during tapping. Otherwise, boron in the form of B2O3 in the slag reports to the steel and the dissolved boron content of the steel may reach several hundred ppm levels. That much of boron is far above the allowable boron content in many steels and cause cracks especially in continuous casting of slabs. More recently, possibility of use of calcined colemanite in copper mattesmelting was investigated [13]. In that study, it was found that use of calcined colemanite was beneficial to enhance slag fluidity and to decrease mechanical (entrapped) copper losses to the slag. In order to investigate the effect of calcined colemanite addition on ferronickel smelting, three preliminary experiments were conducted in the scope of this study. Smelting of charges prereduced with 25% excess coal at the prereduction resulted in iron-nickel alloys, which satisfy the minimum nickel content of the standard ferronickel at all temperatures used in the scope of this study. Therefore, it was concluded that production of crude ferronickel from Sivrihisar latйrites is possible. 1550 °C was determined as the optimum temperature for smelting. An extension in experiment period beyond 40 minutes was reported to yield unsatisfactory results. The preliminary runs investigating the effect of calcined colemanite addition showed that the extent of reduction of iron increased with the use of calcined colemanite. This caused a decrease in the metal nickel composition and a corresponding increase in metal weight was observed. 459 Studies on calcined colemanite addition are currently continued and will hopefully be discussed in a future work, in detail. ###### **Acknowledgements** The authors would like to thank The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TUBITAK) for the financial support given under the Project No: 109M068 and META Nickel & Cobalt Co. for supplying the lateritic ore samples of Sivrihisar.

###### **Abstact** 

Phosphorite is the main raw material for the production of phosphorus in chemical industry. More attentions have been drawn to the phosphorite concentrate beneficiated from low-grade phosphori

te due to the decrease of high-grade phosphorite. For another, the agglomeration process is necessary for the phosphorite concentrate after beneficiation process. The mineralogy and sintering process of the phosphorite from Leshan, China were studied in this work. The result shows that the main phases in the phosphorite are fluorapatite (Ca3(P04)3F), hydroxylapatite (Ca5(P04)3(OH)), quartz (Si0 2 ) and dolomite (CaMg(C03)2). The yield of the sinter increases with increasing the carbon dosage to 7%, and then decreases when it continuously increases. Similar regularities were found for the strength and the content of P2O5 of the sinter. The best strength of the sinter as well as its P2O5 content were discovered when the carbon dosage is 7%. Fluorapatite ((Ca5(PC>4)3)F) is the main phase in the sinter while fuggerite (Ca2MgSi2C>7) is the main binder phase . 

###### **Introduction** 

Phosphorus is an important foundation industrial raw material of national defense industry, food industry and chemical industry, where it is used to produce red phosphorus, phosphonium hydroxide, phosphorus pentasulfide and phosphoric anhydride[l-2]. 

White phosphorite is mainly produced by Electric furnace at present, which need low carbonate and good hot strength of the phosphorite. However, more attentions have been drawn to the phosphorite concentrate beneficated from low grade phosphorite due to the decrease of high grade phosphorite. Furthermore, the agglomeration process is necessary for the phosphorite concentrate due to small particle and high carbonate of phosphorite concentrate. Sintering is considered to be the best method for low P content and high carbonate of phosphorite concentrate as it can increase P grade and remove carbonate of raw material [3-5]. Therefore, sintering reduce the unite costs because of reducing power consumption. Several investigations of phosphorite sinter had been performed in China. This current study employed the property of phosphorite concentrate and sintering process of phosphorite. The effect of carbon dosage on sinter process and the main binder phase of sinter were also studied [6-7].

###### COMPREHENSIVE EFFECT OF COKE BREEZE AND LIMESTONE PARTICLE SIZE ON SINTER PERFORMANCE IN SINTERING OF A COARSE HEMATITE IRON ORE 

Zhe Wang<sup>1</sup> , Jianliang Zhang<sup>1</sup> , Xiangdong Xing<sup>1</sup> , Shan Ren<sup>1</sup> , Bing Gao<sup>1</sup> , Xueqi Zhang<sup>2</sup> School of Metallurgical and Ecological Engineering, University of Science and Technology Beijing, 100083, Beijing, China 

2Tianjin Iron and Steel Group Co., Ltd., 300301, Tianjin, China 

Keywords: Sinter, Coke breeze and limestone particle size, Productivity, Microstructure, 

RDI 

###### **Abstract** 

In sintering, the flame front speed (bed permeability) and sinter qualities are greatly depended on the feed size, especially coke breeze and limestone particle size. It is well known that coke breeze provides sinter bed with heat to meet the demand of partial fusion and diffusion bonding while limestone reacts with iron ore to generate bonding phase in the sintering process. Accordingly, it is necessary to find the optimum combination of different particle size of coke breeze and limestone to yield sinter associated with better qualities. In this study, sinter was produced in the sinter pot with varying coke breeze and limestone particle size together in sintering of a coarse hematite iron ore. The sintering productivity was measured and all of the result sinters were examined by microstructure analysis and reduction degradation test (RDI test). For the sintering of a coarse hematite iron ore, it was found that the optimum mean particle size combination of coke breeze and limestone was 1.71mm and 1.55mm in the sinter mix. On such a circumstance, sintering productivity was higher and the properties of sinter were better. 

###### **Introduction** 

Nowadays, as the main iron bearing burden material of modern blast furnaces, sinter has a great influence on the blast furnace operation. Sintering is a greatly complex process involving various chemical reactions to form kinds of mineral phases [1, 2]. In the sintering process, coke breeze is used for fuel and it generates heat to raise the green bed temperature. Limestone serves as flux and it reacts with iron ore to produce various mineral phases. On one hand, during the sintering process, the particle size of coke breeze can have an effect on temperature, atmosphere, the flame front speed and all of them act on the microstructure and mineral constitutions of sinter [3, 4]. On the other hand, different particle size of limestone has the different ability to the formation

of different calcium ferrite initiating from the decomposition of limestone. Accordingly, the particle size of coke breeze and limestone has an important role to effect the bed permeability and then to have an influence on sinter properties. 

469 

Therefore, it takes many researchers lots of efforts to understand how the particle size of coke breeze and limestone has an influence on the quality of sinter by varying the particle size. C. S. Teo found that coke breeze with different particle size was in a different position of the granulation, although researcher gave the different definition of nucleus and adhering layer fines [5, 6].The coarser coke breeze had little adhering fines which compose of iron and ore. The coarser decreased combustion efficiency. The finer coke breeze embedded into the adhering fines layer and the intermediate coke breeze was attached to the surface of the granule [7]. Umadevi et al. observed that as the proportion of coke breeze below 3 mm in the sinter mix increased from 53.0 to 90.0%, the calcium ferrite phase which had better strength and reducibility increased in the sinter, as well as the physical and metallurgical properties of sinter [8]. He also found that compared to sinter with larger or finer limestone mean particle size, sinter with limestone mean particle size of 1.52 to 1.25 mm had better sinter strength and lower RDI. Ichiro et al. reported that as the size of limestone particle size increased the decomposition of limestone was delayed, yet the permeability of the sinter bed increased and the heat pattern sharpened leading to better productivity and sinter qualities [9]. 

The aim of this paper is to find the appropriate combination of the particle size of coke breeze and limestone to promote the qualities of sinter and correlate the effect of coke breeze particle size or limestone particle size on sinter qualities. Therefore, there are considerable benefits in understanding the multifactor of the particle size which causes the quality of sinter to change.

Coke breeze and limestone particle size has an effect on the temperature and atmosphere profile through the sinter bed. Coarser coke breeze and limestone result in high permeability and relatively low temperature and stronger oxidizing atmosphere, and then limits the reaction between iron ore and flux to form calcium ferrite. Sinter with the coarse coke breeze and limestone particle size produces larger pore and gives a high performance of sintering productivity due to good permeability of the sinter bed. (2)Sinter with intermediate coke breeze and coarser limestone has the better mineral composition compared to sinter with other particle size combination of coke breeze and limestone. 1.71 mm 475 coke breeze and 1.55 mm limestone render a higher proportion of calcium ferrite and a lower proportion of magnetite and silicate melt. ###### **Abstract** 

The differences of raw material characteristic among six kind of iron concentrates and the influences on ballability were studied from the aspect of the size distribution, specific surface area and particles morphology. The results show that the specific surface area of iron concentrates has crucial influence on ballability, and the effective method of improving ballability for weak ballability iron concentrate has been found. It is of important guidance for Chinese steel mills to import and use iron concentrate from the whole world. 

###### **Introduction** 

China's steel industry has developed rapidly in recent years, crude steel production in 2011 is an unprecedented 683 million tons, which is almost half of the world crude steel production, and it is equivalent to the total sum production of the nations which rank at 2,3,4,5 and 6 in the world [1]. In order to match the development of steel industry, the blast furnaces are becoming larger and more modernization, therefore charging burden of higher quality is requested, and the reasonable blast furnace burden structure is more and more important, at the same time, for iron ore powder sintering process's continuous improvement and development, another method providing "concentrate" for blast furnace-pelletizing is also taken seriously. The grate-kiln method of pelletizing has achieved great development for its unique advantage, and in just a few years, there are over 60 rotary kiln production lines have built or being built in China, the sum of pellets has reached to more than 140 million

[2, 3]. The rapidly growth of pelletizing yield demands diverse source of pellet, which include not only domestic magnetite concentrate, but also imported hematite which is high in iron and low in silicon. Usually the ratio of imported hematite concentrate increased gradually. The imported hematite concentrate has high grade and fine particle size (the content of-0.074 mm mostly higher than 90%), but the ballability of part of the concentrates is poor. The ballability, roasting characteristic at high temperature and pellet metallurgical properties of different iron concentrates is vary greatly since the differences of raw material characteristic such as the size distribution, the surface properties and structure of particle, and the differences even influence the pelletization and operation of blast furnace [4]. ###### **Conclusions** 

(1) The imported hematite concentrate has high grade and fine particle size (the content of -0.074 mm mostly higher than 90%), but the ballability of part of the concentrates is poor, it's hard to meet the requirement to assess the ballability only by size distribution. 

483 

(2) Different iron ore concentrates have different properties. For different kind of iron ore concentrates, the specific surface area is not really high although it has fine size distribution. The specific surface area can better reflect the ballability of pellet feed compared with the size distribution, and the higher the specific surface area, the better ballability and the higher drop strength of green balls. 

(3) Simply grinding by ball mill to levigate the iron ore concentrate, the specific surface area doesn't increase significantly though the content of fine particles increase obviously. If the iron ore concentrates is pretreated by high-pressure roll mill, it can get higher specific surface area although the increased content of fine particle(-0.043 mm) is lower than that grounded by ball mill. Therefore the specific surface area is an important aspect in determining the strength of green balls, meanwhile, the high-pressure roll mill is an important and effective measure to achieve high specific surface area and improve the ballability of concentrates.

###### STUDY ON IMPROVING THE STRENGTH OF COPPER CONCENTRATE PELLETS BY ADDING BINDERS 

Xiaohui Fan , Shan He , Lin Zhang , Yanbin Tang , Xuling Chen ,Min Gan , Guohua Bai

Key words: Copper concentrate, Binder, Green pellets, Strength 

###### **Abstract** 

For reducing the dust content in flue gas during copper smelting in the Ausmelt, technologies and mechanism of strengthening the pelletizing of copper concentrate were studied. The results show that adding bentonite, organic binder or composite binder can effectively enhance the strength of green pellet and reduce the rate of shedding powder in drying process, and composite binder works best. When adding 1% of composite binder, the drop strength of green pellet increased from 1.9 times/P to 4.5 times/P , the rate of damage dropping from 2 m reduced from 50.12% to 13.08% and the rate of shedding powder reduced from 60.28% to 25.13% at drying temperature of 400EL In addition, the mechanism of binder absorbed in the surface of mineral was investigated by infrared spectroscopy. The results showed that composite binder absorbed in the surface of copper conc

entrate was in the form of chemisorptions, which made hydrophilic enhanced, while bentonite absorbed in the surface of copper concentrate was physisorption. 

###### **Introduction** 

With the technologies of copper smelting developing, the equipment of copper smelting steps into a large-scale and efficient level in recent years. As Ausmelt smelting is characterized by being efficient, environmentally-friendly and energy-saving, it is generally recognized by the enterprises of copper smelting [1]. The process of Ausmelt smelting starts with materials mixing, and then pelletizing. From this point onwards, pelletized balls are charged to the top of the furnace, undergoing drying and smelting reaction[2]. Since copper concentrate is fine-grained, directly adding into smelting furnace can make it blown out of the furnace together with the airflow upwards, rendering flue gas high in flue dust, which can cause the loss of concentrate greatly, and make smelting environment poor as well. The concentrate transported into the furnace and smelted after disc balling is conducive to improve the capacity of melting furnace during copper concentrate smelting, reduce the powder shedding rate and improve enterprise benefits. 

Copper concentrate is produced through flotation, so that the surface of concentrate contains numerous flotation agents, such as xanthate, aerofloat, thionocarbamate etc., which made concentrate strong hydrophobicity[3]. Apart from that, mixed with copper-bearing dust, collected from smelting process and other lump impurities, copper concentrate is poor ballability. Besides, green balls pelletized by a disc have several numbers of falling during transportation, and the

With the green pellets moisture increasing, the drop strength of green pellets experienced an upward trend and the rate of 2 m damage dropping showed a downward trend. The main reason was that the main force of liquid adhesive between particles in green pellets was capillary force that generated by water, which got enhanced due to capillary extrusion shrinkage under the mechanical action of pellet nucleus; that the excess water became gravity water when the pores between the particles felt water, green pellets easily deformed during pressing each other. The optimum green pellets moisture was around 9.94%, the drop strength of single copper concentrate was 1.9 times/P, the rate of 2 m damage dropping was 50.12%, and the bursting temperature was 370E. The relationship between temperature and drying of green pellet was in Figure 3 when maintaining wind speed at 1.4 m/s for 2 min. With the drying temperature increasing, the rate of green pellets dehydration got a rise. The pellets were completely dried when temperature raised to 350 E. The rate of green pellets shedding powder increased as the drying temperature rose. Especially when the green pellets completely dried, the rate of shedding powder significantly increased. The rate of green pellets shedding powder suddenly increased and offing powder more serious when the drying temperature was up to 350-400 E. The main reasons were that the sulfur minerals of copper concentrate presented in the form of sulfide, temperature of sulfide thermal decomposition was 300-500 El [4]. 487 Moisture content/% Drying temperature/°C

During transportation and drop process the green pellets seriously damaged, and the rate of heat shedding powder was serious, leading to considerable flue dust in airflow, which was difficult to meet the production requirement. ###### Strength of Copper Concentrate Pellets by Adding Single Binder The effect of adding inorganic binder bentonite on the strength of copper concentrate green pellets is shown in Figure 4. It can be seen from the table that as the dosage of bentonite added increased, the drop strength of green pellets experienced an upward trend and the rate of 2 m damage dropping was decline. When the dosage of bentonite was 2% and the moisture of green pellets was 11.70%, the drop strength of green pellets reached 5.9 times/P and the rate of 2 m damage dropping was 20.37%. The reasons that bentonite improving the strength of green pellets were

that bentonite added improved the size composition of materials, narrowing the capillary diameter of green pellets inside, so as to increase capillary force and plasticity; that after absorbing water, bentonite became colloidal particles and filled in the gaps between particles of green pellets, which increased the adhesive force between particles of green pellets, the strength of green pellets therefore improved. But the main ingredient of bentonite was montmorillonite, which was the clay mineral of aluminum silicate. Consequently, extra gangue would be brought into if a large quantity of bentonite was added as binder, then the copper grade of concentrate charged into furnace became lower. Besides, bentonite contained large amounts of impurities e.g. AI, Mg, which would change the characters of slag, and reduce the life of the Ausmelt melting furnace [5-6]. 

The effect of adding organic binder on the strength of copper concentrate green pellets is given in Figure 5, where can be seen that as the dosage of organic binder adding increased, the suitable moisture of green pellets was significantly increasing, the drop strength of green pellets ascended, and the rate of 2 m damage dropping declined obviously. When the dosage of organic binder was 0.1% and the moisture of green pellets was 13.85%, the drop strength of green pellets reached 6.5 times _IV,_ the rate of 2 m damage dropping was 22.75%. Since the organic binder was polymer of macromolecule, which had strong ability to absorb water, and its viscosity could increase when encountered with water, thereby enhancing the adhesive force between the

The strength of green pellets improved markedly by adding organic binder, the organic binder could completely decompose at high temperature, which had little influence on the grade of copper concentrate. Nonetheless, the dosage of organic binder was less, so that mixing effect and the accuracy of binder adding were of great importance. In addition to that, high green pellet moisture would consume more energy during drying and smelting process.

###### **Conclusions** 

(1) Produced through flotation, copper concentrate's surface hydrophilicity as well as ballability was poor, and its rate of heat shedding powder was high. Pelletizing alone, the drop strength of green pellets reached 1.9 times/P, the rate of 2 m damage dropping was 50.12% and at 40013 the rate of heat shedding powder was 60.28%. 

(2) Adding bentonite, organic binder or composite binder improved the strength of green pellet of copper concentrate significantly. The drop strength of green pellets reached 5.9 times/P, 6.5 times/P and 4.5 times/P, respectively, the rate of 2 m damage dropping was 50.12%, 22.75% and 13.08%, respectively and at 400 El the rate of heat shedding powder was 60.28%,30.61% and 25.13%, respectively. Considering smelting energy consumption and slag, adding composite binder was recommended. 

(3) The detecting results of infrared spectroscopy revealed that absorbed in the surface of copper concentrate in the form of chemisorptions, which made hydrophilic enhanced and pellets pelletizing improved, while bentonite absorpted in the surface of copper concentrate was physi sorption.

###### SINTERING PROCESS OF CHROMITE CONCENTRATE

Pan Chen, Donghai Li, Cheng Pan, Mei Liu, Xuewei Lv 

(College of materials Science and Engineering, Chongqing University, Chongqing, 400044) Keywords: Chromite, Concentrate, Sinter 

###### **Abstract** 

Chromite concentrate after beneficiation can not be directly used in the electric furnace. Therefore sintering is one of the effective way to agglomeration, by which the chromite concentrate can be utilized and the power cost of ferrochrome smelting can be reduced. The properties of raw materials and the sintering process of chromite concentrate were studied in this work. The results showed that chromite concentrate used can hardly granulated alone, while chlorite addition can improve the effect of granulation. Moisture plays an important role in sintering process. The granulation effect is optimal when the amount of water addition is 12%. Strength and abrasion index are the evaluation indexes of sinter quality. It was found that the strength of sinter increased with coke dosage increasing to 12%, and then decreased when it continuously increased. Opposite regularities were found for the abrasion index of the sinter. 

###### **1 Introduction** 

Chromium is a very important metal element which is mostly used in the production of stainless steel. In the earth, it is always formed compound with iron as ferrochromium spinel (FeO.C^Os), and its mineralogical name is chromite. [1] Currently, the global production of chrome ore is about 20 million tonnage every year , in which fine ore (less than 8 mm) accounted for about 80% [2] Although the price of the fine ore is cheaper than the lump one, too much fines will lead to the poor permeability and causes increased electricity consumption while producing ferrochrome. Therefore, the agglomeration process of chrome ore is one of the effective measures to increase the usage ratio of fine ore. 

Generally, the agglomeration process in the industrial used can be classified as the sintering, pelletizing and briqutting. [3] The sinters have good strength, uniform size, as well as the good thermal stability and reductivty due to its porous structure . According to the reports, the usage of sinter can reduce the energy consumption during the smelting process.[4] However ,the sintering of chromites is more difficult than the of iron ore. That is because (1) the liquid phase is hard to form during the heating process of the chromite, (2) the granulation ability of the raw materials is low due to the poor wettability of chromite by water and the smooth surface of the particles. Therefore, in this paper, many methods were used to optimize the granulation and sintering process.

Lishun Yuan<sup>1</sup> , Xiaohui Fan, Min Gan, Guiming Yang, Xiaoxian Huang, Zhiyun Ji, Zhiyuan Yu 

School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan, 410083, P.R.China. 

Keywords: Magnesium pellets, Roast, Ionic diffusion, Strength, Crystal grain 

###### **Abstract** 

The roasting characteristics of hematite pellets containing MgO were studied where magnesia powder, serpentine and magnesite were used as magnesium-additives respectively. The mechanical strength of both preheated and roasted pellets decreased when MgO content increased, which implied the addition of MgO had an adverse effect on pellet consolidation. By adding flux containing CaO, the mechanical strength of both preheated and roasted pellets were improved. The addition of calcium flux facilitated the formation of calcium ferrite and provided a certain amount of liquid phase, resulting in faster diffusion of Mg<sup>2+</sup> and Fe<sup>3+</sup> . The result showed that diffusing speed of Mg<sup>2+</sup> was enhanced by 1.48 times, and rate constant of Fe 20 3 crystalline growth was enhanced by 62% when basicity was around 0.4. Improvement of mineralization degree and recrystallization of Fe 20 3 assisted in consolidation of hematite pellets containing MgO. 

###### **Introduction** 

Oxidized pellets are ideal iron-bearing burdens in blast furnace. At present, magnetite is the main raw material for oxidized pellet production in China. However, as the rapid development of iron and steel industry, resources of magnetite have been depleted and cannot satisfy the requirement of pellet production. Using hematite concentrates to produce oxidized pellets has become a trend [1, 2]. Many pellet enterprises abroad nowadays have adopted high proportions of hematite concentrates when producing oxidized pellets, e.g. the percentage is 100% in a lot of Brazilian factories [3, 4]. But high proportion of hematite concentrates will lead to low mechanical strength and high reduction swelling index of pellets. Some studies show that Mg-bearing pellets have excellent metallurgical properties, and the reduction swelling phenomenon can be solved by adding fluxes containing MgO [5, 7]. However, there are problems such as low pellet strength and bad roasting characteristics for Mg

O-bearing pellets, which remains an obstacle in pellet industry. Hence, it's vital to undertake the study on strengthening measures for indurations of Mg-bearing hematite pellets. From Figure 5, Figure 6 and Figure7, Calcium flux can improve the mechanical strength of Mg-bearing hematite pellets by accelerating the diffusion of Mg<sup>2+</sup> and facilitating the growth of hematite crystal particles. Calcium fluxes result in the formation of low melting point minerals which exist in liquid phase. The more liquid phase, the faster Mg<sup>2+</sup> and Fe<sup>3+</sup> can diffuse. Mineralization of Mg-bearing materials and the growth of hematite crystal particles lead to an increase of mechanical strength of pellets. 

###### **Conclusions** 

(1) When adding serpentine, magnesia powder or magnesite as Mg-bearing fluxes into the hematite pellets, the strength of both preheated and roasted pellets decreased as the MgO content increased. 

(2) Adding limestone into Mg-bearing hematite pellets, as the basicity increased, the strength of both preheated and roasted pellets increased at first then decreased, reaching maximum values at basicity around 0.4-0.5. Certain amount of limestone can improve the strength of Mg-bearing hematite pellets. 

(3) Ca-bearing fluxes helps to produce certain liquid phase, assisting in the diffusion of Mg<sup>2+</sup> and Fe<sup>3+</sup> . Mineralization of Mg-bearing materials and the growth of hematite crystal particles lead to an increase of mechanical strength of pellets.

###### STUDY ON THE IMPROVEMENTS OF REDUCTION SWELLABILITY 

###### AND LOW TEMPERATURE REDUCTION DISINTEGRATION OF 

###### VANADIUM-TITANIUM MAGNETITE OXIDIZED PELLETS 

Yufeng Guo , Jianfeng Zhou , Tao Jiang , Feng Chen , Xiaolei Song , Minjun Tang , Linjiang Qing 

School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan 410083, P.R.China 

Key Words: Vanadium-Titanium Magnetite, Reduction Swellability, Low Temperature Reduction Disintegration, Oxidized Pellets 

###### **Abstract** 

Reduction swellability index (RSI) and low temperature reduction disintegration index (RDI) of vanadium-titanium magnetite oxidized pellets are harmful to the processing of ironmaking, for example, causing serious gas permeability, decreased yield, higher coke ratio and more furnace dust. Thus, the improvements of RSI and RDI of vanadium-titanium magnetite oxidized pellets were investigated in this paper, including the pretreatment of raw material, additives of dolomite or boric acid, pellets treated in chloride solution and so on. The results showed that damp milling as pretreatment and boric acid added in pelletizing were conducive to the RSI which decreased 5% and 7% respectively, while they were not efficient enough in improving RDI. Dolomite was efficient in improving RSI, but had negative effect on RDI. There was no evidence to show that RSI and RDI would be improved when pellets were treated in chloride solution. Pursuing this further, the mechanism of those improvements were investigated. 

###### **Introduction** 

In the world, vanadium-titanium magnetite utilization is investigated around how to recover iron, titanium, vanadium, and divided into blast-furnace method and non-blast-furnace method according to respective characteristics. Blast furnace method [1,2] can recover iron and vanadium effectively, but TiC>2 cannot be recycled. Non-blast-furnace methods include rotary kiln-electric furnace method, pre-reduction electric furnace method, reductiongrinding method and sodium vanadium-rotary kiln-electric furnace method and so on. [3-7]Comparing to the Non-blast-furnace method, the method of blast furnace smelting has been put into industrial applications. And it has the following advantages: First of all, effective recycling iron and vanadium; Second, technical problems of high titanium slag in blast furnace smelting; Third, it has mature technology in blast furnace smelting.

In blast furnace smelting procession, the situation is extremely serious that pellets are disintegrated in low temperature (400°-600°) during

reduction period. The results showed that RDI of vanadium-titanium magnetite is more serious than ordinary iron ore. Serious disintegration leads to a series of problems, for example, causing serious gas permeability, decreased yield, higher coke ratio and more furnace dust, thus the enterprise benefit drops. So how to solve RDI of sinter and pellets become the key of investigation for years. There were fewer researches on RSI and RDI of vanadium-titanium magnetite compared with other iron ore. Specific methods are as follows, (1) Pellets disintegration is dropped by decreasing hematite and increasing FeO. (2) [(l-x)Mg-FexO]0-Fe203 is formed, while MgO gets into magnetite crystal lattice by adding MgO. Thus magnetite crystal lattice can be stabilized and is efficient on decreasing RSI and RDI. (3) RDI will be decreased when pellets were treated in chloride solution. The laws of RSI and RDI are investigated by raw material grinding and pretreated of HPRG in the process of pellets, additives of dolomite and borax, pellets treated in chloride solution and so on. ###### Experimental Methods 

The main experimental procedures are described as follows. Firstly Raw materials used by pelletizing which went through artificial ingredients and each of them included 5kg , additive of blinder according to certain proportion, and adding a certain amount of moisture when mixing. Then, pelletizing was carried out by the pretreatment of high pressure roller grinding (HPRG) or damp milling, additives of dolomite or boric acid, pelletizer rate 24r/min and pelletizing time 12min. The reduction disintegration function of pellets was measured according to GB/T 13242-91 National Standard Test Method. The samples in a range of particle size (10-12.5mm) were carried out static reduction under 500° in fixed bed. After temperature reduction 120min, the samples were cooled, loaded into drum (€) 130x200mm) under the condition of time 10min and rotation rate 30r/min, and rated b

###### MIX AND ITS BASIC RESEARCH 

Yong-bin Yang, Qi-bing Tan, Qian Li, Kai Li, Yuan-yuan Zhu, Dong-ye Li, Qiang Xie, Chao Li
