Keywords: sintering mix, permeability, on-line test, gas seepage 

###### **Abstract** 

The permeability of sintering mix is a vital technological property in sintering process. However, it can only be measured by off-li

ne method on samples picked from the production. In order to acquire the properties of sintering mix accurately, on-line measuring of permeability is urgently required. Based on the reflection characteristics of bed permeability on pipe flowing parameters, a new method is presented in this paper for on-line measuring of sintering mix permeability. The measurement can be performed by blowing gas flow in the bed with the measuring pipe. Measuring results are obtained by picking the data on flowing rate and pressure in the pipe. The function of flowing rate to pressure may be certain for samples with the same permeability. Thus, the permeability was determined by contrasting this function to the result of off-line measuring, and the relative coefficient or R<sup>2</sup> value was more than 99%. 

###### **Introduction** 

The permeability of sintering mix is a vital technological property in sintering process, which directly determines production and quality of sinter, or even determines '<sup>31</sup> whether the sinter production is carried out smoothly<sup>[1</sup> . 

The permeability have more obvious influence on vertical sintering speed,which is mainly related to air quantity passing through material bed. Under certain inducing capacity and negative pressure, the vertical sintering speed mainly depends on the permeability of sintering mix. Low permeability may make burning through point of sintering move back, and the sinter mix cannot be burnt through. High permeability may make burning through point of sintering move forward, improving production efficiency by increasing the speed of sintering machine<sup>[41</sup> . Good permeability means a small resistance of fan .reduction of negative pressure of sintering machine, and full contact between air and sulfide, which can strengthen physical-chemical reaction during sintering process and increase desulphurization rate. In gas well through material layer process, gas-solid desulfurization reaction and gas-solid-liquid heat exchange are completed and hot gas through the combustion zone supplies the 

517 

sintering process with heat. Finally uniform sintering of the material layer in height and width direction is achieved<sup>[51</sup> . While high permeability index leads to weak sinter strength, fast sintering speed, short residence time of high temperature region and little liquid phase. Moreover, liquid phase in the fast cooling process is too late to fully crystallize but forming glass phase which is harmful to sinter strength as well. Bad permeability means a big fan resistance and increase of negative pressure of sintering machine, which make the air pass through material layer difficultly. When air and mix contact difficultly, removal of sulfide reduces so that desulfurization is incomplete. Meanwhile, low caking efficiency, slow sintering speed and easily burnt sinter , reduce sinter output. Therefore appropriate permeability of sintering mix is the premise of stable burning through p

oint and satisfactory sinter output and quality. Presently, off-line measuring method is taken to measure sintering mix permeability at home and abroad, which does not enable real-time monitoring of permeability and causes artificial error of measuring result because of difficult sampling and weak representativeness of samples. Sintering plant mainly improves sintering mix permeability by adjusting mix water content. Its disadvantage is lack of corresponding comparing reference[6 '71 . By developing a new on-line detecting permeability index method, permeability parameters can be controlled directly which has a vital significance to guide the sintering production. ###### **Experiment** Research and Development of Test Device l

###### OPTIMIZING THE SINTERING PROCESS OF LOW-GRADE FERROMANGANESE ORES 

Yuanbo Zhang, Wei Luo, Zhixiong You*, Zijian Su, Guanghui Li, Tao Jiang 

(School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan 410083, China) 

Key Words: Ferromanganese ores, Sintering, Basicity, Biomass Charcoal 

###### **Abstract** 

In this study, the appropriate sintering process parameters for low-grade ferromanganese ores were investigated. The results showed that, under the condition of natural basicity (R=0.03), the optimal parameters were obtained as follows: moisture of mixture 9.1%, coke powder 9.9% and sintering negative pressure 7 KPa. And the corresponding yield, ISO tumbling index and utilization coefficient reached at 80.18%, 61.27% and 1.515t-m" -h" , respectively. Under the optimal parameters, the emission of harmful gases, such as SO2 and NOx, were reduced evidently with 30% of coke powder replaced by biomass charcoal. Moreover, it was found that the basicity had obvious effects on the quality of the sinters when it changed between 0.03 and 2.4. The ISO tumbling index gradually decreased from 61.27% to 55.47% with the basicity increasing from 0.03 to 1.2, then, it began to increase after the basicity further increased to 2.4. 

###### **Introduction** 

Manganese is mainly consumed by steel and battery industries, particularly in the steel plants and ferroalloy units. The consumption of metal manganese in the ferroalloy industry accounts for 85%~90%

of the total Mn [1-2]. Therefore, ensuring sufficient manganese alloys is essential to meet the rapid development of steel industry. Recently, rich-manganese slag containing high grade Mn (>40%), low Fe (1%) and P (<0.03%) is considered as superior raw materials for manganese alloys. While the sinters made from manganese ores are major raw materials for producing rich-manganese slag with the increasing exhaustion of natural rich manganese lump ores [3-5]. Conventional processes producing rich-manganese slag, such as blast furnace and electric furnace smelting, require favorable air permeability for stock column. As a result, fine manganese concentrates or fine ores must be agglomerated before being used as burdens. Sintering is an efficient way to agglomerate which has a long history and acquires rapid development in recent years. Especially in China, sintering of manganese fine ores was applied in the majority of iron and steel plants. Some new sintering technologies such as thick-bed and high-basicity sintering were developed. Although solid fuel consumption was reduced from Corresponding author: Zhixiong You, e-mail: yzx445474096@126.com 527 about 300 kg/t to 120~140kg/t and the proportion of return fine was reduced from 30% to 10%~15% in the last several decades, the process of manganese ore sintering was still characterized by high energy consumption, low productivity, serious environment pollution, etc. High-basicity sinters are favorable for smelting rich-manganese slag. However, the drawbacks of pulverization were unavoidable. When the low-grade manganese ores were used as the raw materials for sintering, the problems mentioned above were more prominent. In this present, the appropriate sintering process parameters, including coke powder proportion, moisture of mixture, sintering negative pressure and basicity, were investigated. Biomass fuel was firstly used to partly replace coke powder in order to reduce coke consumption and the emission of harmful gases, such as SO2 and NOx. ###### **Experimental** ###### Materials The manganese ore used in this test is low-grade ferromanganese ore, coming from Hunan province, China. ###### USING OF SPENT FOUNDRY SANDS FOR PRODUCTION OF BURNED CERAMIC BUILDING MATERIALS: INFLUENCE FOR ENVIRONMENT 

Mariusz Holtzer<sup>1</sup> , Jцzef Dahko<sup>1</sup> , Rafal Dahko<sup>1</sup> , Sylwia Zymankowska-Kumon<sup>1</sup> 

'AGH University of Science and Technology, Faculty of Foundry Engineering, Reymonta Street 23, 30-059 Krakow, Poland 

Keywords: Foundry, Sands, Environment. 

###### **Abstract** 

Burning of ceramic materials is carried out at temperatures 900+1300°C, in dependence of the required functional properties. The Faculty of Foundry Engineering together with the Faculty of Material Engineering and Ceramics developed the technology of production of burned ceramic materials with using spent moulding and core sands. The mentioned above waste materials of the foundry industry fulfilled - in plastic masses intended for obtaining ceramic materials - the role of the addition weakening clay raw materials. The laboratory investigations were fully verified by the results of industrial tests. It should be pointed out that none negative effects were observed at the stage of mixing raw materials and preparation of plastic masses. The measurements of exhaust gases emissions performed during burning the product

s containing spent moulding sands as well as during the normal production did not exhibit any significant differences, which could have indicated the harmful impact on the natural environment. 

###### **Introduction** 

Sands are used by the foundry industry to make metal casting molds and are a mixture of silica sand, bentonite clay and carbonaceous additives or resins. During the casting process, the molten metal cause thermal decomposition of carbonaceous additives or resins, which results in the formation of potentially hazardous organics, that are emitted to the atmosphere and condense in the molding sand. Each year the U.S. foundry industry landfills about 10 million tones of sand because it is no longer suitable to make metal casting molds. A large high-silica sand content in spent foundry sands (SFSs) generates rational premises for their reuse in other than foundry practice fields. Efforts to divert the SFSs from landfills and encourage their beneficial use in manufactured soils, geotechnical applications, the construction industry (road construction, highway construction), the building materials industry (cement, bricks, limestone manufacture), in the filling of mining cavities or in landfill construction (roads on landfills, permanent covers) are make [1-7]. 

The limits of these applications are given by either technical criteria for construction materials and/or environmental criteria for given applications. Environmental criteria are generally based on leaching properties and the content of organic compounds. These differ between various world regions. SFSs generally show a low metal leaching potential. An exceedence of the limit values may occur for materials with content of organic binder or with specific additives, such as lustrous carbon. Duo to its quartz content and appropriate granulometry, used sand may be applied as a virgin sand substitute in road construction. Application in the production of building materials (concrete, bricks, tiles, glass, wool) are technically feasible but require a higher level of composition control and logistics. 

537 

A good example can be the industry of building materials, especially production technologies requiring application of large amounts of natural high-silica sands. Spent foundry sands, after the appropriate treatment process, can constitute a partial or even a total substitute of a natural highsilica sand. This process includes crushing of caked sand agglomerates, removal of metallic parts and grain segregation. However, such treatment process of spent sands does not cause a removal of leftovers of applied binding agents from sand grains surfaces [8]. Therefore high-silica raw material originated from such treatment can be applied only in those production technologies of building materials, which apply high temperatures, at which the remains of organic binders are oxidized and the formed gases disposed into the atmosphere. This oxidation process is accompanied by a certain heat emi

ssion causing lowering a fuel consumption for heating raw materials to the heat treatment temperature required in the given process. Sands after a reclamation should be considered as fully suitable for such management if only the emission level of potentially harmful gases (from burning organic binders) does not exceed the permissible values. The make-up water is the minimal amount of water which warrants obtaining the plastic mass of the required reological properties, necessary for the proper forming of semi-finished products. Weakening additions are used for an improvement of a capillary water transport in ceramic masses. High-silica sand is often such an 538 addition. It can be partially substituted by such materials as: fly-ash, furnace slag, brick flour, chamotte, and also sands and slides residues from the processes of dressing raw materials for glass and ceramic industries and of coal cleaning as well as by properly prepared spent foundry sands. These sands can contain residues of organic substances, which constitute an additional source of energy in burned ceramic products. However, as it was mentioned above, the suitability of high-silica sands obtained after the spent foundry sands reclamation, is conditioned by the lack of emission of harmful gases being the products of organic binders oxidation and by the low level of heavy metals elusion. In dependence on the type of the produced building material, the high-silica sand fulfils the role of: microaggregate, filling mater

ial, material weakening clay raw materials or substrate of chemical reactions requiring the participation of SiC>2 [9]. 

###### **Production of Burned Ceramic Building Materials** 

Burned ceramic building materials constitute a group of products, of properties obtained as a result of the heat treatment of samples shaped from the properly prepared ceramic masses. Burning of ceramic materials is carried out at temperatures 90CH-1300°C, in dependence of the required functional properties. To this group of products belong, among others, common bricks, cavity bricks and clinker bricks [10, 11]. When SFSs are applied in the production of building ceramics, the special attention should be directed towards an accurate disintegration and separation of metal parts. Organic components such as resins and also coal dust occurring in SFSs, are not an obstacle in a production of good quality bricks, in accordance with a standard, which was confirmed by the performed examinations. Weakening materials content in ceramic mass depends on a plasticity of clay raw material and increases with its increase. An optimal content of weakening additions should be determined experimentally. 

The management range of after foundry sands in production of burned ceramic building materials, depends obviously on economic and logistic conditions. However, it should be emphasized that an important element in taking a decision of the application of these wastes is the warranty of a continuous supply of reclaimed sands and their proper preparation. 

###### **Laboratory Investigations and the Discussion of Results** 

The Faculty of Foundry Engineering together with the Faculty of Material Engineering and Ceramics of the AGH-University of Science and Technology developed - within the realized the development-research project [12] - the technology of production of burned ceramic materials with using SFSs [13]. The laboratory investigations were fully verified by the results of industrial tests. The mentioned above waste materials of the foundry industry fulfilled - in plastic masses intended for obtaining ceramic materials - the role of the addition weakening clay raw materials. Thus, they constituted the substitute of traditionally applied weakening additions in a form of natural high-silica sands. The main aim of the performed investigations was the elimination of high-silica sand and substituting it by the equivalent amount of sand obtained as a result of the preliminary treatment of spent foundry sands, containing various organic binders, and in consequence obtaining ceramic materials of full value, characterized by properties adequate to the requirements concerning ceramic building materials. Effectiveness of such technological solution was determined on the grounds of the performed comparative analysis, comprising the basic functional features of two kinds of ceramic materials, it means the reference material and the experimental materials, obtained with various quantitative a

nd qualitative 539 fractions of waste foundry sands. The integral stage of estimation of the suitability of spent foundry and/or core sands as auxiliary raw materials intended for production of ceramic building materials was the analysis of a potential hazard for natural environment, related to production and exploitation of ceramic building materials obtained with their participation. The qualitative selective analysis of gases emitted into the atmosphere during burning of ceramic products as well as of heavy metals elusion which can be releasing from the ceramic matrix in the whole period of exploitation of ceramic products, was carried out. The basic raw material for obtaining ceramic materials, both reference and experimental, was the tertiary krakowiecki clay originated from the deposit Kolbuszowa-Kupno (symbol: KK), which is currently used in the Wienerbergier plant. The traditional weakening raw material in reference materials was natural high-silica sand (symbol: PK), which in cases of experimental mixtures was substituted by equivalent amounts of SFSs with furan resin (symbol: RFU) and/or spend sands from the cold-box technology (symbol: RCB). In addition, other supplementing raw materials were used, such as furnace slag from power plants (symbol: ZP) and thermal-electric power stations (symbol: ZR). As material increasing the porosity a sawdust (symbol: T) and paper pulp (symbol: PP) were applied. These raw materials were used for a preparation of several plastic masses from which individual series of ceramic materials were obtained [10]. When working out the raw materials composition of plastic masses it was assumed that they have to represent the composition applied for obtaining ceramic building materials in the mentioned above plant. Thus, these masses had the identical quantitative composition but different qualitative one. The variability of the qualitative composition of experimental masses (symbols: 1H-7) prepared under the laboratory conditions, as compared to the reference mass (symbol: 0), was achieved due to the substitution contained there weakening additions (natural high-silica sand and furnace slag), performed in turns or in a combined way, by spent foundry sands. Additionally, as a reference material, samples (symbol: KK) obtained from the raw material mass of the identical composition as the mass of the symbol 0, but originated from the current production, it means prepared in the technological line of the plant, were examined. They concerned obtaining of hollow bricks of the POROTHERM type [10]. All products were obtained at maintaining the current technological conditions in respect to the methods of formation, drying and burning, while the essential difference concerned only the mixture composition. The difference laid in the substitution of the natural high-silica sand, applied in the current production as the weakening addition, by the equivalent amount of sand obtained by previous processing of SFSs. Thus, the following aims were looked for: - obtaining acceptable external features of products; - verification whether products meet the requirements of the technical specification. In the industrial tests the mixtures of spent foundry sands (supplied directly from the foundry) containing sands with furan resin, sands from the cold-box and hot-box processes as well as sands with bentonite and coal dust were applied. Hollow bricks of the POROTHERM type, after burning, are illustrated in Figure 1. ###### **Conclusions** 

Unanimous assessment of proceeding and results of the carried out tests of products with SFSs performed by interested units was as follows: 

- The strength of products originated from tests is comparable to products from the current production. The strength of hollow bricks of the POROTHERM type, with a fraction of spent moulding sands, from the casting house WSK was 16.01+17.61 (average: 16.8) MPa, while the strength from the last production series was 13.3+17.2 (average 15.3) MPa. 

- The visible improvement of the drying process and the burning process economy as compared to the standard production occurred. The gas consumption decrease in the burning process by app. 27% (average value from 27 production hours), from app. 532 m<sup>3</sup> /h to app. 387 m<sup>3</sup> /h, was observed. 

- An external appearance of hollow bricks with a fraction of spent moulding sands does not differ from the normal production, only they are characterized by a higher compliance to over-heating in the stack middle part (black dye penetrations, blisters). 

- Number of transverse cracks on hollow brick feathers, occurring from time to time, as 1-3, is comparable with the normal production. 

- Measurements of the contamination emission indicated comparability of test samples and the current production. Admittedly an emission of some compounds was higher during tests with the SFSs application, however these values were within the allowable emission range of the foundry plant. On the other hand the NO2 and CO emission was much smaller when the SFSs addition was applied. 

- The composition of gases emitted when the SFSs addition to moulding sands for the bricks production is used will depend on the composition of these sands mixture. Therefore at introducing the technology with utilizing SFSs it is necessary to perform measurements of waste gases emission. 

- Technical parameters of new hollow bricks such as: density (net and gross) and hollowing fraction fulfill specification assumptions. 

- Assessment of external appearance - after sorting in accordance with quality class A.

###### DEVELOPMENTS OF PROCEESING TECHNOLOGIES FOR REFRACTORY GOLD ORES 

Lin Chen<sup>a</sup> ' ' , Tianzu Yang<sup>a</sup> , Weifeng Liu<sup>a</sup> , Deyu Wang a School of Metallurgical Science and Engineering, Central South University, Changsha 410083, China 

b Shandong Gold Group Co., Ltd, Jinan 250100, China 

* Corresponding author, Lei.: +86 0731 88836791, E-mail: chenlin0210@gmail.com 

###### **Key words:** Refractory gold ores, Metallurgy, Review 

###### **Abstract** 

Due to the gradual exhaustion of easily extractive gold ores, it is vital to make efficient use of refractory gold ores which hold 30% gold storage of the world. However, the disadvantage of current processing technologies for refractory gold ores consists of severe pollution, low gold extraction ratio, high investment, etc, thus great research interests were attracted during recent years. Lhis article provides an overview of the distribution and categories of the refractory gold ores in the world. Lhe state of art in processing refractory gold ores by pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy

and biometallurgy techniques and their industrial applications are highlighted. Potential environmental conservative techniques for efficient gold extraction are also reviewed. 

###### **Introduction** 

###### Resources of Refractory Gold Ores 

As easily extractive gold ores are going to be exhausted with the large scale mining nowadays, refractory gold ores are becoming more and more important. Gold in the refractory gold ore cannot be fully extracted using conventional method (cyanidation) even with fine grinding. Lhe amount of gold in the refractory gold ores is about 1500~2000t in China, which occupies 30-40% of the total gold storage [1]. Lherefore, it is vital to make efficient use of refractory gold ores. 

Refractory gold ores are widely distributed in China, but mainly in the provinces listed below: Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Guangxi, Shanxi and Hunan. Most of the gold ores in Ailao mountain, Dianguiqian and Chuanshangan districts are refractory gold ores [1]. Refractory gold ores with a large gold storage are Jinya in Guangxi (30t), Lannigou in Guizhou (52t), Zimuhan in Guizhou (26t), Yata in Guizhou (16t), Luerba in Gansu (30t) and Fengcheng in Liaoning (38t), etc. [2, 3] . 

Refractory gold ores in other part of the world mainly exist in America and Africa. Some of them are famous: Mercur, Getchell, Goldstrike, Mclaughlin in America, Sao Bento in Brazil, Progera in Papua New Guinea, Olympias in Greece [4-7]. 

###### Categories of Refractory Gold Ores 

545 

Due to the mineralogy properties like gold occurrence in the ore, symbiotic relationship, structure of the ore and impurity content, etc., the refractory gold ores are difficult to be processed because of the following reasons [8] : 

(1) Gold exists in fine particles or even incorporated in the crystal structures, which cannot be separated with fine grinding; 

(2) Gold ore contains minerals influencing cyanidation like S, As, Sb and Te et al.; 

(3) Gold ore contains minerals which absorbs gold or its complex. 

Therefore the refractory gold ores can be divided into three types [3,9]: 

The first type is refractory gold ores containing arsenic(>3%), carbon(l%~2%) and sulfur(5%~6%). When conventional cyamding is applied, the gold extraction ratio is under 50%. Further, large amount of NaCN is consumed in the process due to the existence of the impurities. Gold concentrate with high gold grade can be produced when flotation is used. However, the high impurities in the concentrate are unfavorable for gold extraction. 

The second type is the refractory gold ore containing fine gold particle which are encapsulated in gangue and other impurities. In this type of gold ores, about 20%~30% gold exist as fine particles or in the matrix of the gangue. Therefore, either cyamding or flotation shows low gold recovery. 

The third type is the refractory gold ore containing gold symbiosis with other metals like copper, antimony and tellurium etc., forming complex gold-metal compound

s that are very difficult to be dissolved. These compounds may consume cyanides and protecting alkali, or form inert membrane during gold extraction, reducing the gold extraction ratio. 

###### **Process for Refractory Gold Ores** 

Recent progress in processing technologies solved extraction problems of some refractory gold ores. For example, due to the emergence of carbon in pulp and carbon in leach technologies, the refractory gold ores containing carbon and clay can be processed by cyaniding directly. Therefore, the refractory gold ore referred nowadays usually is gold ore containing arsenic and sulfur. The formation of this kind of gold ore has intimate relationship with sulfuric minerals like pyrite, arsenic pyrite, pyrrhotite and chalcopyrite, leading to a low gold extraction ratio in cyanidation (<20%). Gold extraction requires the destruction of the minerals encapsulating the gold particles. Researches have been done to disclose the gold particles by removing sulfur and arsenic, utilizing its physical and chemical properties. These technologies can be divided into three categories: pyrometallurgy method, hydrometallurgy method and biometallurgy method. 

###### Pyrometallurgy Process 

The pyrometallurgy process for refractory gold ores mainly refers to oxidative roasting. Since As and S are volatilized in the form of AS2O3 and SO2 during the roasting, not only a porous roasted 

546 

ore is produced, but also large gold agglomerates are formed with the agglomeration of the fine gold particles. According to the different oxidation conditions required for As and S, they can be separated in the roasting by controlling the oxidative atmosphere and temperature, which is called "two stage roasting" technology. 

Oxidative roasting is the most widely applied method for sulfuric encapsulating gold ores. This method is simple and reliable, especially suitable for gold ores with various impurities, since accompany elements like As, S and Hg can be recovered in the process. In fact, the method is able to produce roasting ore with a direct production cost about 350-500 RMB/t, which is quite low. In China, the first two stage roasting process was built by Shandong Guoda metallurgical plant in 2002. Afterwards, several plants using this method have been built including: Shandong Henbang gold metallurgical plant, Zhaojin Xinta gold metallurgical plant, Zijin gold metallurgical plant, Central South gold metallurgical plant and Qinhai Tanjian mountain gold metallurgical plant. Above 1000t/d roasting gold ores can be produced by these plants [10]. This method also has its application in other countries, for example, Jerritt Canyon gold ore in America uses this method to process Kalin type gold ore, with a capability of 3200t/d. 

However, the oxidative roasting method has some shortages. Firstly, it requires precise temperature and atmosphere control, otherwise the ore may be over or incompletely calcinated, leading to a secondary encapsulating or inco

mplete disclosing of the gold ores. Secondly, as As and S mainly enter the atmosphere in the form of AS2O3 and SO2, air pollution can be a serious problem. Thirdly, even with a precise condition control, some roasted gold ores are still difficult to be processed by cyaniding. Some new methods have also been developed to improve the conventional oxidative roasting method, including oxygen rich roasting, solidification roasting and microwave roasting, etc.. 

Oxygen rich roasting process uses oxygen rich gas as combustion medium and to fluidize ore particles. As the volume of the flue gas is remarkably reduced, energy efficiency and SO2 concentration are greatly raised accordingly. However, refractory gold ores with high sulfur and arsenic content requires a stepwise elimination of S and As. Although higher oxygen concentration in the gas will increase production speed, it also causes a furious oxidation without control, leading to a secondary gold encapsulation. Further, AS2O3 can be easily oxidized to AS2O5, the reaction between AS2O5 and Fe2Ы3 leads to the formatnion of Fe3(As04)2, which is unfavorable in cyanidation [8]. 

Solidification roasting process mixes alkaline calcium and sodium salts with refractory gold ores to solidify sulfur and arsenic in the calcination, avoiding the formation of air polluters (AS2O3 and SO2). With a proper calcium and sodium salt addition, over 90% As and S will be solidified. However, large amount of alkaline materials should be added to reach ideal solidification effect, even as many as some refractory gold ores itself. Since As and S will be solidified without volatilization, gold concentration in the roasted ore is reduced. 

Microwave roasting has been developed as a potential thermal pretreatment process due to its ability to heat ore minerals selectively. The process can not only effectively oxidize the sulfide matrix in refractory gold ores but also greatly reduce the operation cost [11]. Investigation on the removal of sulfur and arsenic from a refractory gold concentrate by microwave heating showed 

547 

that over 90% arsenic can be easily removed even without oxygen, while the removal of sulfur is greatly promoted in a oxidative atmosphere [12]. Other study also showed that microwave heating can easily oxidize pyrite to hematite, but is not so effective for the removal of carbon [13]. 

A new method based on bath smelting technology has also been developed to recover gold from refractory gold ores containing As and S. As copper matte is a good gold collector, most of gold in the ore can be recovered with copper in the melting bath of the refractory gold ores. It has been demonstrated by Fangyuan Corporation in China that 6t gold can be produced based on the production of 100 thousand tones of Cu. In the process, As and S are oxidized and then collected as AS2O3 and SO2, respectively. If their content in the ores exceed 16%, the oxidation could provide energy that is enough for the smelting process.

Moreover, this method extracts gold in the refractory gold ores directly to copper matte, cyanidation is eliminated, which makes the process very energy saving and environmental friendly. However, two problem should be solved before the fully success of this method. Firstly, could the amount of collector be greatly reduced or even use the elements in the refractory gold ores as collector? Secondly, consequent refining of gold from the copper matte can be a very long process, is there any more efficient purification method? ###### Hydrometallurgy Process Hydrometallurgical pretreatment for refractory gold ores usually includes pressure oxidation, which can be categorized into acidic and alkaline pressure system. Acidic pressure oxidation is often conducted in a sulfuric acid system, aiming to decompose pyrite and arsenic pyrite in a condition with high temperature, high pressure and oxidative atmosphere. Considerable research interests have been attracted and many progresses have been made. However, what lies between this process and its wide industrial application is that it takes a long time before the process finishes. The precious metal accumulated in the biometallurgy system will lead to a very large capital cost. Moreover, the living and reproduction conditions required 549 by bacteria are very strict, which is difficult to handle in large scale industrial production. ###### **Conclusions** This article reviews the distribution and categories of the refractory gold ores. The state of art in processing refractory gold ores by pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy and biometallurgy techniques and their industrial applications are highlighted. It can be concluded that each technology has its advantages and shortages. The pyrometallurgy process is a very simple and mature technology that has lots of industrial applications, but it requires precise condition control and causes severe air pollution. Moreover, some refractory gold ores are still difficult to process even after the pretreatment. On the other hand, although the hydrometallurgy process is efficient and clean, either acidic pressure oxidation or alkaline pressure oxidation system has its limit. What

is more, the equipment and capital investment of the process are very demanding, so it is not popular in China. In contrast, biometallurgy process is the most promising technology for refractory gold pretreatment. It is a green metallurgy process requires neither energy nor chemical reagents, which reduces the production cost to 1/3 ofthat of the pyrometallurgy process. However, due to the long reaction time and strict living/reproduction condition, bacteria with higher reactivity and tolerance should be developed before a wide application of this technology. 

The nature of all these technologies is to find an efficient and cheap way to destruct pyrite and arsenic pyrite, which enables the disclosure of the encapsulated gold. Whatever the process is, cyanidation is finally needed for gold extraction. Since cyanidation will bring severe pollution to the environment, the best way to process refractory gold ores should be extracting gold directly from the ores. With the high sulfur content in the gold ores, process based on bath smelting technology can be very attractive.

###### STUDY ON IRON RECOVERY AND DESULFURIZATION OF PYRITE CINDER 

Xiaohui Fan, Hongli Wen, Qiong Deng, Min Gan, Guangkun Shen, Shoujian Huang

###### **Abstract** 

Due to the low iron grade and high sulfur content, pyrite cinder is difficult to be directly used for iron-making. In this paper, technology of magnetic roasting - grinding and magnetic separation - acid leaching was put forward for reclamation of pyrite cinder. For pyrite cinder of TFe53.51%, S2.20 %, studies showed that good magnetic effect can be achieved at roasting temperature 650-700 D, reducing atmosphere CO/(CO + CO2) 10-20% and roasting time 10-30 minutes. In separation conditions of grinding size -0.045mm accounting for 96.09% and magnetic field intensity of 1240 GS, iron concentrate of TFe64.81 %, SO.18% and iron recovery rate 91.44% was achieved. Acid leaching was studied to strengthen desulfurization. Results showed that high-quality iron ore concentrate of TFe66.31%, SO. 10% was obtained under the conditions of hydrochloric acid mass fraction of 5%, pulp density of 30%, leaching temperature of 70 D and leaching time of 2 hours. 

###### **Introduction** 

Pyrite cinder is produced as a by-product of sulfuric acid industry<sup>l</sup> _'._ Domestic production is more than 12 million tons every year and occupied area is over 10 million square meters<sup>l</sup> ' _'._ The pyrite cinder outdoor not only pollutes air but also damages surrounding surface<sup>l</sup> _'._ It after treatment used for iron-making is an ideal reclamation approach for its rich iron which is commonly 40-60%<sup>l</sup> _'._ But pyrite cinder gets low utilization for its low iron grade and high sulfur content in China<sup>l</sup> _'._ Therefore, comprehensive utilization of pyrite cinder has profound significance to environmental protection and the development of domestic iron and steel industry.

###### **Abstract** 

Magnetic roasting process, aiming at obtaining magnetite concentrate, is the principle method of exploiting siderite as a raw material in iron and steel industry. Study on preparing DRI from siderite through coal based reduction technology is sporadic. To make the process of how siderite is reduced to iron clear, roasted ore reduced from siderite by lignite under different time periods were analyzed. The results indicated that: at the temperature of 1050°C, siderite was r

apidly decomposed into magnetite, and further reduced as Fe3C>4^FeO^Fe, the later step was slower than the previous one. A fracture of particles was found during the process of thermal decomposition and the reduction of newly formed magnetite. As the reduction proceeded, metallization rate of products increased, and the iron grain grew along with time. 

###### **Introduction** 

With the rapid development of economy, China demands more and more iron ores for the iron and steel industry. China has rich iron ore resources, but 97% of them are below 30% in iron grade, many are refractory and unutilized [1], therefore large quantities of imported iron ores are in a desperate need. China imported 686 million tons of iron ore in 2011 (data from the China Customs), accounting for nearly 60% of the total consumption. To guarantee the healthy development of iron and steel industry, domestic refractory iron ores have to be utilized both economically and environmentally. 

There are 1.83 billion tons of proved siderite reserves in China, accounting for 3.4% of total reserves of iron ores nationwide [1]. But only 10% of them, which is used for ferrous metallurgy, has been rationally utilized [2]. Magnetic roasting process, aiming at obtaining magnetite concentrate, is the principle method of exploiting siderite. To get the final product (mostly steel), multiple roasting has been involved in the process, and brings the problem of energy waste. Considering the rich coal resources and maturing technology on coal based reduction in China, some scholars suggest the application of coal based reduction-magnetic separation technology in siderite ore. 

Zizong Zhu et al. [3] obtained sponge iron powder with iron content in excess of 84% and metallization rate above 90% after magnetic separation of coal based reduction of siderite in a

XRD patterns of siderite after roasted for different time periods (a- Siderite; b- Quartz; c- Calcite; d- Magnetite; e- Wustite; f- Iron; g- Olivine) Siderite was the main phase of Fe in the original siderite ore, and major gangue minerals were quartz and calcite. Siderite and calcite are typical carbonates that emit C02 under thermal decomposition. It could be seen from Figure 2 that after 10 minutes' roast at 1050°C, part of siderite and calcite were decomposed and large quantities of magnetite were found in the roasted ore. Much wustite and little Iron wer

e found at the 20th minute, when magnetite abounded while siderite disappeared, which indicated the thermal decomposition period of siderite to magnetite was less than 20 minutes in reduction atmosphere at 1050°C. 

The 30th minute saw the disappearance of magnetite and calcite, leaving wustite and iron the major phase of Fe and quartz the only gangue mineral detected by XRD. Magnetite, as an intermediate phase, existed for less than 30 minutes, and magnetite was transformed to wustite within 20 minutes (between the 10th and 30th minute), which suggested the instability of magnetite in reduction atmosphere at 1050°C. The 40th minute witnessed hopping of metallization rate from 10.17% at the 30th minute to 48.90% while the peak of wustite was weaken, which indicated the immediate transformation of wustite to iron after the initial iron nucleus was formed. 

567 

The subsequent reaction mainly focused on the conversion of wustite to iron. Fayalite peak, though frail during its appearance, was detected at the 60th minute, when peak of iron kept on increasing while wustite weakening. Fayalite disappeared at the 100th minute. Compared with the research made by Yan [7], less fayalite was formed because temperature used in this paper was relatively lower, sufficient coal also contributed to the immediate reduction of existing fayalite. By the 120th minute, metallization rate reached 93.22%, iron became the major Fe phase. To conclude, it took more than 100 minutes for wustite to convert to iron from the emergence of iron (before the 20th minute) to the disappearance of wustite (after the 120th minute), therefore the slowest stage of the reduction of siderite lies in the conversion of wustite into iron. 

###### Microscopic Structure Analysis 

Microscopic structure of the roasted ore was analyzed with the help of Laica DMI5000M Microscope to determine the conversion behavior of siderite. All pictures were taken under reflection light. 

Figure 3 to Figure 4 witness the microstructure change during thermal decomposition. New magnetite formed at initial stage remained the original structure of siderite. After staying in reduction atmosphere at 1050°C for 20 minutes, siderite disappeared and the compact bulks were fractured into small particles, and magnetite and wustite composed the major Fe phase. Iron also began to emerge in active spots where wustite was formerly appeared. The particle was even smaller (Figure 5) as the reduction proceeded, which indicated fracture existed not only in thermal decomposition, but also in the transformation of magnetite to wustite. Iron content was rapidly increased after the 30th minute, when iron particle was sporadically distributed. At the 60th minute (Figure 6), iron became the major Fe phase, and the subsequent process saw the size growth of iron grain. 

Enlarged picture shown in Figure 9 and Figure 10 illustrated that average iron grain size increased from smaller than 7 um at the 60th minute to over 30um at the

**Conclusions** (1) As time siderite ore staying in the reactor lengthening, TFe of the roasted ore kept increasing until it became stable, MFe and metallization rate grew rapidly after staying at zero for a short 569 period of time, though the acceleration slowed down gradually before it became nearly zero when most of Fe were reduced to iron. (2) Siderite was rapidly decomposed into magnetite within 20 minutes in reduction atmosphere at 1050°C, and further reduced as Fe 3 0 4 ^FeO^Fe, in which the later step was slower than the previous one. Fayalite, as an intermediate product, slightly emerged and then disappeared. The reason was that 1050°C was not high enough for the springing up of fayalite, and the appeared fayalite was quickly reduced to iron due to sufficient coal. (3) A fracture of particles was found not only in thermal decomposition of siderite, but also in the transformation of magnetite to wustite, and iron grain size grew along with roasting time. ###### **References** 1. ###### **Abstract** 

The effect of reduction temperature on the vanadium titano-magnetite carbon composite pellets was investigated by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and the discussion has put emphasis upon the enhanced reduction mechanism of additives containing CaF2 and NaF in this paper. The results showed that the reduction temperature of 1350 °C was needed for the generation, mergence and growing up of metallic iron as well as monomer dissociation between metallic iron particles and slag phase in the vanadium titano-magnetite metallization pellets. The iron compound was completely reduced into metal iron, and Fe2TiC>4 was mainly transformed into metal iron, (Fe,Mg)Ti205 and FeTi03 at 1350°C The maximum metallization ratio was only 88.5% at 1350D for 30 min without any additive. However, with the addition of 3.0% CaF2 or NaF, the metallization degree of pellets could reach up to 94.8% and 92.5%, respectively. 

###### **Introduction** 

Vanadium titano-magnetite which is mainly distributed in the area of Panxi, Chengde and Maanshan in China is a kind of complex iron ore which contains various valuable metal elements such as iron, vanadium, titanium, etc. Among the above areas, Panzhihua (Sichuan Province in China) area possesses the largest deposits of vanadium titano-magnetite and the future reserves are more than 100><10<sup>8</sup> t, and the reserves of Ti existing as Ti0 2 reach to 8.7><10<sup>8</sup> t which occupy over 91% of the whole nation and ranked No.l in the worldfl]. Lots of researches on the comprehensive utilization of vanadium titano-magnetite have been conducted in the world. And many technological processes have been applied successfully in industrial production. Among these processes, the process of rotary kiln-electric furnace is employed to recover iron and vanadium in South-Africa, while the process of blast furnace-rotary furnace is widely used in Russia and China. Besides, many researchers have made efforts on employing new direct reduction process to realize the effective comprehensive utilization of vanadium titanomagnetite[2-4]. However, the direct reduction process is only researched in laboratory and it has not been used in industry. 

Studies on coal based direct reduction processes of vanadium titano-magnetite ore have been carried our<sup>1-5</sup> '. Reduction of ores by carbon is a key metallurgical reaction in coal based

However, the effects of some metallurgical fluxes such as CaF2, NaF on reduction rate of vanadium titanomagnetite carbon composite pellets have not been reported extensively. Effect of NaF addition on the metallization rate of pellets Microstructures of Reduction Pellets The surface characteristics of the pellets adding additives or not under reduction temperature 1350°C in nitrogen atmosphere were showed in Figure 5. With the additives, it could be inferred via Figure 3 that a lot of low melting point compounds melting were promoted by the additive of CaF2 or NaF and sintering occurred. As a result, pores were eliminated and the direct reduction occurring through gaseous intermediates was broken. However, due to sintering and fusion of grains, a more intimate contact between carbon and oxides would be established by dissolution of carbon in the fused mass. The true direct reduction of carbon could take place in the pellets. 575 Because the dissolution of carbon in the fused mass de

pended on the availability of carbon in the vicinity of fused area, the mixture of additives decreased the melting point of slag, and increased the chances of more carbon to be presented near the fused areas. More dissolution of carbon and more direct reduction of oxides which caused the reduction degree of composites pellets to increase with increasing the amount of additives occurred. Comparing Figure 5(b) to Figure 5(c), CaF2 possessed a greater ability of lowering the melting point of slag than NaF. In addition to this, NaF can strengthen the reduction process due to gaseous sodium passing into the wustite (FexO) lattice, causing the lattice distortion, resulting in interface reduction activation energy lowered to speed up their interface reaction rate [6,7] in the reduction process of vanadium titano-magnetite carbon composite pellets. 



Comparing Figure 3 and Figure 4 with Figure 5, it could be gotten that the gas diffusion would be the rate controlling step. In the literature [5,8-10], it had been showed that carbon gasification was the rate controlling step which was different from the conclusion from this paper. The structure of vanadium titano-magnetite is compact as the disadvantage of gas diffusion. In the contrary, carbon gasification and surface reaction would occur easily at high temperature. In some papers'<sup>11</sup> , the mechanism of additives was explained as promoting the carbon gasification or surface reaction which resulted in the increase of reduction rate of iron oxides. Under high temperature, gas diffusion became the rate controlling step, the decrease of diffusing space of vanadium titano-magnetite carbon composite pellets was due to the converting of crystal lattice which revealed the CaF2 was better than NaF for reduction. The detailed reduction mechanism would be introduced in another paper. 

###### **Conclusion** 

(1) The reduction temperature of 1350°C was needed for the generation, mergence and growing up of metallic iron as well as monomer dissociation between metallic iron particles and slag phase in the vanadium titano-magnetite metallization pellets. Meanwhile, the iron compound was completely reduced into metal iron, and Fe2Ti04 was mainly transformed into metal iron, (Fe,Mg)Ti2C>5 and FeTiC>3 at the same temperature. 

(2) Reduction reaction could be promoted by adding CaF2 or NaF. During the reduction process, CaF2 and NaF could reduce the melting point of solid phase reaction product, then to reduce its viscosity, and optimize reduction process of heat and mass transfer, which were in favour of ions diffusion, growth and enrichment. NaF could also cause the mineral crystal lattice distortion which would reduce the activation energy to speed up the interface reaction rate.

(3) With the addition of 3.0% CaF2 or NaF, the maximum metallization ratio of vanadium titanomagnetite carbon composite pellets in Nitrogen atmosphere could reach up to 94.8% and 92.5%, respectively, all of which were bette

r than 88.5% at 1350 °C for 30 min without any additive.

###### AN INVESTIGATION ON UTILIZATION OF FERROUS SCRAP BY COULD-BONDED PELLETIZING 

Xiao-hui Fan, Li-shun Yuan<sup>1</sup> , Min Gan, Wei Lv, Yi Wang, Xu-ling Chen 

School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan, 410083, P.R.China 

Key words: Cold-bonded pellet, Ferrous scrap, Rust catalyst 

###### **Abstract** 

As the amount of ferrous scrap increases every year, it becomes more and more urgent to deal with this iron-bearing resource properly. This paper puts forward a method on resource-oriented utilization of ferrous scrap (cold-bonded pelletizing), and these cold-bonded pellets can be used as coolant in a converter. The influence on the pellets qualities by using different kinds of chloride as rust agents is studied, and results show t

hat the strength of cold-bonded pellets increases significantly by using a combination of the three kinds of chloride -NaCl,MgCl2NFeCl3, their best dosages are 1.2%, 0.2%, 0.1% respectively. Other iron-bearing materials also have an effect upon the pellets strength, by adding 5% iron powder and maintaining for 48h, the compressive strength of the clumps surpass 2500N/A, dropping strength surpass 4 times/A, and 10% iron slag or 20% steel slag can replace 5% iron powder while obtaining the comparative quality. The influence of different ratios of three ferrous scrap (converter mud, iron scale and dust) is further studied, and results show that when the ratio is 30% : 30% : 40%, the pellet strength reaches the maximum. After maintaining for 24~48h, the clumps can meet the mechanical as well as the physical-chemical requirements as BOF steelmaking refrigerant. 

###### **Introduction** 

Great amounts of converter mud, dust and iron scale are produced in steel production process. These materials are of great values, and their accumulation not only leads to environmental pollution, but also wastes the precious resources, which restricts the sustainable development of the steel industry _"_<sup>_,2_</sup> _>._ The main approach at present to dealing with the ferrous scrap is to add them into sintering. But in this way, the utilization factor of sintering and the quality of sinter decline while the energy consumption increases . Therefore, more advanced and efficient technology is needed to make the best of these iron resources. Cold consolidation of ferrous scrap is a simple process that has many advantages such as less investment, quicker effect, lower energy and lower cost '<sup>4</sup> . But the conventional maintaining period is too long, usually up to four-six weeks, and the pellet strength is low. Therefore, the key points of the

###### Test Methods 

Iron powder blended with a certain proportion of water and rust agents are added into the certain amount of ferrous scrap. After sufficient mixing, 300kg/cm<sup>2</sup> pressure is produced by a hydraulic universal testing machine in order to form <t>30mm X 30mm cylindrical pellets. The green pellets will become cold consolidation pellets after natural maintaining for a certain period of time. Then the compressive strength and the dropping strength of the pellets are tested. Compressive strength is the maximum pressure each cold-mass can withstand before cracking, and it is measured by the ZS-3 intelligent strength tester developed by Central South University. Dropping strength is denoted as the times when the cold-mass drop from 2m height to the steel plate before cracking. 

###### **The Coolant Requirements of Converter Steelmaking** 

There is surplus heat in the process of steelmaking in oxygen top blown converter. In order to keep the heat balance, adding a certain amount of coolant to hit the end point temperature 

580 

accurately is necessary. Oxygen top blown converter commonly uses rich iron ore, sinter, pellets and steel scrap as coolants . Attention should be paid to gangue content when using these materials, because the higher Si0 2 content, the more slag volume, which may lead to a large jet. On the other hand, high gangue content will affect the steel properties. Thus, the harmful impurities of coolant should be as less as possible . If pellets made from ferrous scrap with qualified mechanical strength can meet the chemical composition requirements of steel, it can be applied to converter steelmaking as coolant replacing the rich iron ore and sinter. Chemical requirements of coolant used in steelmaking are listed in Table II<sup>[8]</sup> . At present, there is still no consistent standard of dropping strength for cold-bonded mass in converter steelmaking. Thus, just guarantee the mass not broken in working process. This test set the dropping strength standard to be greater than or equal to 4 times/A.

###### **Abstract** 

In this research, pyrite cinder which contains 53.51% Fe and 0.54% Pb was processed by magnetic roasting separation to obtain a concentrate with 64.62% Fe and 0.56% Pb. The concentrate was then leached with hydrochloric acid to remove lead. Several technological parameters which may influence the removal efficiency were investigated: the mass fraction of hydrochloric acid, pulp density, the leaching time and temperature. On the conditions that the mass fraction of hydrochloric acid of 5%, pulp density of 30%, the leaching time of 30 minutes and leaching temperature of 20°C, the lead content in the concentrate was reduced to 0.19%. The product was suitable for agglomeration and pelletization. Through the analysis of the lead distribution and phase change during the whole process, the mechanism of lead separation from pyrite cinder was analyzed. 

###### **Introduction** 

Pyrite cinder is rich in iron, which defines its most extensive and effective use as raw materials fo

To separate the lead from pyrite cinder, much research was done, including flotation, high temperature evaporation and leaching. High temperature evaporation consumed too much energy. Majority of the leaching was direct leaching of pyrite cinder, which was also difficult to get high-grade iron ore concentrate[3]. This article explored the magnetic roasting method to get high-grade iron ore concentrate, acid leaching method of the concentrate to remove excessive lead, providing guidance for the efficient utilization of pyrite cinder. ###### **Raw Material Properties** Pyrite cinder used in this assay is fine-grained, with -0.074mm and -0.045mm content of 92.05% and 23.61% respectively. ###### **Abstract** 

The microwave reflection loss (RL) of ferric oxide is studied in the temperature range from 297 to approximately 1400 K at frequencies of 915 and 2450 MHz. It is shown that the maximum microwave absorption with RL of-38.46 and -35.97 dB can be obtained for ferric oxide having thicknesses of 0.03 and 0.01 m at 915 and 2450 MHz, respectively. The maximum absorption peak with RL below -10 dB is in a 250 K temperature range from 723 to 973 K at 915 MHz, which shifts to the range between 823 and 1073 K at 2450 MHz. This migration is in good agreement with the variation of the dielectric loss tangent of ferric oxide. 

###### **Introduction** 

Microwave irradiation has distinguishing characteristics such as volumetric and selective heating compared with conventional methods, leading to extremely broad applications in materials heating and processing [l-5].The efficiency of microwave heating was found to be dependent on various factors, such as microwave power [6], frequency [7,8], radiation time [8], applicator geometry [8], sample microwave absorption properties and position as well as dimension [9-11], etc. Among these parameters, sample dimension plays an important role but is usually neglected by researchers in microwave processing of materials. In fact, although numerous studies have been directed toward the utilization of microwave ener

gy to assist materials heating and processing, few reports were released on the effect of sample dimension [12,13].This is because all aforementioned factors influencing microwave heating generally exert interactive effects to each other during the heating process, making clarification of the effect of sample dimension difficult. Therefore, it is necessary to propose a parameter or concept for quantifying the effect of absorber dimension on microwave heating, increasing heating efficiency. In the present study, the concept of reflection loss (RL) is introduced to as a parameter in microwave heating. This is proposed because microwave heating is usually performed in a metallic cavity. The usage of RL indicates the effect of sample dimension on microwave heating by simplifying the problem through studying the sample thickness dependence of microwave absorption. This dependence is shown specifically with ferric oxide (Fe2C>3), a material which is widely used in chemical synthesis and ironmaking [14,15]. The results demonstrate the variation of reflection loss of Fe 20 3 with thickness at commonly used microwave frequencies based on the corresponding microwave permittivity measurements. The work suggests that microwave 597 absorption in ferrie oxide exhibits a strong thickness dependence throughout the microwave heating process. ###### **Theory of Reflection Loss** Reflection loss (RL) quantifies the amount of microwave power reflected from the surface of a material slab backed by metal under microwave irradiation. The smaller RL there is for a sample, the better (larger) the microwave absorption in the material. As shown in Figure 1, microwaves with unit amplitude are incident normally on an absorber (sample) slab backed by metal (or a perfect electric conductor, PEC), resulting in reflected waves traveling in the opposite direction. ###### **Experimental** 

To demonstrate the thickness effect on material reflection loss, ferric oxide powders (99.98 % purity) supplied by Sigma-Aldrich Corp., St. Louis, MO were used for the permittivity measurements. The chemical composition (Fe2Ы3) was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) using a conventional Scintag XDS2000 powder X-ray diffractometer (Scintag Inc., Cupertino, CA) with a graphite monochromator and Cu Ka radiation. Sample microstructure and particle distribution were characterized by using a Hitachi S-4700 field-emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM, Hitachi Ltd., Tokyo, Japan). It is found that the sample powders having spherical shape with particle size between 0.05 and 0.2 um. 

The permittivity of Fe 20 3 was measured using the cavity perturbation technique [17]. The main components of the measurement system include a resistive heating furnace and a cylindrical TMono resonant mode cavity. The system measures the differences (frequency shift and change of quality factors) in the microwave cavity response between a cavity with an empty sample-holder and the same cavity with a sample-holder plus the sample at each specified temperature. These differences are recorded in a Hewlett Packard 8753B vector network analyzer and then used to calculate the permittivity. The details about this technique and apparatus used for the measurements can be found in the published literature [17,18]. 

For the permittivity test, Fe 20 3 powders were first uniaxially pressed at -207 MPa in a die lined with tungsten carbide to form pellets with a diameter of ~3.62 mm having a total stacked length (height) of 12.97 mm. The bulk density (room temperature) of the sample was 2.79 g/cm<sup>3</sup> . During the measurements, the sample was step-heated in the conventional resistance furnace to the designated temperatures in 0.01 L/min flowing argon. The permittivity measurements started at room temperature (297 K) and heated in 50 K intervals to -1400 K. Two frequencies, 915 and 2450 MHz, were used for the measurements because they are the most commonly used ones in microwave heating.

Conclusions In this study, the concept of microwave reflection loss is introduced to indicate the effect of sample dimension on microwave heating. The microwave reflection loss of ferric oxide has been studied in the temperature range from 297 to -1400 K at 915 and 2450 MHz based on permittivity measurements using the cavity perturbation technique. It is demonstrated that the maximum microwave absorption with reflection loss of-38.46 and -35.97 dB can be obtained for ferric oxide having thicknesses of 0.03 and 0.01 m at 915 and 2450 MHz, respectively. The 601 maximum absorption peak with RL below -10 dB is in a 250 K temperature range from 723 to 973 K at 915 MHz, which shifts to the range between 823 and 1073 K at 2450 MHz. The maximum absorption peak position in the RL pattern is determined mainly by the dielectric loss tangent of ferric oxide. It is suggested that a sample with variable thickness is favored during microwave heating. More theoretical investigations into dynamics of microwave propagation and dissipation in materials are required. ###### **Acknowledgements** This work was supported by the Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources, the Michigan Public Service Commission, U.P. ###### **Abstract** 

Response surface method (RSM) based on mono-factor experiment was applied for the process optimization of sintering of chromite fines by microwave. In RSM analysis, effects of binder addition amount, sintering temperature and holding time on the compression strength and shatter strength of the sinter were examined. Results showed that the optimal values of the above parameters were determined as follows: binder addition amount of 1.90% (in mass), sintering temperature of 1153 D and holding time of 16 min. Under the optimized conditions, the compression strength was 11155.8N and shatter strength was 95.6849%. The results show that the process was optimized by response surface methodology is stable and feasible, and provide a new way for sintering of chromite fines.

Chromite ore is the main feedstock for ferrochrome, and ferrochrome can be used as steelmaking additive to produce a variety of great strength, corrosion resistant and oxidation resistant special steel, which can be widely used in the aerospace, automotive, shipbuilding, military departments'<sup>1</sup> , and it has important strategic significance. Thus manufacturing blocks by using cheap chromite fines is an effective measure to reduce the cost of ferrochrome production and use the chromite resources'<sup>3</sup> '. 

The common chromite fines agglomeration methods include sintering, bonding pellet and briquetting process.Wherein the sintering process has been always considered to have unique advantages, and its traditional craft is mixing chromite fines, coke powder and return mines at a certain ratio, pelleting, distributing, igniting, ventilating and sintering .But for chromite's spinel structure, high melting point, acidic sintering production sand difficult to forming liquid phase, its burn-up is high, and yeild is somewhat low. While apply microwave heating in sintering chromite fines, namely take advantage of chromite's strong wave-absorbing properties, we can add no coke powder, cancel the ventilation process, just use a little bentonite as binder, and sinter at low temperature (1100°C~1200°C), obtaining high strength sintered chromite.

###### **Abstract** 

In this paper, the methods of life cycle assessment for microwave hot air systems, and the concept of green degree were proposed. Greenness evaluation index, evaluation system and evaluation model of microwave hot air systems were established. Also, life cycle assessment processing based on these ideas was introduced. Analytic hierarchy process and fuzzy decisionmaking method were utilized to establish and solve the greenness evaluation of assessment model, while the

scores of green degree in microwave hot air systems were obtained. The results show that Life cycle assessment can be applied effectively and efficiently to the microwave hot air systems. 

###### **Introduction** 

Hot air systems are an important industrial operation condition, which is used to provide high temperature air for materials processing. Nowadays, high temperature airs are manufactured by the conventional heating processes, in which some ceramic materials are used as heating materials. However, these processes pollute the environment. Therefore, to explore new method to produce high temperature air with low energy consumption and less environment pollution are necessary. 

Microwaves are now being used in various technological and scientific fields in order to heat dielectric materials [1]. Microwaves irradiation has been explored in materials processing in recent years [2-3]. The main advantage of using microwave heating is that the treatment time can be considerably reduced, which in many cases represents a reduction in the energy consumption as well. Since there is energy absorption but no heat conduction, the heating is very rapid and 

615 

highly efficient, resulting in energy savings and the shortened processing time [2, 4]. Compared with conventional heating techniques, the additional advantage of using microwave irradiation is that microwave irradiation achieves both internal and uniform heating [5-7]. In addition, it is more convenient to control the microwave irradiation processing, because of no direct contact between the heating source and heated materials with less equipment size and waste [2, 8-9]. 

Life cycle assessment is used and accepted methods for the evaluation of the environmental impacts of products or systems [10]. Recently, many appropriate evaluation methods have been developed for life cycle assessment [11-12]. These proposed methods usually are employed for the evaluating product and analyzing results [13]. Among them, the analytic hierarchy process and the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation stand out as a popular method utilized in many fields [14-16]. Analytic hierarchy process and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation are a combination of mathematical and statistical technique that is useful for analyzing the effects of several independent assessment aspects on the system goal without the need of the predetermined relationship between the objective function and the assessment aspects [17-19]. 

Based on the concept mentioned above, the objective of this research was, on one hand, to study the assessment model of microwave hot air systems using life cycle assessment, on the other hand, to characterize and analyze the green degree of assessment model using analytic hierarchy process and fuzzy decision-making method.

###### **Features of Microwave Hot Air Systems** 

Typical industrial microwave hot air systems consists of a magnetron to produce the microwaves, a waveguide to transport the microwaves, a resonance cavity to manipulate microwaves for a specific purpose, and a control system to regulate the temperature and microwave power [2]. A hot air system to produce high temperature airs. Magnetron is used to generate microwave power, which is most widely used for the industrial microwave heating applications due to its availability and low cost. Wave guide transfers the generated microwave energy from the magnetron to the resonant cavity. Resonant cavity is the most important part of microwave tube furnace, whose size is accurately calculated by microwave theories. The power supply of microwave hot air systems was 36 magnetrons at 2.45 GHz frequency and 1.5 kW power. The dimensions of the multi-mode microwave resonance cavity are 1300 mm in height, 2100 mm in length and 1300 mm in width. The temperature was measured using a Type K thermocouple with a thin layer of aluminum shielding, placed at the closest proximity to the heating sample.

###### **Abstract** 

Magnetic iron sulfide ore particles heat rapidly by microwave (MW) irradiation generating plasma during oxidation of surfaces. The high temperatures produced by the exothermic event decompose local portions of samples forming a differentiated flux of partially melted silicate _(si-mt)_ with entrained metal-sulfide _(sul-mt)_ droplets. The _si-mt_ forms crystals of olivine (Ol) in Ca-rich pyroxene (Cpx) melt that resorbs a portion of iron sulfide (Po). The immiscible _sul-mt_ droplets of (Fe,Ni,Cu)i_xS contain magnetic subsolidus Ni-pyrrhotite (Ni-Po) with Cr-bearing ferrospinel (Mag). Sub-micron sized flecks of Au are found on the surface of a _sul-mt_ droplet with scanning electron microscope (SEM). 

###### **Introduction** 

Sulfide ore deposits supply the world's mineral resource in the production of non-ferrous metals. Particularly, Cu-Ni deposits are chemically enriched in metals from high sulfur saturation during magmatic formation that creates the proper geochemical environment for metals enrichment [1, 2]. The sulfur and oxygen fugacity control redox conditions of a differentiated silicate/sulfur magmatic melt with the concentration of iron playing a dominate role in the chemical partitioning of metals in sulfide liquid [3, 4]. The initial magnetic crystallization of (Fe,Ni)i.xS monosulfide solution _(mss)_ from metal-sulf

ide liquid has an exclusive effect on the fractionation of mineral assemblages (zoning) [5]. Phase equilibria of sulfide melt _(sul-mt)_ components are related by a miscibility gap with _mss_ forming Ni-rich pyrrhotite (Ni-Po) followed by the crystallization of (Fe,Cu)i_xS intermediate sulfide solution _(iss)_ [6]. Precious metals form stable chacogenides and are retained in solution until the final liquid solidifies. The redistribution of metals now occurs by subsolidus cooling of _mss_ and _iss_ that exsolve low-temperature Fe-Cu-Ni bearing mineral assemblages [7]. The proper interpretation of ore genesis increases processing capabilities by isolating chemically enriched zones during extraction and should be used to aid in sustainable mine site development [8-11]. 

The non-stoichiometric iron sulfide mineral pyrrhotite (Fei_xS) forms a variety of ferrimagnetic superstructures providing a strong source of microwave (MW) absorption [11-14]. In general, transition metal sulfides have strong dielectric properties from _E-H_ field polarization of loosely bound af-orbital electrons that arise from strong metal-metal interactions within a moderately covalent sulfur structure [15-17]. The electromotive forces induced by MW energy activate diffusion processes that generate frictional heating (irradiation) during atomic collisions [18, 19]. When chemical bonds are broken from

###### **Experimental** 

Iron sulfide ore particles of various sizes are exposed to MW energy in open atmosphere at 2.45 GHz, 1000 W power. Electric arcing (plasma) is generated on the surfaces of particles within seconds after irradiation, seen as sparking along with the generation sulfur gas. The heated material is removed from the crucible and allowed to cool in air before sample mounting. Scanning electron microscope (SEM) is used in backscatter electron imaging (BSE) mode for examination of polished cross sections of melt product and secondary electron imaging (SEI) mode is used on un-polished specimens having surface features and topography. All samples are carbon coated for SEM examination with electron dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) used for qualitative phase identification.

###### **DEVELOPMENT OF BISMUTH SMELTING TECHNOLOGY IN CHINA** 

Tian-zu Yang , Jun Li ,Wei-feng Liu ' , Lin Chen , Wan-da Bin 

(1 .School of Metallurgical Science and Engineering, Central South University, Changsha 410083, China;

**Keywords:** bismuth; pyrometallurgy; hydrometallurgy; new research 

###### **Abstract** 

The Chinese bismuth production accounts for more than 80% all over the world in 2011. The main raw materials of bismuth smelting are bismuth concentrate and by-products of Cu or Pb smelting process. Many traditional methods of bismuth smelting in china was reviewed in this paper, such as reverberating furnace smelting, blast furnace smelting, fire-refining, ferric chloride leaching- hydrolysis, slurry electrolysis, and so on. But all the traditi

onal pyrometallurgy or hydrometallurgy process have such shortages of low recovery, poor environment, and high cost. Therefore new technologies are introduced into the smelting process of bismuth concentrate, such as low-temperature alkaline smelting and side-blown bath smelting with oxygen-enrichment. These technologies have got great progress on energy saving, emission reduction, and friendly environment. Finally the development direction of new technology on bismuth smelting was prospected. 

###### **Introduction** 

As a green metal, bismuth has a wider applications, just extending from the traditional medicine, metallurgical-chemical engineering, low-melting alloys, solders, catalyst, and electronics to cosmetics, flame retardant, storage battery, semiconductor, supper conductor and nuclear energy etc[l,2,3,4,5,6,7]. This will increase the production of bismuth and promote the development and progress of bismuth smelting technology. At present, The major bismuth-product countries are China, Mexico, Peru, KZ, Bolivia and Canada etc, and China are dominating. A survey from the USGS[8] showed that Chinese bismuth production were 12,500 tonnes and got 80% of the world's in 2011. Thus the technology of Chinese bismuth smelting have a great representativeness. 

The currently extraction processes of bismuth in China are mainly pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy and both combination. The conventional pyrometallurgy processes are classified as reduction smelting, precipitation smelting and combination smelting[9,10,11]. There are many methods on the hydrometallurgy processes, such as 

631 

the FeCl3 leaching-cementation with iron powder[12] (or diaphragm electric product[13] or hydrolysis sink bismuth[14]), chlorination leaching-extraction[15] and slurry electrolysis[16]. Some new processes are being researching subsequently recently with the urgence of the environment protection and resource-conserving society, such as the low temperature smelting[17]and bath smelting[18]. And there will be a introduction of the Chinese bismuth smelting from the traditional and new technology. 

###### **Traditional Bismuth Smelting** 

Bismuth concentrates are almost always obtained as by-products from metallic ores containing bismuthinite, bismite, and native bismuth in their gravity concentration, magnetic separation and floatation, Or from the further collection of bismuth-containing materials produced on the metal smelting process, they mainly exist with the phases of sulfide and oxide . The traditional extraction processes on the bismuth concentrates are classified as pyrometallurgy and hydrometallurgy smelt. It will be reviewed as follows. 

###### Pyrometallurgy Smelt 

The traditional pyrometallurgy smelting process are producing in the blast furnace, reverberatory furnace and converter, and mainly contains the reduction smelting, precipitation smelting, and combination smelting. 

Reduction Smelting.The reduction smelting[9,10]is the process on the reacti

on between the reducing agent and the bismuth oxide-containing materials, such as the bismuth oxide dross or the bismuth oxide concentrate obtained by the bismuth sulfide concentrate given an oxidizing roast in order to remove sulfur, and the bismuth metal would be produced in the reduction smelting furnace. Besides coal powder, charcoal and coke breeze are also used as reductants. The dilute slag is attained on the high temperature smelt, which come from the reaction between a certain amount of flux must be added and the gangue materials such as the silicon dioxide, calcium oxide and alumina contained in the concentrate. The flux generally used is soda ash and fluorite. If the sulfur in the bismuth oxide dross are not removed completely, a small quantity of scrap iron normally would be added. Decoppering should be done if the the copper content in the charge is high. In this case, a small amount of pyrite is added to turn it into cuprous sulfide which together with ferrous sulfide forms copper matte. The reduction agent (charcoal) and a large amount of carbon monoxide given off from the charcoal oxidizing reduces bismuth oxide into metallic state-the crude bismuth. Owing to the different density in the products of reduction smelting they are separated into three layers with the slag at the top layer, the matte at the middle, and the bismuth in the bottom of the furnace.The basic reactions are:

The desulfurization solution are concentrated and crystallized to recycle the soda, and molybdenum-containing mother liquor is precipitated into molybdenum concentrate and the precipitation solution are output of calcium carbonate and caustic soda for reusing by lime causticizing.
