###### **Prospects** 

The traditional pyrometallurgy smelting process on bismuth smelt in the blast furnace, reverberatory furnace and converter, and have such shortages that poor environment, high consumption and hard to treat the sulfur dioxide. This will face the development challenge of environment friendly, clean metallurgy and resource saving. There will be a risk for dying out unless reform timely or create new technology. 

The hydrometallurgy of bismuth smelting have better comprehensive recovery efficiency, but its flowsheet are long, and cost more water just not suitable for hydropenic areas, require strict equipment, and higher treatment consumption. 

Just because of this, a more suitable bismuth smelting technology develops, such as the low temperature alkaline smelting and side-blown bath smelting with oxygen-enrich, and they have such advantages as friendly-environment, saving-energy and reduction emission. Thus this will be a milestone in the history of bismuth smelt.

###### **Abstract** 

Moulding sands with furan resin constitute constantly growing part in technologies of producing castings from iron alloys. Due to the presence of harmful substances in resins such as furfuryl alcohol, phenol and formaldehyde, using those mould sands may be hazardous to the natural environment and workers. The general assessment of harmfulness of sands used for molds and cores encompasses 2 basic points: emission of hazardous substances during processes of preparing sands, pouring mold with liquid metals (high temperatures), cooling and shaking-out; possibility of washing out hazardous substances from used sands to the environment, during storage or economic use outside foundries. We present the results of research on the assessment of harmfulness of mould sands with furan resin in the scope of the above points. The research was conducted according to the original method prepared by the authors, which has been used for years in cooperation with various foundries (Poland, abroad). 

###### **Introduction** 

Sands are used by the foundry industry to create metalcasting moulds, where the individual sand grains are typically bound using bentonite clay and carbonaceous additives or resins. During the casting process, the moulds can be exposed to temperatures as high as 1500°C depending upon the metal being poured. The molten metal causes thermal decomposition of carbonaceous additives or resins, which results in the formation of potentially hazardous organics that are emitted to the atmosphere and condense in the moulding sand [1]. The moulding sands are reclaimed within the foundry, but part of them are eventually discarded in landfills, because it is not longer suitable to make metalcasting molds [2, 3]. 

The general assessment of harmfulness of sands used for moulds and cores encompasses two basic points: 

- emission of hazardous substances during processes of preparing sands, pouring mold with liquid metals, cooling and shaking - out, 

- possibility of washing out of hazardous substances from used sands to the environment e.g. during storage or using outside foundries. 

Because there is interest in protecting foundry worker health and using waste molding sands in other applications, concern over potentially harmful thermal decomposition products is warranted. The objective of this study research was to identify thermal decomposition products

from different furan resin bonded sands (depends the furfuryl alcohol contents) emitted during their pyrolysis at 500-1100°C temperatures. 

Furan resin sands are presently one of the

most often applied technology of chemically bonded sands for production of ferrous alloys castings. However, only furan resins not containing nitrogen can be used for making steel castings on account of a danger of defects formations. Furan resins are hardened by acidic hardeners as a result of the exothermic polycondensation reaction, which causes a binding agent hardening at a room temperature already (optimal temperature: 20-30°C; too low sand temperature significantly influences a hardening rate and final sand strength). 

All furan resins contain furfuryl alcohol either in a monomer or a polymer form. In dependence of the required resin properties other chemical compounds, such as: urea, formaldehyde, phenol and its derivatives, can be introduced. The higher content of furfuryl alcohol the smaller viscosity of the resin. Resins modified by urea introduce nitrogen into the system in an amount proportional to the urea concentration. In case of urea introducing, there is usually also formaldehyde since its presence improves resin properties. In this type of a system also free formaldehyde can occur. A resin water content is the result of the applied production process and can be controlled to the needed value. The higher water content the longer hardening time and the lower tensile strength. Furan resins can be produced without free formaldehyde, without water and urea. Often aminosilanes are introduced into resins to improve their moisture content resistance and binder adhesiveness to grain matrix surfaces. A selection of the resin kind depends on the required technological parameters of sands, core quality, kind of casting alloy, casting shape, thickness of its walls and the grain matrix reclamation possibility. The optimal resin fraction in a sand depends mainly on the kind of the applied grain matrix (including its purity and grain shape) as well as the required quality of castings.

The European Union demands a drastic decrease of the furfuryl alcohol fraction (to the level below 30%). This means that furan resins applied in the foundry industry, available in the market, do not meet this requirement. This is caused by the change of the furfuryl alcohol classification (according to the rule WE No. 1272/2008) in the range of its influence on living organisms (from carcinogenic Cat. 3 to Cat. 2), which means suspicion that it causes cancer (H351). ###### **Conclusions** 

On the bases of the investigations performed as the laboratory tests and semi-industrial tests it can be stated: 

- The temperature range: 900-1100°C is the most favourable for the BTEX group compounds formation. 

- Benzene is the dominating compound from the BTEX group educing during the thermal decomposition of furan binders. The second one is toluene, which is formed in smaller amounts. 

- Amounts of ethylbenzene and xylene isomers are small, by 2-3 orders smaller than the main components. 

- Binders in which paratoluensulphonic acid is a hardener (resins A and E) generated large amounts of toluene. 

- Resin D hardened by phenylsulphonic acid educed small amounts of toluene. This resin generated also several times smaller amounts of benzene, than the remaining resins. 

- None explicit dependence between the generated gases volume, the concentration of compounds from the BTEX group and the furfuryl alcohol content was found. Therefore it should be considered that fractions of other compounds (phenol, formaldehyde, urea, etc.) contained in the binder, apart from furfuryl alcohol, are here significant. 

- For all tested resins a maximum emission rate of gases occurs after 50-80 seconds from the moment of pouring the mould with liquid metal. Then, there is a fast decrease of the emitted gases volume and the process slows down. Practically after app. 300 seconds the emission stops entirely. 

- Amounts of emitting gases as well as the process kinetics have a significant influence on the quality of castings, in an aspect of faults occurrence.

###### PREDICTION METHOD OF PRE-IGNITION BED PRESSURE DROP IN COMPOSITE AGGLOMERATION PROCESS 

Helei Zhang, Heng Yu, Zhengwei Yu, Yuanbo Zhang, Guanghui Li<sup>1</sup> , Tao Jiang 

School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan 410083,China 

Keywords: Pre-ignition bed pressure drop, Bed permeability, Composite agglomeration, Prediction method 

###### **Abstract** 

Composite agglomeration process (CAP) is an innovative method for preparing blast furnace burden. For CAP, the classified raw materials of pelletizing feeds and matrix feeds are mixed, charged and sintered. The characteristics of these two kinds of feeds obviously affect the permeability of per-ignition bed, as well as the sinter productivity and quality. In this study, the Ergun equation is proposed to predict the pressure drop of CAP bed using the particle size distribution. The calculation process indicates that the Dv and the sm are the two tuning parameters. The results show that there is a gap between the calculated values by Ergun equation and the measured results by pressure drop testing facility. Eliminated this error by modified the Ergun equation and then validated it through experimental studies using simulated CAP mix and test facility. Therefore, the modified Ergun equation can be used to predict the permeability of CAP bed. 

###### **Introduction** 

The sintering process is one of predominant agglomeration processes for preparing ironmaking burden from iron-bearing materials. Sinter accounts for 70-80% of the blast furnace burden in China and the continuous improvement of sinter quality provides a guarantee to anterograde production of blast furnace. Sinter productivity and quality are strongly related to the permeability of the bed during sintering, which is depen

dent on the structure of the bed before ignition in the early stage [1]. The size distribution, the shape of granules and the bed voidage are the primary affecting factors to pre-ignition permeability. 

Composite agglomeration process (CAP) is an innovative method for preparing blast furnace burden[2-5]. Its principle can be summed up as: 1) firstly, fine grained resources obtained from varied process are pelletized, 2) pellets are mixed into traditional sintering mixture, 3) and then the mixture is fired in sintering machine.

CAP is characterized by several advantages such as permission of diverse iron-bearing materials in production, low fuel consumption and remarkably high productivity. Furthermore, the use of the composite agglomerates prepared by CAP is capable of obviating the negative effects caused by the differences in quality of sinter and pellets on the operation of blast furnaces [6,7]. 

The feed bed structure, obviously changed by adding pellets, closely links to cold bed permeability[8].For acquiring optimized pre-ignition permeability, how to choose a suitable pelletizing feed for certain matrix feed or a suitable matrix feed for certain pelletizing feed is an important issue in CAP. However, the traditional testing method of permeability is limited by the volatile measured values and feedback delay in production. It is logical to seek a model which predicts the permeability of CAP bed from aspects of the size distributions, the shape factor of granules and the bed voidage. 

In this study, the Ergun equation'<sup>9</sup> ' has been proposed to calculated pressure drop. The results are in the inverse proportional to the bed permeability. As shown in Ergun equation, the pressure drop of gas flow velocity across the packed bed is dependent on the bed properties including voidage, mean particle diameter and the particle shape.

From Equation (1), voidage is the most significant factor to bed pressure drop, while even a small decrease in bed voidage may cause a significant increase in the pressure drop under given conditions.

###### **Abstract** 

As a result of the shortage of coking coal and the quality decrease of coke, it is important to know how to make better use of highly reactive cokes. The co-gasification behavior of highly and lowly reactive coke for blast furnace is investigated. The results show that: In the middle stage of reaction, the weight loss ratio of highly reactive coke reacted together with lowly reactive coke is higher than that of it reacted individually. However, the weight loss ratio of lowly reactive coke is lower. The weight loss ratio of highly and lowly reactive coke is almost the same as that of the weighted average. The scanning electron microscope analysis indicated that the reaction degree of surface and interior of lowly reactive coke is relatively uniform w

ith the reaction time increased. And the reaction degree of surface of highly reactive coke is obviously higher than that of interior. ###### **Introduction** In blast furnace iron making process, coke functions as heat supplier, reducing agent, carburizer and skeleton. With development of blast furnace iron making technology, the skeleton function of coke is becoming more and more important in requirements of large scale furnace and high pulverized coal injection. High reactivity coke is usually produced by cheap coal with bad quality, and is not good for blast furnace process. The reactivity of coke is mainly determined by the coals used, and the resource of good quality coking coal is limited and is non-renewable. In order to fulfill the need of blast furnace, a lot of research have been done to improve coal matching using new kinds of coal to enlarge resource, in which coking coal and fat coal are reduced, whereas low price coal with bad caking property are used to lower the cost, and this would inevitably increase the reactivity of coke[ " . Blast furnace iron making would still be the main stream for a predicted future, and high reactivity coke would correspondingly be used more and more, so it has great importance to study how to use high reactivity coke in blast furnace. In recent years, some researchers have transferred study focuses from how to lower 659 reactivity of coke to how to use high reactivity coke in blast furnacel " . It has been proved that using of high reactivity coke could lower the temperature of thermal reserve zone, increase efficiency of reduction and lower the emission of CO2. In this paper, four groups of coke, with high and low reactivity mixed together, were tested for their carbon loss ratio and changes of pore structure. The behaviors of two kinds of coke were studied offering reference for use of high reactivity coke in blast furnace process. ###### **1 Experiment** ###### 1.1 Material Cokes used in this paper were sampled from one work in China, named Gengyang coke and Bagang Coke. Ultimate analysis and proximate analysis are listed in table 1. According to the standard of Japan for reactivity and strength of coke after reaction, the reactivity of Gengyang and Bagang coke are 23.89% and 43.14% respectively. So in this paper, Bagang coke is named high reactivity coke, and Gengyang coke is named low reactivity coke. ###### **3 Conclusion** 

(1) The weight loss ratio of coke increases with time with a linear relation. Compared with single coke charging, with reaction time less than 40min the weight loss ratio of mixed coke is nearly the same; with reaction time over 40min, the weight loss ratio of highly reactive coke is higher than single coke charging, whereas the weight loss ratio of lowly reacctive coke is lower than single charging, which shows that highly reactive coke has protection effect on lowly reactive coke. 

(2) The average weight loss ratio of mixed coke charging is nearly the same as weighted average weight loss ratio of single coke charging. 

(3) The reaction degree of surface and interior of lowly reactive coke is relatively uniform with the reaction time increased. And the reaction degree of surface of highly reactive coke is obviously higher than that of interior.

###### STUDY ON SWELLING BEHAVIOR OF IRON ORE PELLETS IN DIRECT REDUCTION WITH COAL GAS 

###### **Zhucheng Huang , Zhikai Liang , Lingyun Yi , Tao Jiang** 

School of Minerals Processing & Bioengineering, Central South University, Changsha, Hunan 410083, China 

Key words: Iron Ore Pellets, Direct Reduction, Coal Gas, Swelling Behavior, Microstructure. 

###### **Abstract** 

In this study, reduction of iron ore pellets was carried out at 800-950 °C by simulating the atmosphere of typical coal gasification gas. The effects of temperature, gas composition and reduction degree on swelling were investigated respectively. Reduction degree was obtained according to the weight loss records. And volume changes of pellets during reduction were evaluated by infrared photography. Results showed that the pellet swelling increased with temperature and decreased slightly with hydrogen content in the reducing gas. The swelling peaked when reduction degree reached about 40% and then decreased to be stable finally. The microstructures of pellets during reduction were examined by reflected light microscope and relatively rational explanations were proposed for their swelling behaviors. 

###### **Preface** 

Direct reduction iron is an important and indispensable raw material for high-purified and high-quality steel in the electric furnace smelting. Gas-based shaft furnace direct reduction process has very strong competitative ability; however, this technique requires natural gas as reducing agent, so its development has been restricted by gas source and area. Compared with gas-based reduction method, coal based reduction method has the disadvantages of higher production cost and lower productivity. In China, coal resources are abundant and coal gasification technology is mature, and the development of coal gasification shaft furnace direct reduction process is promising. [1] The gasification methods of fixed bed method (Lurgi method), fluidized bed method (Undok method), airflow bed method (Texaco coal water slurry method and Shell dry powder coal method) have been put into use successfully. These syngas generated by different methods can meet the actual production requirement of shaft furnace. However, the compositions of the effective reduction gas in the syngas are quite different. The ratios of hydrogen and carbon monoxide (H2/CO) of Undok or Shell coal gas, Texaco coal gas and Lurgi coal gas are 0.4, 0.6~1.0 and 1.6~2.3, respectively. [2] In the coal gas direct reduction process, the swelling behavior of iron ore pellets is various due

It should be mentioned that a completely different structure was expressed. The structure was mainly composed of iron oxides grains and more macro-pores can be identified. As for the whole pellets, the reduction reaction belongs to the volume reaction model on account of the porous structure and high diffusion coefficient of the reducing gas. At higher temperatures such as 900 and 950 °C, many small particles were reacted and the pore wall's structure was destroyed as a result of rapid reduction 673 reaction of large magnetite particles, which leads to the generation of large holes and significant decrease in compressive strength. ###### **Conclusions** (1) Both the reduction temperature and reducing gas composition have significant effects on swelling change behavior of iron ore pellets. The maximum swelling of pellets increased when the temperature is raised. The swelling decreased with H2 content at the temperature of 800~850°C while the gas of H2/CO=1.6 obtained the maximum swelling value at 9 0 0 ~ 950 °C. (2) The swelling index reached the maximum when the reduction degree got to about 40%. The most rapid swelling behavior mainly appeared in the prophase with reduction degree of 0—15%.
